Albertosaurus.etymology: Named after Alberta, Canada, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Alberta lizard'
Albertosaurus.description: Albertosaurus is a genus of large tyrannosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in northwestern North America during the early to middle Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period, about 71 million years ago. The type species, A. sarcophagus, was apparently restricted in range to the modern-day Canadian province of Alberta, after which the genus is named, although an indeterminate species ("cf. Albertosaurus sp.") has been discovered in the Corral de Enmedio and Packard Formations of Mexico. Scientists disagree on the content of the genus and some recognize Gorgosaurus libratus as a second species.
diagnostic_features: Mandibular ramus devoid of triangular osseous plates between the teeth
Anterior truncate teeth reduced to a single small pair
Fifteen mandibular teeth, including one small anterior tooth truncated posteriorly
Reduced alveolar partitions between the mandibular teeth; principal alveolar grooves on inner surface of outer dentary wall with little or no development of grooves on alveolar plate
Skull with two preorbital openings; lower jaw with a distinct presplenial
Teeth laterally compressed, lenticular in section, upper portion more rounded oval, near bases recurved, serrate on both borders

Albinykus.etymology: Named after 'albin', a term used by Mongolian shamans to describe light phenomena in the Gobi Desert, combined with Greek 'onyx' meaning 'claw'.
Albinykus.description: Albinykus is a genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur whose fossils have been found in the Late Cretaceous-aged (Santonian) Javkhlant Formation in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia. The type species, A. baatar, was named by Sterling J. Nesbitt, Julia A. Clarke, Alan H. Turner and Mark A. Norell in 2011.

Phalanx IV-4 longer than both IV-2 and IV-3
Deep groove on anterior face of the ascending process of the astragalus

Alcovasaurus.etymology: Named after Alcova, Wyoming, where the holotype was discovered
Alcovasaurus.description: Alcovasaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous stegosaurian dinosaurs that lived in the Late Jurassic. It was found in the Morrison Formation of Wyoming, United States. The genus contains a single species, Alcovasaurus longispinus, originally assigned to the genus Stegosaurus. It is likely a member of the Dacentrurinae, and has been referred to the genus Miragaia by some authors.

dispute.summary: Alcovasaurus has an unstable position, recovered outside Eurypoda by Raven and Maidment (2017, attributed to missing data and possible immaturity) and within Dacentrurinae after recoding by Sánchez-Fenollosa and Cobos (2025). It is placed at Stegosauridae without a subfamily pending stable resolution.

Alectrosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'alektros' meaning 'without a mate' or 'unmarried' (hence 'alone') and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'alone lizard'
Alectrosaurus.description: Alectrosaurus is a genus of tyrannosauroid theropod dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period, about some 96 million years ago in what is now the Iren Dabasu Formation.
diagnostic_features: Humerus long and slender, with high thin radial/deltoid crest; length exceeds that of Tyrannosaurus rex.
Manual ungual of digit I exceptionally large, laterally compressed, strongly curved, and sharply pointed.
Femur and tibia subequal in length (distinguishing it from Gorgosaurus sternbergi, which has tibia longer than femur).
Ascending process of astragalus proportionally shorter: one-fourth the combined length of astragalus and tibia (vs. one-third in Gorgosaurus libratus).
Humerus shaft lacks the torque present in Antrodemus (Allosaurus), with both expanded ends lying in the same plane.

species.etymology: Named for George Olsen, the assistant paleontologist who discovered the first specimens of this dinosaur in Mongolia in 1923.

Aletopelta.etymology: From Greek 'aletes' ('wanderer') and 'pelte' ('shield'); meaning 'wandering shield', referring to the northward wandering of the Peninsular Ranges Terrane that carried the specimen from opposite middle Mexico.
Aletopelta.description: Aletopelta is a monospecific genus of basal ankylosaurid dinosaur from Southern California that lived during the Late Cretaceous (upper Campanian stage, 75.5 Ma) in what is now the Point Loma Formation. The type and only species, Aletopelta coombsi, is known from a partial skeleton preserving osteoderms. It was originally described in 1996 by W. P. Coombs, Jr. and T.A. Deméré before being named in 2001 by Tracy Ford and James Kirkland. The holotype formed a miniature reef and was scavenged upon by invertebrates and sharks.

Femur greatly longer than tibia and fibula, yielding a tibia/femur ratio of 0.63 to 0.67.
Three metatarsals in the pes.
Ilia covered by sutured, polygonal, low-peaked scutes arranged in a mosaic pattern.
Massive, short-pointed spike in the shoulder region with a flat (non-beveled) base.
Hollow, dorsoventrally asymmetrical triangular caudal scutes with the dorsal surface significantly more extensive than the ventral surface.

species.name: Aletopelta coombsi
species.etymology: Named for vertebrate paleontologist Walter Preston Coombs, Jr., in recognition of his work and years of research.

Algoasaurus.etymology: Named for Algoa Bay in South Africa, near where its remains were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Algoasaurus.description: Algoasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Berriasian to early Valanginian ages) Upper Kirkwood Formation of Cape Province, South Africa, specifically near a town called Despatch. Only one species, A. bauri, is known.

Scapula lower half shape resembling Brontosaurus, with estimated greatest breadth ~200 mm when complete

Alioramus.etymology: From Latin 'alio' meaning 'different' and 'ramus' meaning 'branch', meaning 'different branch', referring to its divergent position within the tyrannosaurid family tree.
Alioramus.description: Alioramus is a genus of tyrannosaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous period of Asia. It currently contains two species. The type species, A. remotus is known from a partial skull and three foot bones recovered from the Mongolian Nemegt Formation, which was deposited in a humid floodplain. These remains were named and described by Soviet paleontologist Sergei Kurzanov in 1976. A second species, A. altai, known from a much more complete skeleton also from the Nemegt Formation, was named and described by Stephen L. Brusatte and colleagues in 2009. Its relationships to other tyrannosaurid genera were at first unclear, with some evidence supporting a hypothesis that Alioramus was closely related to the contemporary species Tarbosaurus bataar. However, the discovery of Qianzhousaurus indicates that it belongs to a distinct branch of tyrannosaurs, namely the tribe Alioramini.
diagnostic_features: Skull very low and elongated, with a skull length-to-height ratio of about 3.6 (vs. 2.1-2.5 in other tyrannosaurids)
Nasals bearing well-developed separate crests about 1-1.5 cm high
Second antorbital fenestra displaced anteriorly, reaching the level of the anterior end of the 5th tooth
High tooth count: 16 maxillary teeth and 18 dentary teeth
Labial foramina arranged in two rows on the jaws
Teeth narrow and oval in transverse section, slightly compressed at mid-length

species.etymology: From Latin 'remotus' meaning 'removed', reflecting Soviet paleontologist Sergei Kurzanov's belief that this dinosaur was far removed from other members of the tyrannosaurid family.

Allosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'allos' meaning 'different' or 'other' and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'different lizard', alluding to its lightweight vertebrae
Allosaurus.description: Allosaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived 155 to 145 million years ago during the Late Jurassic period (Kimmeridgian to late Tithonian ages). The first fossil remains that could definitively be ascribed to this genus were described in 1877 by Othniel C. Marsh. The name "Allosaurus" means "different lizard", alluding to its lightweight vertebrae, which Marsh believed were unique. The genus has a very complicated taxonomy and includes at least three valid species, the best known of which is A. fragilis. The bulk of Allosaurus remains come from North America's Morrison Formation, with material also known from the Alcobaça, Bombarral, and Lourinhã formations in Portugal. It was known for over half of the 20th century as Antrodemus, but a study of the abundant remains from the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry returned the name "Allosaurus" to prominence. As one of the first well-known theropod dinosaurs, it has long attracted attention outside of paleontological circles.
diagnostic_features: Vertebral centra deeply excavated on the sides to reduce weight, producing an hourglass form in some elements
Vertebrae biconcave with shallow cavities, centra not pneumatic but greatly lightened by lateral excavations
Anterior caudal centrum so strongly constricted that its least transverse diameter (38 mm) is far less than its anterior face diameter (90 mm)
Foot bones very slender

notable_specimens.significance: A 95 percent complete, partially articulated subadult, one of the most famous Allosaurus specimens. Renowned for its 19 broken or infected bones, including a long-lived foot infection that may have contributed to its death; later referred to A. jimmadseni.

A second well-preserved Allosaurus from Howe Ranch. Preserves a 20 by 20 centimeter skin impression at the base of the tail showing large scales up to 2 centimeters across, though the scales resemble sauropod skin and associated non-theropod remains cast some doubt on the attribution.

Found in 1879 but left unpacked until 1903, when it proved to be one of the most complete theropod specimens then known. Put on view in 1908 as the first free-standing mount of a theropod dinosaur, famously posed as if scavenging an Apatosaurus, though never scientifically described.
The largest definitive Allosaurus specimen, estimated at about 9.7 meters long and 2.3 to 2.7 tonnes, used to anchor maximum-size estimates for the genus.

Alocodon.etymology: From Greek 'alotrou' (a furrow) and 'odous' (tooth); meaning 'furrow tooth', alluding to the ribs and furrows ornamenting the lingual surfaces of the cheek crowns.
Alocodon.description: Alocodon is a genus of ornithischian dinosaur known from multiple teeth from the Middle or Late Jurassic Cabaços Formation of Portugal, and also the Forest Marble and Chipping Norton Formations of England. A single species is known, A. kuehnei.

dispute.summary: Alocodon is a nomen dubium based on isolated teeth from the Middle to Late Jurassic of Portugal; its affinities are highly uncertain, having been suggested to be an ornithopod or a thyreophoran but not demonstrable (Jones, 2026). It was formerly placed in the deprecated Fabrosauridae.

history.note: Reparented from the deprecated Fabrosauridae to Ornithischia incertae sedis; tooth-based nomen dubium.

diagnostic_features: Heterodont dentition with fully and uniformly enamelled tooth crowns.
Buccal surfaces of crowns smooth and inflated; lingual surfaces ornamented with fine vertical ribs.
Anterior premaxillary crowns tall, acutely conical, recurved, often with a shoulder-like swelling of the distal margin near the cervix.
Cheek crowns with occlusal tip formed by a single large denticle; lingual surface with short cingula near the distal (and often mesial) margin, sometimes elaborated into small denticles.
Posterior cheek crowns depressed, much longer than high, with large marginal denticles; cingula weak or absent.

Altirhinus.etymology: From Latin 'altus' meaning 'high' and Greek 'rhinos' meaning 'nose', meaning 'high nose', referring to its distinctively arched nasal profile.
Altirhinus.description: Altirhinus is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Albian) Khuren Dukh Formation of Dornogov, Mongolia. The only known species, Altirhinus kurzanovi, is characterized by its distinctive highly arched nasal region.

dispute.summary: Altirhinus kurzanovi is recovered within Hadrosauroidea as an early-diverging member by recent analyses (Godefroit et al., 2012; Poole, 2022). Norman (1998), describing the genus, instead regarded it as a derived iguanodontid alongside Iguanodon and Ouranosaurus — a position outside Hadrosauroidea as currently delimited — and interpreted its hadrosaurid-like cranial features as convergent rather than synapomorphic; that assessment rested on a provisional cladogram, with a full numerical analysis deferred. Norman (2014) later recovered it within a poorly resolved neoiguanodontian plexus.

history.note: Placed at Hadrosauroidea (basal) following the prevailing view; the styracosternan alternative reflected.
Retained at Hadrosauroidea (basal) following Godefroit et al. (2012) and Poole (2022); the iguanodontid assignment of Norman (1998) is recorded as the historical alternative.

diagnostic_features: Rostral tip of nasals strongly arched, giving the snout a distinctively elevated profile.
Lateral flaring of premaxilla to widen the oral cavity not bounded by a raised rim; rostral portion of premaxilla downcurved.
Carpus well ossified but not co-ossified into two discrete blocks as in Camptosaurus, Iguanodon, and Ouranosaurus.
Shaft of ischium straight, parallel-sided and with an axial twist.
Large, finger-shaped lesser trochanter not flattened and appressed to the anterolateral margin of the greater trochanter.
Two replacement crowns in deeper (caudal) portions of both maxillary and dentary dentitions.

Alvarezsaurus.description: Alvarezsaurus is a genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous, living in Argentina approximately 86 - 83 million years ago. It was a small dinosaur, measuring 1-1.4 m (3.3-4.6 ft) long and weighing approximately 3 kg (6.6 lb). It was found in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation and was named by paleontologist José Bonaparte in 1991 after the historian Don Gregorio Alvarez. The type species is A. calvoi.

Alxasaurus.etymology: Named after the Alxa (Alashan) Desert/region of Inner Mongolia combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Alxa lizard'
Alxasaurus.description: Alxasaurus is a genus of therizinosauroid theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous (Albian age) Bayin-Gobi Formation of Inner Mongolia. It is known from five specimens, recovered from the Bayin-Gobi in 1988, as part of the China-Canada Dinosaur Project. During their preparation, paleontologists Dong Zhiming and Dale Russell noted strong similarities to Segnosaurus. In 1993, they described Alxasaurus and named its type species, A. elesitaiensis. While therizinosaurs had previously been tentatively seen as late-surviving basal sauropodomorphs, the description of Alxasaurus lent credence to the idea that they were instead highly derived coelurosaurs.

Amargasaurus.etymology: Named for La Amarga arroyo in Argentina, where it was discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'La Amarga lizard'.
Amargasaurus.description: Amargasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous epoch (129.4-122.46 mya) of what is now Argentina. The only known skeleton was discovered in 1984 and is virtually complete, including a fragmentary skull, making Amargasaurus one of the best-known sauropods of its epoch. Amargasaurus was first described in 1991 and contains a single known species, Amargasaurus cazaui. It was a large animal, but small for a sauropod, reaching 9 to 13 meters (30 to 43 feet) in length. Most distinctively, it sported two parallel rows of tall spines down its neck and back, taller than in any other known sauropod. In life, these spines could have stuck out of the body as solitary structures that supported a keratinous sheath. An alternate hypothesis, now more favored, postulates that they could have formed a scaffold supporting a skin sail. They might have been used for display, combat, or defense.

Amargatitanis.etymology: Named after La Amarga Formation where the fossils were collected, combined with Greek 'titans' meaning 'giant'; meaning 'Amarga giant'
Amargatitanis.description: Amargatitanis is a genus of dicraeosaurid sauropod dinosaur (a type of large, long-necked quadrupedal herbivorous dinosaur) from the Barremian-aged (Lower Cretaceous) La Amarga Formation of Neuquén, Argentina. It is known from a single, incomplete postcranial skeleton consisting of a partial hindlimb, ischium, and two vertebrae. These remains were unearthed by Argentine paleontologist José Bonaparte in 1983 during an expedition by the Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales and later described as a new genus and species, Amargatitanis macni by Sebastián Apesteguía. The genus name comes from the words Amarga, where the fossils were collected, and titanis meaning "titan". Its species name is in reference to the MACN (Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales), where the remains are stored.

dispute.summary: The position of Amphicoelias altus within Diplodocoidea is highly labile. Tschopp et al. (2015) recovered it as Diplodocidae incertae sedis, outside both Apatosaurinae and Diplodocinae. A dedicated redescription (Mannion et al., 2021) found its position unstable across matrices and weighting schemes, recovering it variously as the sister to Diplodocimorpha (a non-diplodocimorph diplodocoid, like Haplocanthosaurus), as a basal diplodocine, or as an apatosaurine; the low scorability of the holotype drives the instability. It is consistently recovered as a valid diplodocoid distinct from Diplodocus.

history.note: Placed at Diplodocoidea, the least inclusive uncontested node, pending resolution of its labile position between a non-diplodocimorph diplodocoid and a basal diplodocid (Tschopp et al., 2015; Mannion et al., 2021).

Marked placement as incertae sedis: Amphicoelias is consistently a diplodocoid but its position within Diplodocoidea is unresolved (Mannion et al., 2021). Amtosaurus.etymology: Named after Amtgai, the Mongolian type locality, plus Greek sauros ('lizard')

Amurosaurus.etymology: Named for the Amur River near where its remains were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'Amur lizard'.
Amurosaurus.description: Amurosaurus is a genus of lambeosaurine hadrosaurid dinosaur found in Late Cretaceous (70 to 66 million years ago) deposits of what is now eastern Asia.
diagnostic_features: Largely dorsally directed, helmet-shaped hollow supracranial crest, slightly longer anteroposteriorly than dorsoventrally tall (height/length ratio ~0.9)
Robust, knob-like ventral end of the jugal anterior process, strongly posteriorly curved
Several anterodorsally-posteroventrally oriented lateral foramina on the maxilla, the last very large and partly obscured by the jugal contact
Narrow infratemporal region of the jugal, about 70% as wide as the orbit
Anterior third of the strongly ventrally bowed parietal sagittal crest low, with a transversely wide, posteriorly tapered dorsal outline
Mesiodistally wide maxillary tooth crowns (about 1.2-1.3 teeth per cm)
Posterolateral process of the sternum slightly shorter than the anteromedial plate, and preacetabular process of the ilium gently ventrally deflected

species.etymology: Named for the late Russian paleontologist Anatoly Riabinin, who conducted the first Russian expeditions to recover dinosaur remains in the Amur region in 1916 and 1917.

dispute.summary: Amygdalodon is a fragmentary early sauropod whose position is labile. Pol and Gomez (2022) recover it near the base of Sauropoda in a polytomy with Gongxianosaurus, outside Eusauropoda, and Jones (2026) likewise places it near the base of Sauropoda without assigning it to Gravisauria; older treatments regarded it as a basal eusauropod or cetiosaurid.

history.note: Moved from Gravisauria to Sauropoda incertae sedis following Pol and Gomez (2022) and Jones (2026); its membership in Gravisauria and Eusauropoda is unresolved.

Amygdalodon.etymology: From Greek 'amygdale' meaning 'almond' and 'odon' meaning 'tooth', meaning 'almond tooth', referring to the almond-shaped teeth.
Amygdalodon.description: Amygdalodon is an extinct genus of basal sauropod from the Early Jurassic of Argentina. The type species is Amygdalodon patagonicus. Fossils of Amygdalodon have been found in the Toarcian-aged Cerro Carnerero Formation (about 180-172 million years ago). Very little is known about it, but it is one of the few Jurassic dinosaurs from South America found thus far.
diagnostic_features: Lateral walls of the neural canal and the centropostzygapophyseal laminae flared laterally toward the posterior
Neural canal strongly flexed anteroposteriorly within the dorsal neural arches

Anabisetia.etymology: Named for the late Ana Maria Biset, an influential archaeologist from Neuquén Province, Argentina, where the remains were found.
Anabisetia.description: Anabisetia is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period of Patagonia, South America. It was a small bipedal herbivore, around 2 meters (6 ft 7 in) long.
diagnostic_features: Cranioventrally oriented occipital condyle
Fifth metacarpal transversely flattened with sharp lateral borders
Scapula with exceptionally strong and well-developed acromial process, stronger than in any other ornithopod
Ilium with preacetabular process longer than 50% of total ilium length; when articulated reaches the same anterior point as the prepubic process
Ischiadic shaft triangular proximally and quadrangular distally in cross section
Tarsus with fibula-astragalar contact

species.etymology: Named for Roberto Saldivia Blanco, a local farmer who discovered the fossils in 1985 and brought them to the attention of science in 1993.

Analong.etymology: Named for the village of A'na in Yunnan, China, where the fossils were discovered.
Analong.description: Analong is an extinct genus of mamenchisaurid sauropod from the Chuanjie Formation in Yunnan, China. The type and only species is Analong chuanjieensis.
diagnostic_features: Caudal transverse processes persisting only until the 10th caudal vertebra (autapomorphy)
Angle between ulnar anterolateral and anteromedial processes approximately 45 degrees (autapomorphy)
Proximal width of metacarpal II is 7% the length of the radius, the lowest value among mamenchisaurids (autapomorphy)
Distal width approximately 40% of the total length of the pubis, the greatest value among mamenchisaurids (autapomorphy)
Weakly developed posterior condylar ball in anterior caudal vertebrae
Ulnar proximal condylar processes sub-equal in length

Anasazisaurus.etymology: Named for the Anasazi (Ancestral Pueblo Native Americans) of the American Southwest, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'Anasazi lizard'.
Anasazisaurus.description: Anasazisaurus is a genus of saurolophine hadrosaurid ("duckbill") ornithopod dinosaur that lived about 74 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous Period. It was found in the Farmington Member of the Kirtland Formation, in the San Juan Basin of New Mexico, United States. Only a partial skull has been found to date. It was first described as a specimen of Kritosaurus by Jack Horner, and has been intertwined with Kritosaurus since its description. It is known for its short nasal crest, which stuck out above and between its eyes for a short distance.

dispute.summary: Prieto-Márquez (2013) synonymized Anasazisaurus into Kritosaurus as K. horneri, treating its distinctive downturned nasal as individual or ontogenetic variation; other workers retain it as a distinct kritosaurin genus. Kept valid within Saurolophinae pending broader consensus.

history.note: Placed at Saurolophinae following the kritosaurin consensus (Prieto-Márquez, 2013; Jones, 2026); genus-level synonymy with Kritosaurus reflected but not adopted.

diagnostic_features: Short, posteriorly folded nasal crest that is above the level of the frontals but does not extend posterior to the anterior end of the frontals

species.name: Anasazisaurus horneri
species.etymology: Named for Jack Horner, the influential paleontologist who first described the skull in 1992.

type_specimen.institution: Earth Sciences Museum, Brigham Young University
type_specimen.material: Partial skull (Farmington Member equivalent).

Anchiceratops.etymology: From Greek 'anchi' meaning 'near' or 'close to' and 'keratops' meaning 'horned face', indicating its close relationship to Triceratops.
Anchiceratops.description: Anchiceratops is an extinct genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur that lived approximately 73 to 68 million years ago during the latter part of the Cretaceous Period in what is now Alberta, Canada.
diagnostic_features: Supraorbital horns massive at base, rising close together and divergent, curving outward then forward
Crest large, thick and flat with small lateral fontanelles; border ornamented by large epioccipital bones
A pair of short knob-like processes on the superior posterior end of the crest
Squamosal intermediate in length between Monoclonius and Triceratops
Fontanelles about half as large as in Monoclonius and wholly within the boundary of the postfrontals
Epijugal attached equally to jugal and quadrato-jugal (differs from Triceratops where it attaches only to jugal)

A complete skull, originally named as the species A. longirostris, now widely regarded as a junior synonym of A. ornatus. Its cast supplies the skull for the NMC 8547 mount.

Anchiornis.etymology: From Greek 'anchi' meaning 'near' and 'ornis' meaning 'bird', meaning 'near bird', reflecting its close morphological similarity to modern birds.
Anchiornis.description: Anchiornis is a genus of small, four-winged paravian dinosaurs, with only one known species, the type species Anchiornis huxleyi, named for its similarity to modern birds. Anchiornis fossils have been found only in the Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning, China, in rocks dated to the Late Jurassic, about 160 million years ago. It is known from hundreds of specimens, and given the exquisite preservation of some of these fossils, it became the first Mesozoic dinosaur species for which almost the entire life appearance could be determined, and an important source of information on the early evolution of birds.
diagnostic_features: Ventral surface of the coracoid sculptured by numerous small pits.
Extremely short ischium, less than one-fourth of femoral length.
Tibiotarsus approximately 150% of femur length, substantially longer proportionally than any other known non-avian theropod.
Manual phalanx II-1 much thicker than all other manual phalanges and nearly as thick as the ulna.
Estimated body mass of approximately 110 grams, making it the smallest known non-avian theropod at time of description.

species.name: Anchiornis huxleyi
species.etymology: Named for Thomas Henry Huxley, an early proponent of biological evolution and one of the first to propose a close evolutionary relationship between birds and dinosaurs.

Anchisaurus.etymology: From Greek 'anchi' meaning 'near' or 'close to' and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', referring to its placement near the base of the sauropodomorph family tree.
Anchisaurus.description: Anchisaurus is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur. It lived during the Early Jurassic Period, and its fossils have been found in the red sandstone of the Upper Portland Formation, Northeastern United States, which was deposited from the Hettangian age into the Sinemurian age, between about 200 and 192 million years ago. Until recently it was classed as a member of Prosauropoda. The genus name Anchisaurus comes from the Greek αγχι (agkhi) anchi-; "near, close" + Greek σαυρος (sauros); "lizard". Anchisaurus was coined as a replacement name for "Amphisaurus", which was itself a replacement name for Hitchcock's "Megadactylus", both of which had already been used for other animals.

iczn_rulings.notes: Opinion 2361 set aside all previous type fixations for Megadactylus polyzelus under the plenary power and designated YPM 1883, the almost complete skull and skeleton that is the holotype of Anchisaurus colurus Marsh, 1891, as the neotype, the original holotype being fragmentary and non-diagnostic. Anchisaurus was placed on the Official List of Generic Names and polyzelus on the Official List of Specific Names.

diagnostic_features: Robust pollex (first digit) of foot with prominent development
Five-toed foot (first, third, and fourth phalanges of fourth toe present)
Large terminal phalanx on first digit, approximately 4 times larger than claw from other digit
Thin and compact bone walls in limb bones with large internal cavities

Andesaurus.etymology: Named for the Andes mountain range, near where the fossils were found in South America, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'Andes lizard'.
Andesaurus.description: Andesaurus is a genus of basal titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur which existed during the middle of the Cretaceous Period in South America. Like most sauropods, it would have had a small head on the end of a long neck and an equally long tail.

Amphiplatyan (platycoelous) caudal vertebrae throughout the available series, with no indication of procoely
Caudal neural spine laminar with axially extensive base; neural arch placed on the centroanterior portion of the centrum
Pubis with markedly wide proximolateral process and pubic foramen located far from the lateral border

Angolatitan.etymology: Named after Angola where the fossils were found, combined with Latin/Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant'; meaning 'Angolan giant'
Angolatitan.description: Angolatitan is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous. It is also the first non-avian dinosaur discovered in Angola. The genus contains a single species, Angolatitan adamastor, known from a partial right forelimb. Angolatitan was a relict form of its time; it was a Late Cretaceous basal titanosauriform, when more derived titanosaurs were far more common.

Posterior facet of the distal epiphysis of metacarpal I with two small splint-like projections

Anhuilong.description: Anhuilong is a genus of mamenchisaurid dinosaur known from the Hongqin Formation of Anhui province, China. The genus contains a single species, Anhuilong diboensis.
diagnostic_features: Lateral edge of deltopectoral crest turns caudolaterally (differs from other mamenchisaurids).
Lateral accessory process of humerus more robust than medial one (reversed from other Mamenchisauridae).
Ratio of total length of radius to humerus is 0.50, the lowest value among mamenchisaurids.
Ratio of total length of ulna to humerus is 0.56, the lowest value among mamenchisaurids.
Elliptical cross-sectional shape of ulna at mid-shaft with highest transverse-to-craniocaudal diameter ratio among mamenchisaurids.
Nearly perpendicular orientation of proximal end of ulna relative to long axis of ulnar shaft.

Aniksosaurus.etymology: From Modern Greek 'anoixi' meaning 'spring' (the season) and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'spring lizard', referring to the onset of spring in the Southern Hemisphere when the fossil was found
Aniksosaurus.description: Aniksosaurus is a genus of avetheropod dinosaur from what is now Chubut Province, Argentina. It lived during the Cenomanian to Turonian of the Cretaceous period, between 96-91 million years ago. The type species, Aniksosaurus darwini, was formally described from the Bajo Barreal Formation of the Golfo San Jorge Basin by Rubén Dario Martínez and Fernando Emilio Novas in 2006; the name was first coined in 1995 and reported in the literature in 1997. The specific epithet honors Charles Darwin who visited Patagonia in 1832/1833 during the Voyage of the Beagle.

Wide, dorsoventrally elliptical neural canal on caudal cervical vertebrae
Cranial caudal vertebrae with a single sagittal ventral keel on the centrum
Manual ungual phalanges robust and transversely thick (height-to-width ratio ~1.1, much lower than other theropods)
Iliac brevis shelf extremely expanded and projected lateroventrally, fan-shaped in ventral view
Metatarsal IV and its corresponding digit transversely very narrow (metatarsal III/IV distal width ratio ~2.14)

Animantarx.etymology: From Latin 'animatus' meaning 'living' or 'animated' and 'arx' meaning 'fortress' or 'citadel', meaning 'living citadel', referring to its heavily armored body.
Animantarx.description: Animantarx is a genus of nodosaurid ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Early and Late Cretaceous of western North America. Like other nodosaurs, it would have been a slow-moving quadrupedal herbivore covered in heavy armor scutes, but without a tail club. The skull measures approximately 25 cm (10 inches) in length, suggesting the animal as a whole was no more than 3 meters (10 feet) long.

Postorbital horns very small
Deltopectoral crest shoulder very high, near level of humeral head, unlike all other nodosaurids
Coracoid elongated, about 63% of scapula length
Oblique ridge on anterolateral surface of femur below lesser trochanter
Armor pattern of skull roof indistinguishable (individual plates not discernible)

Ankylosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'ankylos' (fused, bent) and 'sauros' (lizard), referring to the coossified plates of the skull and the fused vertebral elements.
Ankylosaurus.description: Ankylosaurus is the type genus of Ankylosauridae and the monospecific containing Ankylosaurus magniventris, an iconic North American ankylosaurid known from the latest-Maastrichtian Hell Creek (Montana), Scollard (Alberta), and Lance (Wyoming) Formations. Erected by Barnum Brown in 1908 on a partial skeleton (AMNH 5895) collected by Peter Kaisen near Gilbert Creek, Montana, the genus has since been treated in several descriptive works — Carpenter (2004) and Arbour and Mallon (2017) both redescribing its anatomy, and Arbour and Currie (2015) erecting the tribe Ankylosaurini with Ankylosaurus as its name-bearer. Despite a 100+ year history of armor-arrangement debates and only a handful of partial specimens, Ankylosaurus is among the largest and most-derived ankylosaurids, with a heavily coossified cranial roof, a fully fused tail club, and dental proportions (high tooth count, premaxillary-sinus-driven nare displacement) that distinguish it from coeval Edmontonia. Stratigraphic and sedimentary data indicate a preference for upland facies, in contrast to the coastal lowland setting that yielded most Edmontonia material.
diagnostic_features: Nasal vestibule roofed entirely by the loreal caputegulum (rather than by the supranarial caputegulum as in Anodontosaurus, Euoplocephalus, Scolosaurus, Ziapelta, and Zuul); external nares open ventrolaterally and are not visible in anterior view.
Loreal caputegulum laterally expanded and bulbous, expanding onto the anterior surface of the premaxillary beak and overhanging the lateral surface of the maxilla.
34-36 proportionally small maxillary teeth, crown height less than 2% of basal skull length — a greater tooth count than in Anodontosaurus or Euoplocephalus.
Keel of the anterior and posterior supraorbital caputegulae continuous with the keel of the squamosal horn (discontinuous in Anodontosaurus, Euoplocephalus, and Scolosaurus).

Tail-club handle vertebrae with U-shaped neural spines in dorsal view (V-shaped in most other ankylosaurids); neural arch of the handle vertebrae at least twice as wide as in Anodontosaurus and Euoplocephalus of equivalent length.
Substantially larger body size than all other known Laramidian ankylosaurines, with skull width across the supraorbitals 35-70% greater than the largest known skulls of contemporaneous relatives.

notable_specimens.significance: Found in the Scollard Formation by the Red Deer River, Alberta. Includes a complete skull, the only mandibles and the first and only tail club known for the genus, plus ribs, vertebrae, and limb bones, making it the most informative Ankylosaurus specimen.

Represents the largest known individual of the genus: its skull, at 64.5 cm long, is the largest known for Ankylosaurus and underpins the maximum body-size estimates, though it is damaged in places. Collected near the Red Deer River, Alberta.

Anodontosaurus.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'an' meaning 'without', 'odon' meaning 'tooth', and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'toothless lizard', inspired by compression damage to the specimen that removed the teeth and misled the describer into assuming large trituration plates had replaced the normal dentition.
Anodontosaurus.description: Anodontosaurus is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid dinosaurs within the subfamily Ankylosaurinae. It is known from the entire span of the Late Cretaceous Horseshoe Canyon Formation (mid Late Campanian to "middle" Maastrichtian stage, about 72.8-67 Ma ago) of southern Alberta, Canada, and is also known from the Dinosaur Park Formation (75.6 Ma ago). It contains two species, A. lambei and A. inceptus.
diagnostic_features: Skull very much depressed; completely covered with moderate-sized, irregular dermal ossifications
Teeth entirely absent; broad flat bony plates developed on maxillae and dentaries for masticating food
Mandible greatly reduced and without coronoid process
External nares transversely elongate and terminally placed, facing almost directly forward
Pterygoids small and meeting on midline; palatines not fused on midline and not uniting with pterygoids
Dermal scutes uniformly thin and concave inferiorly, even in long high-keeled forms

Anomalipes.description: Anomalipes is an extinct genus of caenagnathid oviraptorosaurian dinosaurs known from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian age) Wangshi Group of China. The genus contains a single species, Anomalipes zhaoi, known from a partial hindlimb.

Accessory trochanter low and confluent with lesser trochanter.
Lateral ridge present on femoral lateral surface, not known in other oviraptorosaurs.
Weak fourth trochanter present along posteromedial margin of femoral shaft.

Metatarsal III with triangular proximal articular surface, prominent anterior flange near proximal end, medial hemicondyle much narrower than lateral hemicondyle, and longitudinal groove on distal articular surface.
Pedal phalanx II-3 with lateral collateral groove deeper and more dorsally located than medial groove.

Anoplosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'anoplos' meaning 'unarmed' or 'unarmored' and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'unarmed lizard'
Anoplosaurus.description: Anoplosaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous nodosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian age) Cambridge Greensand of Cambridgeshire, England. It has in the past been classified with either the armored dinosaurs or the ornithopods, but current thought has been in agreement with the "armored dinosaur" interpretation, placing it in the Ankylosauria.
diagnostic_features: Dorsal ribs T-shaped: visceral surface compressed and dorsal surface expanded like crosspiece of capital T, suggesting great development of intercostal muscles
Scapula with distinctive massive quadrate spinous process on humeral side, increasing thickness of bone, rounded inferiorly like pulley surface
Sacral region with enlarged neural canal much wider than diameter of dorsal centrum, indicating hind limbs relatively more developed than fore limbs
Body carried in semierect position: dorsal vertebral centrums form upward arch unlike straight horizontal column, suggesting semierect progression
Sacral vertebrae lack anchylosis but in intimate juxtaposition; series includes six centrums with dissimilar forms unlike rounded dorsal forms
Tail shows semierect posture correlation: caudal vertebrae form curve with convex side downward, root elevated well above ground

Anserimimus.description: Anserimimus is a genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaur, from the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now Mongolia. It was a lanky, fast-running animal, possibly an omnivore. From what fossils are known, it probably closely resembled other ornithomimids, except for its more powerful forelimbs.

Antarctopelta.etymology: From 'Antarctica' and Greek 'pelta' meaning 'shield', meaning 'Antarctic shield', reflecting its discovery in Antarctica.
Antarctopelta.description: Antarctopelta is a genus of ankylosaurian dinosaur, a group of large, quadrupedal herbivores, that lived during the late Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous period on what is now James Ross Island, Antarctica. Antarctopelta is the only known ankylosaur from Antarctica and a member of Parankylosauria. The only described specimen was found in 1986, the first dinosaur to be found on the continent, by Argentine geologists Eduardo Olivero and Robert Scasso. The fossils were later described in 2006 by paleontologists Leonardo Salgado and Zulma Gasparini, who named the type species A. oliveroi after Olivero. A 2024 reappraisal by Soto Acuña, Vargas, and Kaluza redescribed the holotype, placed the genus within Parankylosauria, and reinterpreted its caudal osteoderms as a Stegouros-like bony tail weapon.
diagnostic_features: Asymmetrical cheek teeth with at least seven denticles on the mesial border, marked vertical ridges confluent with the denticles on the lingual side, and an ornamented cingulum with fine striations.
Scapular girdle unfused (scapula and coracoid not coossified).
Metatarsal IV with a proximal epiphysis noticeably wider than those of the other metatarsals.
Well-marked striations on the supracetabular shelf of the ilium.
Sacral shield filling the space between both ilia and covering the sacral neural spines, ornamented with several irregular sulci and pits.
Intradermal ossicles approximately 8 mm in diameter.

Antarctosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'antarktikos' meaning 'southern' (opposite of the north/arctic) and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'southern lizard'
Antarctosaurus.description: Antarctosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now South America. The type species, Antarctosaurus wichmannianus, and a second species, Antarctosaurus giganteus, were described by prolific German paleontologist Friedrich von Huene in 1929. Three additional species of Antarctosaurus have been named since then but later studies have considered them dubious or unlikely to pertain to the genus.

Peg-shaped teeth similar to Diplodocus; lower jaw forms right angles at both anterior corners

Quadrate ham-shaped; extraordinarily large orbit positioned far back and high
Posterior cervical vertebrae flat, wide, deeply furrowed on flanks with coarse mesh interior
Scapula slender with very tall deltoid process projecting at right angle
Femur straight and slender with highly vaulted head; fourth trochanter above midpoint
Tibia with both articular terminations very thick; tibial tuberosity prominent but relatively smaller than Titanosaurus

Antetonitrus.etymology: From Latin 'ante' meaning 'before' and 'tonitrus' meaning 'thunder', meaning 'before thunder', referring to its existence before Brontosaurus (the 'thunder lizard').
Antetonitrus.description: Antetonitrus is a genus of sauropodiform dinosaur found in the Early Jurassic Elliot Formation of South Africa. The only species is Antetonitrus ingenipes. Sometimes considered a basal sauropod, it is crucial for the understanding of the origin and early evolution of this group. It was a quadrupedal herbivore, like its later relatives, but shows primitive adaptations to use the forelimbs for grasping, instead of purely for weight support.

Extremely short, broad metacarpal I (maximum length only 85% of proximal width).

The type species, Anzu wyliei, is known from numerous skeletons that preserve cranial and postcranial elements.

dispute.summary: Aorun zhaoi is based on a juvenile skeleton, and its affinities are highly unstable. It was originally described as a basal coelurosaur (Choiniere et al., 2013) and recovered as an early-diverging alvarezsaurian by Xu et al. (2018), Qin et al. (2019), and — with weak support — Meso et al. (2024). Broad theropod analyses reject this: Hartman et al. (2019) recovered it as a compsognathid, and Cau (2024) recovered it as an early-diverging allosauroid, interpreting its coelurosaurian signal as an artifact of the holotype's juvenile ontogeny. Jones (2026) treats it as a basal coelurosaur.

history.note: Placed conservatively at Avetheropoda, the least-inclusive clade shared by all hypotheses; alvarezsaurian, compsognathid, and allosauroid placements are all in play.
Confirmed placement at Avetheropoda incertae sedis; the within-Coelurosauria-versus-allosauroid position remains unresolved and is confounded by the juvenile holotype.

Apatosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'apate' meaning 'deception' and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'deceptive lizard'
Apatosaurus.description: Apatosaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Jurassic period. Othniel Charles Marsh described and named the first-known species, Apatosaurus ajax, in 1877, and a second species, Apatosaurus louisae, was discovered and named by William H. Holland in 1916. Apatosaurus lived about 152 to 151 million years ago (mya), during the late Kimmeridgian to early Tithonian age, and are now known from fossils in the Morrison Formation of modern-day Colorado, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Wyoming, and Utah in the United States. Apatosaurus had an average length of 21-23 m (69-75 ft), and an average mass of 16.4-22.4 t (16.1-22.0 long tons; 18.1-24.7 short tons). A few specimens indicate a maximum length of 11-30% greater than average and a mass of approximately 33 t (32 long tons; 36 short tons).

Appalachiosaurus.etymology: Named for the Appalachian region of eastern North America where it was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'Appalachian lizard'.
Appalachiosaurus.description: Appalachiosaurus is a genus of tyrannosauroid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period of what is now eastern North America. It was a basal member of the clade Eutyrannosauria, meaning it was rather close in relation to the true tyrannosaurids such as Tyrannosaurus. Like most theropods, it was a bipedal predator. Only a juvenile skeleton has been found, representing an animal approximately 6.5 meters (21 ft) long and weighing 623 kilograms (1,373 lb), which indicates an adult would have been significantly larger.

Aquilarhinus.etymology: From Latin 'aquila' meaning 'eagle' and Greek 'rhinos' meaning 'snout' or 'nose'; meaning 'eagle snout', after the unusual beak morphology
Aquilarhinus.description: Aquilarhinus is a genus of hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur from the Aguja Formation from Texas in the United States. The type and only species is Aquilarhinus palimentus. Due to its unusual dentary, it has been inferred to have had shovel-like beak morphology, different from the beaks of other hadrosaurs. It was originally classified as a Kritosaurus sp. before being reclassified as a new genus in 2019.

Aralosaurus.etymology: Named after the Aral Sea (near where the fossils were found northeast of it) combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Aral Sea lizard'
Aralosaurus.description: Aralosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Kazakhstan. It is known only by a posterior half of a skull (devoid of its mandible) and some post-cranial bones found in the Bostobe Formation in rocks dated from the Upper Santonian - lower Campanian boundary, at about 83.6 Ma (millions of years ago). Only one species is known, Aralosaurus tuberiferus, described by Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky in 1968. The genus name means "Aral Sea lizard", because it was found to the northeast of the Aral Sea. The specific epithet tuberiferus means "bearing a tuber" because the posterior part of the nasal bone rises sharply in front of the orbits like an outgrowth.

Proximal end of metatarsal III is wide, comprising approximately half its entire length.

Archaeoceratops.etymology: From Greek 'archaios' meaning 'ancient', 'keras' meaning 'horn', and 'ops' meaning 'face', translating to 'ancient horned face'.
Archaeoceratops.description: Archaeoceratops, meaning "ancient horned face", is a genus of basal neoceratopsian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian stage) of north central China. It appears to have been bipedal and quite small, reaching 0.9 m (3.0 ft) in length and 10 kg (22 lb) in body mass. It had a comparatively large head but no horns, possessing only a small bony frill projecting from the back of its head.
diagnostic_features: Modest bumpy ornamentation covering much of the lateral surface of the jugal, resembling that seen on the jugals of pachycephalosaurs.

Archaeopteryx.etymology: From Greek 'archaios' meaning 'ancient' and 'pteryx' meaning 'feather' or 'wing', meaning 'ancient wing'.
Archaeopteryx.description: Archaeopteryx , sometimes referred to by its German name, "Urvogel " (lit. 'Primeval Bird') is a genus of bird-like dinosaurs. The genus name derives from the Ancient Greek ἀρχαῖος (archaîos), meaning 'ancient', and πτέρυξ (ptérux), meaning 'feather, wing'. Between the late 19th century and the early 21st century, Archaeopteryx was generally accepted by paleontologists and popular reference books as the oldest known bird (member of the group Avialae). Older potential avialans have since been identified, including Anchiornis, Xiaotingia, Aurornis, and Baminornis.

Ardetosaurus.description: Ardetosaurus is an extinct genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) Morrison Formation of northern Wyoming, United States. The genus contains a single species, Ardetosaurus viator. It was first described in 2024 on the basis of a partial articulated skeleton, including vertebrae from the neck, back, and tail, hip bones, and part of the left hindlimb. The genus is a member of the Diplodocinae, a subfamily of large long-necked dinosaurs with whiplike tails. Ardetosaurus represents one of many distinct sauropod taxa that coexisted in this formation.

Arenysaurus.etymology: Named for Arén, the town in the Pyrenees of Spain near where it was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Arenysaurus.description: Arenysaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (66 million years ago), being one of the last non-avian dinosaurs and it went extinct during the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event. It is known from a partial skull and skeleton found in the late Maastrichtian-age Tremp Formation of the Pyrenees Mountains in Spain. The type species is A. ardevoli, described in 2009 by Pereda-Suberbiola et al., a group of researchers from Spain. The genus name refers to Arén, where it was found, and the specific epithet honors geologist Lluís Ardèvol. Arenysaurus was a lambeosaurine, a member of the hadrosaurid subfamily with hollow and decorative cranial crests. It is one of the most complete and best dated ever found in the Late Cretaceous period.

It was a member of Titanosauria, the dominant group of sauropods during the Cretaceous.

Aristosuchus.etymology: From Ancient Greek aristos (ἄριστος) meaning 'bravest, best, noblest' + Soukhos (σοῦχος), the Ancient Greek form of the name of the Egyptian crocodile-headed god Sobek; overall meaning 'best/noblest Sobek'.
Aristosuchus.description: Aristosuchus is a genus of small coelurosaurian dinosaur that lived in the Early Cretaceous period (Barremian stage, sometime between 130 and 123 million years ago) of what is now England, UK. The type and only species is Aristosuchus pusillus, originally referred to the carnosaurian genus Poekilopleuron.
diagnostic_features: Sacrum of five vertebrae in which each centrum supports its own neural arch (neural foramen not shifted to overlap adjacent centrum, unlike Megalosaurus)
Sacral transverse processes arise from individual vertebrae, not at the junction between centra
Sacral centra strongly constricted from side to side, with transverse midpoint measurement only 7-8 mm despite 2.2 cm wide articular faces
Pubes rod-like and anteriorly directed, converging distally and uniting with a horizontal posterior keel - a Coelurus/Allosaurus-type pubis not previously recorded from Britain
Metapophyses (accessory lateral neural spines) developed on third and fourth sacral vertebrae, indicated as ridges on second and fifth

species.etymology: From Latin for 'very small', referring to the diminutive size of the animal.

Arkansaurus.etymology: From Arkansas (the U.S. state where fossils were found) + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'Arkansas lizard'.
Arkansaurus.description: Arkansaurus is an extinct genus of ornithomimosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived during the Aptian and Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous in what is now North America. The type and only species is Arkansaurus fridayi.
diagnostic_features: Third metatarsal laterally compressed proximally but visible along its entire extensor surface (subarctometatarsalian condition)
Proximal articular facets of the metatarsals ovoid in shape when articulated
Pedal unguals more strongly ventrally curved distally than any other ornithomimosaur
Distal ungual with a very weak flexor tubercle, curved rather than flat, lacking mediolateral spurs

species.etymology: Named for Joe B. Friday, who discovered the fossilized foot on his land in Arkansas in 1972.

Arkharavia.etymology: From the village of Arkhara (Amur Region, Far East Russia) and the Latin via (road); referring to the locality near the Arkhara River.
Arkharavia.description: Arkharavia is a dubious genus of somphospondylan sauropod, although at least some of its remains probably belong to a hadrosaurid. It was discovered in the Udurchukan Formation in Russia and lived during the Late Cretaceous. It was described in 2010 by Alifanov and Bolotsky as the type species A. heterocoelica.
diagnostic_features: Anterior caudal centra narrow in lateral view, with saddle-shaped (heterocoelous) articular surfaces.
Neural spine of anterior caudal vertebrae high and narrow, with a distinct groove at the base of its cranial surface.

species.name: Arkharavia heterocoelica
species.etymology: From Greek heteros (different) and koilos (hollow); "differently hollowed", referring to the heterocoelous (saddle- shaped) articular surfaces of the anterior caudal centra.

Arrhinoceratops.etymology: From Ancient Greek a-/alpha privative (ἀ-) meaning 'no/without' + rhis (ῥίς) meaning 'nose' + keras (κέρας) meaning 'horn' + ops (ὤψ) meaning 'face'; overall meaning 'no nose-horn face'.
Arrhinoceratops.description: Arrhinoceratops is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur. The name was coined as its original describer concluded it was special because the nose-horn was not a separate bone, however further analysis revealed this was based on a misunderstanding. It lived during the latest Campanian/earliest Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, predating its famous relative Triceratops by a few million years, although it was contemporary with Anchiceratops. Its remains have been found in Canada.
diagnostic_features: Nasal horn core absent; nasal bone forms only a sharp longitudinal ridge with fine rugosities, without horn core or epinasal
Supraorbital horn cores large, approximately circular in cross section, directed upward, outward, and forward
Facial region unusually short relative to crest length (ratio ~0.52)
Crest strikingly subquadrate in outline and very flat posteriorly, with no epoccipitals on margin
Anterior process of jugal unusually long, overlapping the maxillary extensively and making suture with nasal unusually short
Lower temporal arcade remarkably bar-like, producing a low isosceles-triangular lateral temporal fossa

species.name: Arrhinoceratops brachyops
species.etymology: Means 'short-faced', derived from the Greek brachys, meaning 'short'.

Arrudatitan.etymology: Named after Arruda (a person's name honored in the genus), combined with Greek Titan meaning 'giant'; overall meaning 'Arruda's giant'.
Arrudatitan.description: Arrudatitan is an extinct genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian-Maastrichtian)-aged Adamantina Formation of Brazil. The type species, A. maximus, was named and described in 2011 as a species of Aeolosaurus, but was separated into its own genus in 2021. It was relatively gracile for a titanosaur.
diagnostic_features: Posterior cervical vertebrae with posterior centrodiapophyseal lamina (pcdl) at least 50% thicker than the postzygodiapophyseal lamina (podl).
Posterior trunk vertebrae with oblique anterior centropostzygapophyseal lamina (acpol) that bifurcates from the proximal portion of the centropostzygapophyseal lamina (cpol).
Accessory intrapostzygapophyseal lamina on posterior trunk vertebrae, creating two small lateral camerae on the spinopostzygapophyseal fossa.
Mid-trunk ribs with well-developed anterior and posterior crests producing a D-shaped cross section.

species.name: Arrudatitan maximus
species.etymology: From Latin 'maximus' meaning 'greatest' or 'largest', in reference to the large size of the taxon; originally published as 'Aeolosaurus maximus' before the genus was renamed Arrudatitan to honor the late Professor Antonio Celso de Arruda Campos, one of the original describers.

Arstanosaurus.etymology: From "Arstan" (the name of an old well at the type locality, in the northeastern Aralkum, Kazakhstan) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Arstan lizard'.
Arstanosaurus.description: Arstanosaurus is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous-aged (Santonian-Campanian) Bostobe Formation of Kazakhstan. It has had a confusing history, being considered a hadrosaurid, a ceratopsid, or both at the same time (chimeric).

dispute.summary: Arstanosaurus is a nomen dubium based on a fragmentary maxilla, with concerns that the referred material is chimeric (mixing hadrosaurid and ceratopsian remains).

history.note: Placed at Hadrosauridae incertae sedis; nomen dubium.

diagnostic_features: Maxilla massive and low, with a practically straight dorsal edge.
Supershelf process horizontally elongated and overhanging above the shelf surface, dorso-ventrally flattened and rounded.
Outer replacement tooth placed directly above the functional tooth rather than lingual and slightly higher, with the crown lying within the branching of the root of the functional tooth.

species.name: Arstanosaurus akkurganensis
species.etymology: From the Akkurgan locality near Qyzylorda, Kazakhstan, where the holotype was collected.

dispute.summary: The phylogenetic position of Asfaltovenator vialidadi is unstable. Its describers recovered it as a basal allosauroid and noted that its mosaic of megalosauroid and allosauroid characters destabilizes tetanuran topology (Rauhut and Pol, 2019); Jones and Viola (2026) likewise treat it as a basal allosauroid outside both Allosauria and Metriacanthosauridae. Other analyses instead place it within Allosauridae as the sister taxon of Allosaurus (Rauhut et al., 2024; Kellermann et al., 2025). It is placed conservatively at Allosauroidea incertae sedis.

history.note: Placed at Allosauroidea incertae sedis; recovered as a basal allosauroid by Rauhut and Pol (2019) but within Allosauridae by later analyses.

Asfaltovenator.etymology: From the Cañadón Asfalto Formation (the fossil formation where remains were found, named for asphalt deposits) + Latin venator meaning 'hunter'; overall meaning 'Cañadón Asfalto Formation hunter'.
Asfaltovenator.description: Asfaltovenator is a genus of possibly allosauroid dinosaur from the Early to Middle Jurassic Cañadón Asfalto Formation of Chubut Province, Argentina. The type and only species is Asfaltovenator vialidadi.

Exoccipital with pronounced horizontal ridges between paroccipital processes and foramen magnum
Neural spines of cervical vertebrae three and four triangular and backswept
Dorsals 11 and 12 with small additional anterior centrodiapophyseal lamina
Articulated metacarpus broader than long
Manual digit III significantly more slender and shorter than digits I and II

Asiaceratops.description: Asiaceratops is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur. It lived during the Early-Late Cretaceous. The type species, A. salsopaludalis is known from Uzbekistan, while A. sulcidens is known from China and Mongolia.

It is retained provisionally at Dromaeosauridae incertae sedis.

history.note: Retained at Dromaeosauridae incertae sedis; nomen dubium, teeth of uncertain affinity (possibly Richardoestesia or non-theropod).

Asiamericana.etymology: From the ancient continent "Asiamerica", reflecting Nessov's interpretation of the genus as evidence of Late Cretaceous faunal links between Asia and North America.
Asiamericana.description: Asiamericana is a dubious genus of coelurosaur known only from isolated teeth found in the Bissekty Formation of Uzbekistan. It was named to recognize the occurrence of similar fossil teeth in Central Asia and North America. These regions once formed a connected land mass, during the Cretaceous period.
diagnostic_features: Teeth straight and strongly laterally flattened, with a plane of symmetry perpendicular to the plane through the crown apex and cutting edges.
Tooth edges entirely lack serrations.
Crown bearing a weakly sloping vertical groove that may be replaced by a flat surface occupying one-third to one-half of the anteroposterior width.

Asiatosaurus.etymology: From Greek Asia and sauros (lizard); meaning "Asian lizard", with the genus name explicitly derived in the original description.
Asiatosaurus.description: Asiatosaurus is a dubious sauropod tooth-taxon erected by Osborn (1924) on isolated camarasaur-like teeth from the Öösh Formation of Mongolia. The type species A. mongoliensis is based on a single posterior dentary tooth (AMNH 6264) from the Oshih basin; Osborn himself noted that the holotype and paratype might not belong to the same individual or even the same species. A second nominal species (A. kwangshiensis) was named on a tooth from China and is also generally treated as a nomen dubium. Asiatosaurus has been variably placed in Camarasauridae, Brachiosauridae, and Euhelopodidae over the decades, but the fragmentary nature of the type material precludes confident placement.
diagnostic_features: Subspatulate dentary tooth crown with an asymmetric apex; the internal (lingual) surface is spoon-shaped near the crown tip, bearing a small median vertical groove.
Tooth crown more robust anteroposteriorly than in classic Morrison-Formation camarasaurs, with two lateral grooves on the external surface flanking the apex.

species.name: Asiatosaurus mongoliensis
species.etymology: From mongoliensis ("of Mongolia"), referring to the country of origin of the holotype.

type_specimen.material: Single posterior dentary tooth with a subspatulate crown bearing two lateral external grooves and one median internal groove.

species.authors: Osborn, H. F.

references.title: Sauropoda and Theropoda of the Lower Cretaceous of Mongolia

Asiatyrannus.etymology: From Asia (the continent where fossils were found) + Greek tyrannos (τύραννος) meaning 'tyrant'; overall meaning 'Asian tyrant'.
Asiatyrannus.description: Asiatyrannus is an extinct genus of tyrannosaurine theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, A. xui, known from a single specimen consisting of a skull and partial postcranial skeleton. Asiatyrannus is notable for its deep-snouted skull and small body size, in contrast to the gracile snout and larger size of the contemporary Qianzhousaurus. It represents the southernmost record of an Asian tyrannosaurid.

Large and sub-rectangular shaped maxillary fenestra
Posterior protuberances of the nasals connect to form two separated medium low ridges
Low ridge-like jugal accessory horn with the ventral margin of the anterior ramus curving ventrally anterior to the horn
Lateral surface of the descending process of the postorbital with anterodorsally trending fine lineations
Lateral surangular shelf extending to the posterior end of the surangular

Astigmasaura.etymology: From compound Latin 'astigma' meaning 'without signs' and Ancient Greek 'saura' (feminine of sauros) meaning 'lizard'; references the type locality El Orejano, whose name refers to unmarked animals.
Astigmasaura.description: Astigmasaura is an extinct genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Huincul Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Astigmasaura genuflexa, known from an incomplete articulated skeleton.

Anterior caudal vertebrae with tall transverse processes (exceeding centrum height) positioned anterior to the neural spine in lateral view
Asymmetric middle haemal arches with a straight anterior articular surface longer than the posterior one
Pubis with an anterodorsally extended iliac peduncle, a wide elliptical obturator foramen (obturator-to-acetabular area ratio greater than 0.40), and a laminar, distally extended symphysis
Femur with a prominent trochanteric shelf beneath the greater trochanter on the posterior surface of the proximal epiphysis, forming a posterior bulge in proximal view

Pes with posteriorly expanded proximal halves of metatarsals II-IV, distolateral and medioproximal processes on proximal phalanges II-IV, and ungual phalanges bearing a longitudinal crest and fossa on the dorsal margin of the lateral surface

Astrodon.etymology: From Greek 'astron' meaning 'star' and 'odon' meaning 'tooth', referring to the star-like cross-sectional pattern seen in its tooth enamel.
Astrodon.description: Astrodon is a genus of large herbivorous sauropod dinosaur, measuring 20 m (66 ft) in length, 9 m (30 ft) in height and 20 metric tons (22 short tons) in body mass. It lived in what is now the eastern United States during the Early Cretaceous period, and fossils have been found in the Arundel Formation, which has been dated through palynomorphs to the Albian about 112 to 110 million years ago.

Summit compressed conical, curved inward, convex externally, depressed internally, sub-acute at lateral borders
Dentine interior with multitude of minute tubuli radiating from narrow elliptical pulp cavity
Thick enamel layer surrounding pulp cavity and dentine in transverse section

Asylosaurus.etymology: From Ancient Greek asylos (ἄσυλος) meaning 'unharmed, inviolable, having right of asylum' + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'unharmed lizard', referring to the specimens surviving World War II bombardment unlike the Thecodontosaurus holotype.
Asylosaurus.description: Asylosaurus is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Late Triassic Avon Fissure Fill of England. It is based on partial remains, discovered in the autumn of 1834, described in 1836 by Henry Riley and Samuel Stutchbury as pertaining to Thecodontosaurus, that Othniel Charles Marsh brought to Yale University between 1888 and 1890. These remains thus escaped destruction by a bombardment in 1940 during World War II, unlike the original holotype of Thecodontosaurus. Asylosaurus was described in 2007 by Peter Galton. The type species is A. yalensis, referring to Yale. The bones originally came from a Rhaetian-age cave fill at Durdham Down, Clifton, Bristol.

dispute.summary: Asylosaurus yalensis is a basal sauropodomorph from the Late Triassic of England, closely comparable to Thecodontosaurus; Jones (2026) regards it as a probable nomen dubium whose material cannot be confidently distinguished from Thecodontosaurus.

history.note: Placed at Sauropodomorpha incertae sedis; possible nomen dubium close to Thecodontosaurus.

Athenar.etymology: Named for Cleveland metal artist Athenar, whose music was described as 'the soundtrack to the majority of the work done on this specimen'. The species name honors David Berman, who carried out foundational modern work on diplodocoid skulls.
Athenar.description: Athenar is an extinct genus of dicraeosaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of Utah, United States. The genus contains a single species, Athenar bermani, which was described by John Whitlock and colleagues in 2025 based on the holotype specimen CM 26552: a braincase and skull roof previously ascribed to the genus Diplodocus. The specimen was found in rocks belonging to the Morrison Formation at the Carnegie Quarry at Dinosaur National Monument.

Single foramen for passage of the abducens (VI) nerve (distinct from Suuwassea emilieae)

Presence of frontoparietal and postparietal fenestrae (absent in Kaatedocus and Smitanosaurus)
Frontal contributes to the full anterior margin of the supratemporal fenestra (absent in Smitanosaurus and all other Morrison Formation sauropods except Suuwassea)

dispute.summary: The affinities of Atlasaurus are contested and unresolved. The dedicated titanosauriform analyses of D'Emic (2012) and Mannion et al. (2013) recover it as a non-neosauropod eusauropod, outside Macronaria, whereas Moore et al. (2020) recover it variably as a non-neosauropod eusauropod (equal weighting), a brachiosaurid (implied weighting), or a basal macronarian (Bayesian). Its describers (Monbaron et al., 1999) originally interpreted it as a brachiosaurid; Jones (2026) treats its affinities as ambiguous.

history.note: Moved from Macronaria to Eusauropoda following the dedicated titanosauriform analyses that place it outside Neosauropoda; finer placement remains unresolved.

Placement unchanged; dispute citations corrected — Royo-Torres et al. (2020) does not include Atlasaurus, and the D'Emic (2012) result is a non-neosauropod eusauropod, not a basal macronarian.

Atlasaurus.etymology: Named for the Atlas Mountains of North Africa, where its fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Atlasaurus.description: Atlasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaurs from Middle Jurassic (Bathonian to Callovian stages) beds in North Africa.

Atlascopcosaurus.etymology: Named for Atlas Copco, the company whose equipment sponsored the Dinosaur Cove excavation in Australia, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.

Atrociraptor.etymology: From Latin 'atrox' meaning 'savage' or 'cruel' and 'raptor' meaning 'robber' or 'thief', meaning 'savage robber'.
Atrociraptor.description: Atrociraptor is a genus of dromaeosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Alberta, Canada. The first specimen, a partial skull, was discovered in 1995 by the fossil collector Wayne Marshall in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation, about 5 km (3 mi) from the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology where it was brought for preparation. In 2004, the specimen became the holotype of the new genus and species Atrociraptor marshalli; the generic name is Latin for "savage robber", and the specific name refers to Marshall. The holotype consists of the premaxillae (frontmost bones of the upper jaw), a maxilla (main bone of the upper jaw), the dentaries (tooth-bearing bones of the lower jaw), associated teeth, and other skull fragments. Isolated teeth from the same formation have since been assigned to Atrociraptor.
diagnostic_features: Shorter, deeper face than Saurornitholestes and Velociraptor; subnarial body of premaxilla taller than its anteroposterior length
Internarial and maxillary processes of premaxilla subparallel and oriented more dorsally than posteriorly
Maxillary fenestra larger than in any other velociraptorines and positioned directly above the promaxillary fenestra rather than well behind it
Maxillary teeth more strongly inclined toward the throat (posteroventrally) than in all other dromaeosaurids except Bambiraptor and Deinonychus
Maxillary dentition essentially isodont with no replacement gaps and minimal height variation between adjacent teeth

Atsinganosaurus.etymology: From the Greek word 'τσιγγάνος' or 'αθίγγανος' meaning 'gypsy', referring to the possible migration from east to west of the species, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'. The species name honors its discovery locality Velaux-La Bastide Neuve.
Atsinganosaurus.description: Atsinganosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur which existed in what is now France during the Late Cretaceous. Well-preserved remains (and the only known) of Atsinganosaurus were collected from the Grès à Reptiles Formation of the Aix-en-Provence Basin. The type and only species is A. velauciensis.

Distal end of humerus very slightly transversely expanded; dorsal edge of scapular blade perpendicular to proximal expansion of scapula

Aucasaurus.etymology: Named after Auca Mahuevo, the fossil site in Argentina where it was found; 'saur' from Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'Auca Mahuevo lizard'.
Aucasaurus.description: Aucasaurus is a genus of medium-sized abelisaurid theropod dinosaur from Argentina that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Santonian to Campanian stage) of the Anacleto Formation. It was smaller than the related Carnotaurus, although more derived in some ways, such as its extremely reduced arms and almost total lack of fingers.

Augustynolophus.etymology: Named after the Augustyn family (donors to the Los Angeles County Museum) combined with Greek lophos meaning 'crest', a reference to its relative Saurolophus.
Augustynolophus.description: Augustynolophus is an extinct genus of herbivorous saurolophine hadrosaur dinosaur which was discovered in the Moreno Formation in California, dating to the late Maastrichtian age, making it one of the last non-avian dinosaurs known from the fossil record before the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event.

Auroraceratops.etymology: From Latin aurora meaning 'dawn' and Greek keras/ceratops meaning 'horned face'. Full meaning: 'dawn horned face', referring to its status as an early ceratopsian and also honoring Dawn Dodson.

The etymology of the generic name refers to its status as an early ceratopsian and also to Dawn Dodson, wife of Peter Dodson, one of the paleontologists who described it.

Australodocus.description: Australodocus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic period, around 150 million years ago, in what is now Lindi Region, Tanzania. Though initially considered a diplodocid, recent analyses suggest it may instead be a titanosauriform.

Australotitan.etymology: From Latin 'australis' meaning 'southern' and Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant', referring to the large size of this dinosaur from southern Australia.
Australotitan.description: Australotitan is an extinct genus of possibly titanosaurian somphospondylan dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Winton Formation (Cenomanian-Turonian) of southern-central Queensland, Australia. The genus contains a single species, A. cooperensis, known from multiple partial skeletons. The genus Australotitan may be synonymous with Diamantinasaurus, a contemporary relative.

Ulna with a distinct radial interosseous ridge within the distal half of the radial fossa, and anterolateral process bearing a distal accessory projection proximal to a proximally beveled distal epiphysis.
Humerus with a rounded ridge extending from the distal end of the deltopectoral crest to just proximal of a tri-lobate distal epiphysis.
Distal ischial blades curve ventrally to produce a dorsal face that is posteriorly directed.
Femur with a medially sloped proximolateral margin, anteroposteriorly narrow diaphysis, and distal condyles directed anterolaterally to posteromedially.

Australovenator.etymology: From Latin australis meaning 'southern' + Latin venator meaning 'hunter'; overall meaning 'southern hunter', referring to its discovery in Australia.
Australovenator.description: Australovenator is a genus of megaraptoran theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Winton Formation (Cenomanian, 95 million years ago) of Australia. Some specimens from the Albian-aged Eumeralla Formation and the Wonthaggi Formation may belong to Australovenator. It is known from partial cranial and postcranial remains, which were described in 2009 by Scott Hocknull and colleagues, although additional descriptions and analyses continue to be published. It is the most complete predatory dinosaur discovered in Australia. It has been suggested that Australovenator is a sister taxon to Fukuiraptor, although some phylogenetic analyses find it to be a more derived member of the Megaraptora, possibly being part of the main Megaraptoridae family itself.

Austrocheirus.etymology: From Latin austro- meaning 'southern' + Greek cheir (χείρ) meaning 'hand'; overall meaning 'southern hand', referring to its discovery in southern Argentina and the partial hand fossils known.
Austrocheirus.description: Austrocheirus is an extinct genus of theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period. It was named and described by Martin Ezcurra, Federico Agnolín and Fernando Novas in 2010. It contains the type species Austrocheirus isasii. The generic name means "southern hand". The specific epithet honors discoverer and preparator Marcelo Pablo Isasi.

Metacarpal III with posteriorly displaced collateral tendon fossae located at the same level of the proximal end of distal condyles.
Pedal phalanges with a conspicuous longitudinal crest delimiting the dorsal margin of the distal collateral tendon fossae.
Tibia with a slightly convex posterior surface at the distal end.
Metatarsal III with a very well-developed ventral scar for the insertion of the M. gastrocnemius.

Austroposeidon.etymology: From Latin austro- meaning 'southern' + Poseidon (Ποσειδῶν), the Greek god of the sea, used here as a reference to enormous size (as in Sauroposeidon); overall meaning 'Southern Poseidon'.
Austroposeidon.description: Austroposeidon is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Presidente Prudente Formation of Brazil. It contains one species, Austroposeidon magnificus (meaning "Magnificent Southern Poseidon").

dispute.summary: Placed conservatively within Colossosauria. The describing analysis (Bandeira et al., 2016) recovered Austroposeidon as the sister group of Lognkosauria rather than within it, whereas a later analysis (Navarro et al., 2022) recovered it inside Lognkosauria; most other studies leave it unresolved owing to its fragmentary remains. Colossosauria is the least-inclusive node these placements share.

history.note: Reparented from Lognkosauria to Colossosauria; the describing analysis places it just outside Lognkosauria and only Navarro et al. (2022) recovers it within, so it is placed at the shared uncontested node.

Austroraptor.etymology: From Latin auster meaning 'south' and Latin raptor meaning 'thief/plunderer'. Full meaning: 'southern thief/plunderer', referring to its South American (southern) origin.
Austroraptor.description: Austroraptor is a genus of unenlagiine theropod dinosaur that lived during the Campanian and Maastrichtian ages of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Argentina.

Maxillary and dentary teeth small, conical-shaped, unserrated and fluted (enamel surface fluted as in spinosaurids)

Avaceratops.description: Avaceratops is a genus of small herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaurs which lived during the late Campanian in what are now the Northwest United States. Most fossils come from the Judith River Formation.
diagnostic_features: Short-squamosaled ceratopsid with distinctive robust squamosal bearing a long rostral portion that equals or exceeds the length of the caudal portion

Parietal fan-shaped and thin, with no sagittal emargination along the caudal margin; parietal fenestrae apparently absent (solid frill inferred)
Jugal thin, unsculptured, and lacking a central ridge
Maxilla robust with a strong medial longitudinal ridge
Occipital condyle fully fused (no sutural trace) at a small diameter of 38 mm, suggesting an unusual growth pattern
