Erliansaurus.etymology: From Erlian (the town of Erlian/Erenhot in Inner Mongolia, China, near the discovery site) + Greek sauros (lizard): 'Erlian lizard'.
Erliansaurus.description: Erliansaurus is a genus of therizinosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Nei Mongol, Iren Dabasu Formation.

dispute.summary: Erliansaurus is an intermediate-grade therizinosaur whose family-level assignment depends on how Therizinosauridae is defined. Under the narrow node-based definition of Zanno (2010) it lies outside Therizinosauridae as an intermediate therizinosauroid, a result followed by Hartman et al. (2019) and the Princeton Encyclopedia (Jones, 2026). Under the broader Therizinosaurus-anchored definition of Kobayashi et al. (2022, 2025) it is drawn into Therizinosauridae, recovered with Neimongosaurus as the family's most basal clade. It is placed conservatively in Therizinosauroidea.

history.note: Placed at Therizinosauroidea (outside Therizinosauridae) following Zanno (2010), Hartman et al. (2019) and Jones (2026); Kobayashi et al. (2022, 2025) include it in a more broadly defined Therizinosauridae.

Erlikosaurus.etymology: Named after Erlik, the god of the underworld in Turkic and Mongolian mythology, + Greek sauros (lizard): 'Erlik's lizard'.
Erlikosaurus.description: Erlikosaurus is a genus of therizinosaurid that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period. The fossils, a skull and some post-cranial fragments, were found in the Bayan Shireh Formation of Mongolia in 1972, dating to around 96 and 89 million years ago. These remains were later described by Altangerel Perle and Rinchen Barsbold in 1980, naming the new genus and species Erlikosaurus andrewsi. It represents the second therizinosaur taxon from this formation (after Segnosaurus), with the most complete skull among members of this peculiar family of dinosaurs.

Eshanosaurus.etymology: Named for Eshan County in Yunnan Province, China, where the fossil was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Eshanosaurus.description: Eshanosaurus is a genus of a dinosaur from the early Jurassic Period. It is known only from a fossil partial lower jawbone, found in China. It may be a therizinosaurian, and if so the earliest known coelurosaur.

dispute.summary: Both the affinities and the age of Eshanosaurus are contested. The original description (Xu et al., 2001) and a dedicated reassessment (Barrett, 2009) interpret its partial dentary as therizinosaurian, which, given the Early Jurassic age reported for the type locality, would make it the oldest known coelurosaur and imply an extensive ghost lineage. Others read the same material as a basal sauropodomorph (Kirkland and Wolfe, 2001); Senter and others (2012) noted that all but three of the cited therizinosaurian characters also occur in sauropodomorphs, and both Zanno (2010) and Sues and Averianov (2016) treat its therizinosaurian identity as problematic. It has never been included in a numerical phylogenetic analysis. Saurischia is the least-inclusive clade the therizinosaur (theropod) and sauropodomorph hypotheses share.

history.note: Placed at Therizinosauria following the therizinosaurian affinity defended by Xu et al. (2001) and Barrett (2009); its position within the clade is untested and its identity and Early Jurassic age remain disputed.

Broadened to Saurischia incertae sedis. The therizinosaurian identity (a coelurosaurian theropod) is untested and doubted, and a basal-sauropodomorph reading is credible, so the two hypotheses straddle the theropod-sauropodomorph divide and the conservative shared node is adopted.

Eucamerotus.etymology: From Greek eu- (well/good) + kamara (chamber/vault) + -otos (pertaining to): 'well-chambered', referring to the hollow pneumatic cavities in its vertebrae.
Eucamerotus.description: Eucamerotus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) Wessex Formation (Wealden) of the Isle of Wight, England. The type specimen, part of a vertebra (one of the bones of the spine), was discovered in the autumn of 1869 by John Hulke. After confirming its point of origin with the Rev. William Fox, Hulke presented his find to the Geological Society of London in 1870. Two years later, he assigned to it the name Eucamerotus, though did not provide a species name. Eucamerotus was subsequently treated as a junior synonym of two existing sauropods, Pelorosaurus and Ornithopsis. In 1995, William T. Blows gave a species name, creating the combination Eucamerotus foxi. While the validity of the genus has continued to be questioned, a 2011 publication found it to be a valid genus of titanosauriform. Comparisons with the fossils of other macronarians suggests it may have reached up to 15 m (49 ft) in length.
diagnostic_features: Opisthocoelous centrum (concave anterior articular surface)
Large deep excavation in side of centrum beneath neural canal root (pneumatic foramen); pneumaticity unusual for sauropod contemporaries
Vertical median wedge-plate (bolt) descending from postzygapophyses to neural canal crown, articulating with notch between prezygapophyses
Extremely complex neural arch with composite multi-pillar neural spine (anterior pillars rising from arch crown; posterior pillars above postzygapophyses) joined by thin laminae

Eucnemesaurus.etymology: From Greek eu- (good/well) + kneme (tibia/shin) + sauros (lizard): 'good tibia lizard', referring to its robust tibiae.
Eucnemesaurus.description: Eucnemesaurus is a basal sauropodomorph dinosaur genus usually considered to be a synonym of Euskelosaurus. Recent study by Yates (2006), however, indicates that it is valid and the same animal as putative "giant herrerasaurid" Aliwalia.
diagnostic_features: Tibia head proportionally much larger (longer and broader) than in all compared Plateosauridae and Anchisauridae, including Gryponyx, Plateosaurus, and Massospondylus
Trochanter minor of femur situated nearly equidistant from medial and lateral sides, not near the medial side as in most Plateosauridae

Femur of practically solid structure with thick lamellar substantia compacta and only small central cavity, contrasting with hollow limb bones typical of Theropoda
Trochanter quartus situated relatively closer to the proximal end of the femur than in Euskelesaurus Browni

Euhelopus.etymology: From Greek 'helos' meaning 'swamp' and Greek 'pous' meaning 'foot', giving 'true marsh-foot' (prefix 'eu-' meaning 'true' was added by Romer in 1956 when renaming from Helopus); the name refers to the marshy area of the finds and to Swedish swamp shoes (truga) which Wiman said resembled the animal's wide feet.
Euhelopus.description: Euhelopus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived between 143 and 133 million years ago during the Berriasian and Valanginian ages of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Shandong Province in China. It was a large quadrupedal herbivore. Like sauropods such as brachiosaurids and titanosaurs, Euhelopus had longer forelimbs than hindlimbs. This discovery was paleontologically significant because it represented the first dinosaur scientifically investigated from China - seen in 1913, rediscovered in 1922, excavated in 1923, and studied by T'an during the same year.
diagnostic_features: Teeth procumbent, with an asymmetrical crown-to-root margin (mesial margin nearer the crown apex) and well-developed crown buttresses on the mesiolingual surface
Cervical neural arches with an epipophyseal-prezygapophyseal lamina dividing two pneumatocoels throughout the cervical series
Anterior cervical ribs with three costal spurs on the tuberculum and capitulum; middle cervical ribs hanging well below the centrum on elongate parapophyses and capitula
Presacral neural spines 16 to 21 trifid, with a median tubercle as large as or larger than the metapophyses
Middle and posterior dorsal parapophyseal and diapophyseal laminae crossing to form a K-shaped configuration on the lateral face of the neural arch
Presacral pneumaticity extending into the ilium

Euoplocephalus.etymology: From Greek 'eu' meaning 'well', 'hoplon' meaning 'weapon' or 'armor', and 'kephale' meaning 'head', meaning 'well-armored head'.
Euoplocephalus.description: Euoplocephalus is a genus of large herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaurs, living during the Late Cretaceous of Canada. It has only one named species, Euoplocephalus tutus.
diagnostic_features: Cranial ornamentation absent posterior to the orbits; lacks postocular caputegulae (subcircular ornamentation) at the bases of the squamosal and quadratojugal horns
First cervical half ring with oval to subcircular-based keeled medial and lateral primary osteoderms, lacking interstitial osteoderms at their bases
Tail club knob with semicircular major osteoderms in dorsal view
Laterally directed sacral ribs
Proportionately short postacetabular process of the ilium
Anteriorly directed nares and no continuous keel between the squamosal horn and the supraorbitals

Euronychodon.etymology: A contraction of "Europe" and Paronychodon (the genus whose teeth Euronychodon's resemble); the popular gloss is "European claw tooth".
Euronychodon.description: Euronychodon is the name given to a genus of coelurosaur dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Europe and Asia. It is known from teeth only, which are similar to those of another coelurosaur tooth genus, Paronychodon.
diagnostic_features: Teeth recurved with completely smooth (unserrated) anterior and posterior edges.
Crown divided into a convex labial face and a truncated, flattened lingual face.
Lingual face traversed by one or several longitudinal ridges subject to strong wear.
Longitudinal ridges on lingual face abraded and marked by fine oblique striations due to wear.
Anterior and posterior edges of crown parallel at base then diverge at abrupt angle before curving.

dispute.summary: Europasaurus is consistently recovered as a basal macronarian, but its precise placement is disputed: the analyses of D'Emic (2012) and Mannion et al. (2006) place it as a basal camarasauromorph outside both Camarasauridae and Brachiosauridae. Jones (2026) leaves the family-level placement open.

Europasaurus.etymology: From Europa (Europe, named after the Phoenician princess in Greek mythology) + Greek sauros, 'lizard'; means 'Europe lizard', referring to its discovery in Germany
Europasaurus.description: Europasaurus is a genus of dwarf sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Süntel Formation of Lower Saxony, Germany. The type and only species, Europasaurus holgeri, is notable for being among the smallest known adult sauropods, likely the result of insular dwarfism on the Late Jurassic European archipelago.
diagnostic_features: Nasal process of premaxillary projecting anterodorsally.
Medial notch on posterior dorsal margin of cervical vertebral centra.
Scapular acromion with a prominent posterior projection.
Transverse width of astragalus twice its dorsoventral height and anteroposterior length.
Wing-shaped posterior process of postorbital slightly longer and wider than the anterior process (differs from Camarasaurus where it is much shorter).

species.name: Europasaurus holgeri
species.etymology: Named for Holger Lüdtke, the private fossil collector who discovered the first sauropod tooth at the Langenberg quarry in Germany in 1998.

Uniquely among the specimens it shows lines of arrested growth and partly lamellar internal bone, indicating it died after reaching full adult body size and securing the dwarf taxon's maximum size.

The youngest and smallest known individual at 1.75 meters long. It lacks growth marks and laminar bone tissue, identifying it as a young juvenile and anchoring the histological growth series used to show Europasaurus was a true dwarf rather than a juvenile of a larger taxon.

Europatitan.etymology: From 'Europa' (Europe), referring to its discovery in Iberia, combined with Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant', meaning 'European giant'.
Europatitan.description: Europatitan is an extinct genus of somphospondylan sauropod from the Early Cretaceous Castrillo de la Reina Formation of Iberia, known from a relatively complete specimen discovered in the early 2000s. It contains a single species: the type species, Europatitan eastwoodi.

Europelta.etymology: From Europa (Europe, where it was found) + Greek pelte (shield): 'Europe's shield', reflecting its nodosaurid armor and European origin.
Europelta.description: Europelta is a monospecific genus of nodosaurid dinosaur from Spain that lived during the Early Cretaceous (early Albian stage, ~113.0 Ma) in what is now the lower Escucha Formation of the Teruel Province. The type and only species, Europelta carbonensis, is known from two associated partial skeletons, and represents the most complete ankylosaur known from Europe. Europelta was named in 2013 by James I. Kirkland and colleagues. Europelta has an estimated length of 5 meters (16 feet) and weight of 1.3 tonnes (2,866 lbs), making it the largest member of the clade Struthiosaurini.

Tibia longer relative to femur length (90%) than in other ankylosaurs for which these proportions are known
Laterally compressed, flanged osteoderm with flat plate-like base present anteriorly on the pelvic shield

Eustreptospondylus.etymology: From Ancient Greek eu- (well) + streptos (twisted) + spondylos (vertebra): 'well-twisted vertebra', referring to the morphology of its vertebrae.
Eustreptospondylus.description: Eustreptospondylus is an extinct genus of megalosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Callovian and Oxfordian stages of the Jurassic period (some time between 166 and 154 million years ago) in southern England, at a time when Europe was a series of scattered islands due to tectonic movement that raised the sea-bed and flooded the lowland.

Squamosal with a hypertrophied ventral flange that overhangs the infratemporal fenestra in lateral view, partially obscuring its posterodorsal corner.
Ventral midline keels absent from the centra of the cervical, cervicodorsal, and dorsal vertebrae.
Marked depression on the anterior part of the ventral surface of cervical vertebra 10.

Excavation along the posterior surface of the ventral process of the postorbital, forming a shallow fossa around the anterior margin of the infratemporal fenestra (distinguishing it from all other spinosauroids).

Fabrosaurus.etymology: From Fabre (honoring Jean Fabre, the French geologist who collected the holotype with Ginsburg's expedition) and Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "Fabre's lizard".

dispute.summary: Fabrosaurus is a nomen dubium based on a fragmentary dentary from the Early Jurassic of Lesotho, widely regarded as indeterminate and possibly a junior synonym of Lesothosaurus (Jones, 2026). The former family Fabrosauridae erected around it is no longer recognized.

Falcarius.description: Falcarius is a genus of primitive therizinosaur dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous period in what is now North America. Its remains were first collected in the Cedar Mountain Formation in 1999, with subsequent findings made during the 2000s. The genus is known from multiple specimens ranging from immature to fully-grown individuals.

Flexor tubercle of phalanx I-II with well-defined collateral pits on distal aspect

Ferenceratops.etymology: From Hungarian 'Ferenc' (Francis), the birth name of paleontologist Franz Nopcsa von Felső-Szilvás (1877-1933), who first reported dinosaur remains from the Haţeg Basin, and Greek 'keras/keratos' (horn) and 'ops' (face).
Ferenceratops.description: Ferenceratops is an extinct genus of basal ceratopsian dinosaur from the Maastrichtian Sînpetru and Densuș-Ciula Formations of the Haţeg Basin, western Romania. The single species, Ferenceratops shqiperorum, was originally described by Weishampel et al. (2003) as a second species of the rhabdodontid ornithopod Zalmoxes; Maidment et al. (2026) reanalysed the holotype postcrania and recovered it as a ceratopsian, erecting a new genus and arguing that 'Zalmoxes' shqiperorum belongs to a previously unrecognised European ceratopsian lineage that also includes Ajkaceratops from Hungary.

dispute.summary: Ferenceratops shqiperorum was erected by Maidment and others (2026) for material formerly assigned to the ornithopod Zalmoxes shqiperorum, which they recovered as a European ceratopsian near the Ceratopsoidea. Its affinities within Ceratopsia are not yet corroborated by other analyses.

history.note: Placed at Ceratopsia incertae sedis following Maidment and others (2026); finer placement unresolved.

diagnostic_features: Scapula with a narrow, strap-like scapular blade bearing a distal expansion.
Well-developed, upwardly concave acromial process of the scapula.
Coracoid with an extremely elongate and slender sternal process that projects well below the ventral margin of the glenoid.
Gently curved ischium that lacks an obturator process.

species.etymology: Honors the Albanian people (Albanian 'shqiptarët').

Ferganocephale.etymology: From Fergana (the Fergana Valley region of Central Asia, near Kyrgyzstan where it was found) + Greek kephale, 'head'; means 'Fergana head'
Ferganocephale.description: Ferganocephale is a dubious genus of neornithischian dinosaur. It was from the Middle Jurassic Balabansai Svita of Kyrgyzstan. The type and only species is F. adenticulatum.

dispute.summary: Ferganocephale was originally described as the oldest pachycephalosaur on the basis of isolated teeth (Averianov and others, 2005), but this was soon disputed (Sullivan, 2006) and it is now treated as an ornithischian of uncertain placement (Butler and Sullivan, 2009; Jones, 2026).

history.note: Placed at Ornithischia incertae sedis; tooth-based nomen dubium, the pachycephalosaur identification rejected.

Marginal crown denticles absent or so small that they are eliminated by the slightest wear.
Basal crown cingulum interrupted at the center of the labial side in maxillary teeth and of the lingual side in mandibular teeth.
Vertical wrinkled ornamentation present on the less concave crown side adjacent to the basal cingulum interruption, at least in some teeth.

Ferrisaurus.etymology: From Latin 'ferrum' meaning 'iron' and Ancient Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'iron lizard', referring to the discovery along a rail line.
Ferrisaurus.description: Ferrisaurus is a genus of leptoceratopsid ceratopsian dinosaur from the Sustut Basin (Tango Creek Formation) in British Columbia, Canada. The type and only species is Ferrisaurus sustutensis. It is the first non-avian dinosaur described from British Columbia.

Astragalus and tibia coossified, a condition otherwise reported in only one Montanoceratops specimen among leptoceratopsids
Distal end of ulna proportionally broader relative to radius length than in Leptoceratops

Fona.description: Fona is an extinct genus of thescelosaurine thescelosaurid ornithischian dinosaurs from the 'mid'-Cretaceous Cedar Mountain Formation (Mussentuchit Member) of Utah, United States. The genus contains a single species, F. herzogae, known from several partial skeletons and skulls. Based on anatomical similarities to the closely related and similarly aged Oryctodromeus, Fona was likely a semi-fossorial animal, likely spending a significant amount of time in underground burrows. It also represents the oldest known definitive thescelosaurine.

Foskeia.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'phōs' meaning 'light' and 'boskein' meaning 'to forage', referring to its small size and presumed herbivorous habits.
Foskeia.description: Foskeia is an extinct genus of rhabdodontomorph ornithopod dinosaurs known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian to Aptian ages) Castrillo de la Reina Formation of Spain. The genus contains a single species, Foskeia pelendonum, known from fossils of multiple individuals of different ontogenetic stages. Before its formal description, it had been nicknamed the "Vegagete ornithopod."

Fruitadens.etymology: From Fruita (the city of Fruita, Colorado, USA, where fossils were found) + Latin dens (tooth): 'Fruita teeth'.
Fruitadens.description: Fruitadens is a genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur. The name means "Fruita teeth", in reference to Fruita, Colorado (USA), where its fossils were first found. It is known from partial skulls and skeletons from at least four individuals of differing biological ages, found in Tithonian (Late Jurassic) rocks of the Morrison Formation in Colorado. Fruitadens is one of the smallest known ornithischian dinosaur, with young adults estimated at 65 to 75 cm (26 to 30 in) in length and 0.5 to 0.75 kg (1.1 to 1.7 lb) in weight. It is interpreted as an omnivore and represents one of the latest-surviving heterodontosaurids.
diagnostic_features: Premaxillary crowns small and subequal in size, expanded labiolingually and mesiodistally above the root (autapomorphic within Heterodontosauridae).
Denticles extend over half of the maxillary/dentary crowns, not restricted to apical third (autapomorphic within Heterodontosauridae).
Dentary caniniform present but apicobasal height does not exceed that of the largest dentary cheek tooth crown (autapomorphic within Ornithischia).

Fukuivenator.etymology: From Fukui (Fukui Prefecture, Japan, where it was found) + Latin venator (hunter): 'hunter of Fukui Prefecture'.
Fukuivenator.description: Fukuivenator is an extinct genus of maniraptoran theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Kitadani Formation of Japan.

dispute.summary: The affinities of Fukuivenator are disputed. Its original description (Azuma et al., 2016) recovered it as a basal maniraptoran of uncertain position that could not be referred to any known coelurosaurian subgroup, and Hartman et al. (2019) placed it near the base of Maniraptora. A CT-based osteological restudy by the same group (Hattori et al., 2021) instead recovered it as the basalmost member of Therizinosauria, citing therizinosaurian synapomorphies such as a subotic recess, eleven or more cervical vertebrae, and anterior humeral condyles, though the authors caution that support for this position is weak. The Princeton Encyclopedia (Jones, 2026) adopts the basalmost therizinosaur placement. Maniraptora is the least-inclusive clade all these hypotheses accept.

history.note: Placed at Therizinosauria as its basalmost member following Hattori et al. (2021) and Jones (2026), which supersede the incertae sedis interpretation of Azuma et al. (2016); the placement is weakly supported.

Broadened to Maniraptora incertae sedis. The basalmost-Therizinosauria placement (Hattori et al., 2021) is by the authors' own admission weakly supported, and Hartman et al. (2019) instead recover Fukuivenator near the base of Maniraptora, outside Therizinosauria, so the conservative shared node is adopted.

diagnostic_features: Unusually large external naris slightly smaller than antorbital fenestra in dorsoventral height; large premaxillary fenestra subequal in size to maxillary fenestra.
Highly heterodont dentition with robust unserrated teeth: small spatulate anterior teeth, large posteriorly curved middle teeth, and small nearly symmetrical posterior teeth.
Anterior and middle cervical vertebrae with transversely bifid neural spines, a feature unknown in any other theropod.
Dorsoventrally bifurcated sacral ribs, a feature previously unreported in any other theropod.
Middle caudal vertebrae with distally bifid prezygapophyses, not reported in any dinosaur previously.
Caudal zygapophyseal facets expanded to be substantially wider than the zygapophyseal processes.

Galeamopus.etymology: From Latin 'galeam' (accusative of 'galea', 'helmet') and 'opus' meaning 'need'; intended as a translation of 'Wil-helm' ('want helmet'), honoring the first names of Utterback and Holland, and alluding to the brittle braincase of the type specimen being in need of a helmet.
Galeamopus.description: Galeamopus is a genus of herbivorous diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs. It contains two known species - Galeamopus hayi, known from the Late Jurassic lower Morrison Formation (Kimmeridgian age, about 155 million years ago) of Wyoming, United States, and Galeamopus pabsti, known from Wyoming and Colorado. The type species is known from one of the well-preserved diplodocid fossils, a nearly complete skeleton with an associated skull.
diagnostic_features: Dorsoventral height of parietal occipital process low, subequal to less than diameter of foramen magnum (unique among Diplodocinae)
Basipterygoid processes widely diverging (>60°; unique among Diplodocinae)
Ulna to humerus length ratio of more than 0.76 (unique within Diplodocoidea)
Distal articular surface for the ulna on the radius reduced and relatively smooth (unique within Diplodocidae)
Distal condyle of the radius beveled at least 15° to the long axis of the shaft (unique within Diplodocinae)
Lateral edge of proximal end of tibia forms a pinched out projection posterior to the cnemial crest (unique among Diplodocidae)

Galleonosaurus.etymology: Galleon lizard; named for the resemblance of the upper jaw bone to an upturned galleon, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Galleonosaurus.description: Galleonosaurus is a genus of basal ornithopod dinosaur from the Wonthaggi Formation of the Gippsland region of Victoria, Australia. The type and only species is Galleonosaurus dorisae.

Lingual margin of maxillary tooth roots in midregion of tooth row form an S-bend at their bases
Posterior third of maxilla on some specimens deflects posterolaterally at an abrupt kink
Lateral end of palatine lateral ramus forms a hatchet-shaped flange

Gallimimus.etymology: Chicken mimic; from Latin gallus (chicken) and mimus (mimic), referring to similarities between its neck vertebrae and those of Galliformes
Gallimimus.description: Gallimimus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous period. Several fossils in various stages of growth were discovered by Polish-Mongolian expeditions in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia during the 1960s; a large skeleton discovered in this region was made the holotype specimen of the new genus and species Gallimimus bullatus in 1972. The generic name means "chicken mimic", referring to the similarities between its neck vertebrae and those of the Galliformes. The specific name is derived from bulla, a golden capsule worn by Roman youth, in reference to a bulbous structure at the base of the skull of Gallimimus. At the time it was named, the fossils of Gallimimus represented the most complete and best preserved ornithomimid ("ostrich dinosaur") material yet discovered, and the genus remains one of the best known members of the group.
diagnostic_features: Very long snout, broad and flattened dorsoventrally at the tip; infratemporal fossa subtriangular with jugal excluded from its borders.
Common exit for third and fourth cranial nerves merges with the optic fissure.
Lower jaw shovel-like anteriorly, with elongated external mandibular fenestra.
Length of presacral vertebral column equal to combined length of femur, tibia-astragalus, and third metatarsal; transition point between caudals 15 and 16.
Humerus longer than scapula; manus equal about a quarter of total forelimb length; ungual of digit III shorter than penultimate phalanx of digit III.
Metatarsus more than 70% of crural length; metatarsal II equal 97% of length of metatarsal IV; pedal digit III equal a third of crural length.

dispute.summary: Galvesaurus has been recovered as a non-neosauropod eusauropod within Turiasauria (Royo-Torres et al., 2006, a placement favored by Mocho et al., 2014) and as a basal titanosauriform or basal macronarian near the base of Titanosauriformes (Mannion et al., 2017; Perez-Pueyo et al., 2019; Jones, 2026). The more recent and dedicated analyses favor a basal titanosauriform position.

history.note: Moved from Brachiosauridae to Titanosauriformes incertae sedis following the recent consensus (Mannion et al., 2017; Perez-Pueyo et al., 2019; Jones, 2026); the turiasaurian alternative is noted.

Galvesaurus.etymology: Galve lizard; named after Galve, the town in Spain where fossils were found, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Galvesaurus.description: Galvesaurus, or Galveosaurus (meaning "Galve lizard"), is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic period. Fossils of the only known species, G. herreroi, were found in Galve, Spain, hence its generic name. The specific name herreroi honors the discoverer, José María Herrero. Some researchers suggest that the taxon might represent a junior synonym of the Portuguese genus Lusotitan.
diagnostic_features: Elongation Index in mid-dorsal vertebrae is approximately 0.5.

In mid-dorsal vertebrae, centrum and neural arch connected only by anterior and posterior centrodiapophysial laminae, with no contact of centroprezygapophysial or centropostzygapophysial laminae with the centrum.
Parapophyses in dorsal vertebrae situated in the centroprezygapophysial lamina rather than dividing the anterior centrodiapophysial lamina as in other sauropods.
In mid-dorsal vertebrae, accessory laminae connect intraprezygapophysial laminae with centroprezygapophysial laminae.
Composite lamina formed by union of lateral spinopostzygapophysial and spinodiapophysial laminae runs along the posterior margin of the spine in mid-dorsal vertebrae.
Deep cavity between spinoprezygapophysial and spinodiapophysial laminae in mid-dorsal vertebrae, bridged by an accessory lamina connecting both.

synonyms.name: Galveosaurus
synonyms.reason: Controversial near-simultaneous publication; Galvesaurus (Barco et al., July 2005) generally accepted as senior over Galveosaurus (Sánchez Hernández, August 2005), though publication-date disputes and ethical concerns remain.

Gandititan.etymology: Combines 'Gan' referencing Ganzhou City, the Chinese word 'di' meaning 'Earth' (also the first syllable of 'dizhi', meaning 'geology'), and 'titan' referencing the pre-Olympian giants of Greek mythology; the specific name cavocaudatus combines Latin 'cavum' (cavity) and 'cauda' (tail), alluding to the caudal vertebrae morphology.
Gandititan.description: Gandititan is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Zhoutian Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, G. cavocaudatus, known from a partial skeleton.
diagnostic_features: Long and narrow fossae present on dorsal and ventral parts of lateral surfaces of middle and posterior cervical centra
Sacral neural spines fused into a dorsal platform with undulating (wave-shaped) lateral margins
Anteriormost six caudal vertebrae with bifurcated neural spines
Prominent triangular dorsal flanges on transverse processes of anteriormost caudal vertebrae (caudals 1-3)
Paired slit-like foramina present on ventral surface of each anterior caudal centrum
Additional (accessory) spinoprezygapophyseal laminae present on some anterior caudal vertebrae (caudals 4-5)
Prominent lamina extending anteroposteriorly between bases of pre- and postzygapophyses in anterior caudal vertebrae (caudals 6-11)

species.name: Gandititan cavocaudatus

history.note: Placed conservatively at Somphospondyli following the original description; the titanosaurian alternative (Jones, 2026) is noted.

Gannansaurus.etymology: Gannan lizard; named after the Gannan region (Ganzhou Basin) of Jiangxi Province, China, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Gannansaurus.description: Gannansaurus is an extinct genus of somphospondylan sauropod dinosaur known from the latest Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation of Ganzhou Basin, Jiangxi Province of southern China. It is known from specimen GMNH F10001 which consists of a single, nearly complete dorsal vertebra and a mid-caudal vertebra. Gannansaurus was first named by Lü Junchang, Yi Laiping, Zhong Hui and Wei Xuefang in 2013 and the type species is Gannansaurus sinensis. Gannansaurus shares some characters with Euhelopus, indicating that it is more closely related to it rather than to other titanosauriforms.
diagnostic_features: Two centroprezygapophyseal lamina fossae, with neural canal and distinct openings separately located at the bottom and upper portion of the large square-shaped concavity formed by centroprezygapophyseal laminae and dorsal margin of the centrum.
Large infraparapophysial fossa.
Large, round lateral concavity with an eye-shaped pleurocoel inset, occupying 65% the length of the centrum.
PCPL (posterior centroparapophysial lamina) and ACPL (anterior centroparapophysial lamina) weakly developed.
PCDL (posterior centrodiapophysial lamina) separated into two branches by an infradiapophysial fossa dorsally.
Wide and shallow ventral concavity on the caudal vertebra.

species.etymology: From Latin 'sinensis' meaning 'of China', referring to the country where the specimens were found.

Ganzhousaurus.etymology: Ganzhou lizard; named after Ganzhou City in Jiangxi Province, China, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Ganzhousaurus.description: Ganzhousaurus is an extinct genus of oviraptorid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation of Nankang County, Ganzhou City of Jiangxi Province, southern China. It was found in a Maastrichtian deposit and contains a single species, Ganzhousaurus nankangensis. It is distinguished by a combination of primitive and derived features.
diagnostic_features: Relatively shallow dentary with length-to-depth ratio of 1.90, shallower than in other oviraptorids such as Citipati (1.50) and Nemegtomaia (1.38).
Absence of fossa or pneumatopore on lateral surface of dentary, in contrast to Gigantoraptor, Chirostenotes, and Caenagnathasia.
Ventral border of external mandibular fenestra formed mainly by angular, unlike other oviraptorids where the dentary posteroventral branch forms most of the ventral border.
Angular anterior process wider transversely than deep dorsoventrally, unknown in other oviraptorosaurs.
Shallow longitudinal groove along medial surface of dentary posteroventral process, condition uncertain in most other oviraptorosaurs.
Prominent ventral flange along distal half of metatarsal II, giving bone a subtriangular mid-shaft cross-section; absent in Citipati and Heyuannia.

Gargoyleosaurus.description: Gargoyleosaurus is one of the earliest ankylosaurs known from reasonably complete fossil remains. The holotype was discovered in 1995 at the Bone Cabin Quarry West locality, in Albany County, Wyoming in exposures of the Upper Jurassic (Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages) Morrison Formation.

First neck armor ring consists of five partly fused plates; second ring consists of six partly fused plates
Body armor consists of thin-walled cones, unlike the solid conical armor of Mymoorapelta

Garudimimus.etymology: Garuda mimic; named after Garuda, the divine bird from Hindu and Buddhist mythology, combined with Latin mimus (mimic)
Garudimimus.description: Garudimimus is a genus of ornithomimosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous. The genus is known from a single specimen found in 1981 by a Soviet-Mongolian paleontological expedition in the Bayanshiree Formation and formally described in the same year by Rinchen Barsbold; the only species is Garudimimus brevipes. Several interpretations about the anatomical traits of Garudimimus were made in posterior examinations of the specimen, but most of them were criticized during its comprehensive redescription in 2005. Extensive undescribed ornithomimosaur remains at the type locality of Garudimimus may represent additional specimens of the genus.
diagnostic_features: Jaw articulation positioned more posteriorly than the postorbital bar (quadrate mandibular condyle behind the postorbital bar), making the posterior edge of the skull nearly vertical.
Paired fossae at the base of the dorsal process of the supraoccipital, absent in other ornithomimosaurs.
Paired depressions on the lateral surface of the neural spines at the base of the proximal caudal vertebrae.
Deep groove at the proximal end of the lateral surface of pedal phalanges III-1 and III-2.

Garumbatitan.etymology: Garumba giant; named after the Garumba river near the discovery site in Spain, combined with Titan from Greek mythology
Garumbatitan.description: Garumbatitan is an extinct genus of somphospondylan sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Arcillas de Morella Formation of Spain. The genus contains a single species, G. morellensis, known from multiple partial skeletons.
diagnostic_features: Depression near anterior edge of centrum above lateral crest in middle-posterior caudal vertebrae
Middle-posterior caudal vertebral pedicels covered by complex of three anteroposteriorly elongated ridges
Middle-posterior caudal neural spines expanded posteriorly resulting in lateral rounded boss
Femur with markedly developed lateral bulge representing 44% of transverse minimal width of femoral shaft
Trochanteric shelf with proximolaterally-to-distolaterally orientation
Metatarsals II, III, and IV more gracile and longer than metatarsals I and V with abrupt transition, causing retraction of most medial and lateral toes

dispute.summary: Gasosaurus constructus is most likely a basal tetanuran of indeterminate position (Carrano, Benson and Sampson, 2012). It is placed conservatively at Tetanurae incertae sedis.

Gasosaurus.etymology: From English 'gasoline' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', named for the gasoline company whose workers discovered the fossils.
Gasosaurus.description: Gasosaurus is a genus of tetanuran theropod that lived approximately 171.6 to 161.2 million years ago during the middle of the Jurassic Period. The name "Gasosaurus" is derived from the English "gasoline" and the Greek σαῦρος (sauros) ("lizard / generic reptile"). Only one species is currently recognized, G. constructus, from which the specific name honors the gasoline company that found the Dashanpu fossil quarry in Sichuan Province, China, now named as the Lower Shaximiao Formation.

Ilium low with weakly developed anterior process
Pubis and ischium with circular shaft cross-section and lacking boot-shaped distal process, distally unfused

Gasparinisaura.description: Gasparinisaura is a genus of herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous. The first fossils of Gasparinisaura were found in 1992 near Cinco Saltos in Río Negro Province, Argentina. The type species, Gasparinisaura cincosaltensis, was named and described in 1996 by Rodolfo Coria and Leonardo Salgado. The generic name honors Argentine paleontologist Zulma Brandoni de Gasparini. The specific name refers to Cinco Saltos.

Gastonia.etymology: Named for American fossil collector Robert Gaston, who discovered the specimens.
Gastonia.description: Gastonia is a genus of herbivorous ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of North America, around 139 to 125.77 million years ago. It is often considered a nodosaurid closely related to Polacanthus. Gastonia has a sacral shield and large shoulder spikes.
diagnostic_features: Three sacral vertebrae (vs. four in Polacanthus); ilia with slender, anteriorly diverging preacetabular processes (vs. short and nearly parallel in Polacanthus).

Tibia considerably shorter and more robust than in Polacanthus and Hylaeosaurus, with strongly flaring proximal and distal ends.
Dorsal armor uniquely characterized by scutes bordered by radially directed ridges around their margins.

Skull unique among all known ankylosaurs in having a broad premaxillary notch, posteriorly placed narial openings, and basisphenoid with elongate basipterygoid processes forming a gliding joint with the unfused pterygoids.

dispute.summary: The placement of Genusaurus is contentious. It has been assigned to Coelophysoidea originally, then to Noasauridae (Carrano and Sampson, 2008), and to Abelisauridae by most subsequent analyses (Tortosa and colleagues, 2014; Rauhut and Carrano, 2016); it is often unstable, and Pol and colleagues (2024) could not place it, pruning it from their consensus as an unstable taxon. Buffetaut (2026) revised the type material and argued it is an early member of the abelisaurid clade Furileusauria, the earliest known, though it may prove an indeterminate furileusaurian.

history.note: Placed at Abelisauridae following the prevailing recent analyses.
Buffetaut (2026) revised the type material and interpreted Genusaurus as an early furileusaurian; retained at Abelisauridae pending broader acceptance of the finer placement.

Genusaurus.etymology: Knee lizard; from Latin genu (knee) and Greek sauros (lizard), referring to distinctive features of the knee region
Genusaurus.description: Genusaurus is a genus of abelisaurid theropod from the Early Cretaceous. Its fossils were found in France. Genusaurus is believed to have lived during the Albian stage, around 112-100 million years ago.

Genyodectes.etymology: Jaw bite; from Greek genys (jaw) and dektes (bite)
Genyodectes.description: Genyodectes is a genus of ceratosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous (Aptian-Albian) of South America. The holotype material (MLP 26-39, Museo de La Plata, La Plata, Argentina) was collected from the Cerro Barcino Formation, Cañadón Grande, Departamento Paso de Indios in the Chubut Province of Argentina and consists of an incomplete snout, including the premaxillae, portions of both maxillas, the right and left dentary, many teeth, a fragment of the left splenial, and parts of the supradentaries. These elements are generally poorly preserved and some are in articulation. The premaxilla of Genyodectes possesses relatively large and protruding teeth, similar to those of Ceratosaurus. The specific name, serus, means "late". In 2016 it was estimated to be 6.25 meters (20.5 ft) in length and 790 kg (1,740 lb) in weight.
diagnostic_features: Premaxillary teeth closely spaced and arranged in an overlapping en-echelon pattern (shared, if at all, only with Ceratosaurus).
Longest maxillary tooth crowns exceeding the minimal dorsoventral depth of the mandible in apicobasal length (shared, if at all, only with Ceratosaurus).
Four premaxillary teeth, versus three in Ceratosaurus.

Geranosaurus.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'geranos' meaning 'crane' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', giving 'crane lizard'; the name refers to the bird-like limb bones, while the specific name atavus is Latin for 'ancestor', referencing its position as an early ornithischian.
Geranosaurus.description: Geranosaurus is a genus of heterodontosaurid ornithischian dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic, between 191.1 and 187.5 million years ago. It is known from a single species, G. atavus, that was named in 1911 by Robert Broom for partial jaws found during road-cutting in South Africa. The genus name is likely derived from the word for "crane" in reference to the bird-like limb bones, while the species name means "ancestor" likely in reference to its position as an early ornithischian. The limited material and poor preservation of Geranosaurus have rendered it difficult to diagnose, with authors accepting it as a dubious name though differentiable from its relative Heterodontosaurus, the only other heterodontosaurid known from the Clarens Formation.

dispute.summary: Geranosaurus is a nomen dubium based on fragmentary jaw material from the Early Jurassic of South Africa; it shows heterodontosaurid features but most analyses conclude the remains lack sufficient diagnostic characters (Sereno, 2012; Jones, 2026).

history.note: Retained at Heterodontosauridae incertae sedis; nomen dubium, a heterodontosaurid by anatomy but not diagnosable.

Giganotosaurus.etymology: From Greek gigas/gigantos, 'giant', + Greek notos, 'south/southern', + Greek sauros, 'lizard'; means 'giant southern lizard', referring to its enormous size and South American origin
Giganotosaurus.description: Giganotosaurus is a genus of large theropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Argentina, during the early Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 99.6 to 95 million years ago. The holotype specimen was discovered in the Candeleros Formation of Patagonia in 1993 and is almost 70% complete. The animal was named Giganotosaurus carolinii in 1995; the genus name translates to "giant southern lizard", and the specific name honors the discoverer, Ruben Carolini. A dentary bone, a tooth, and some tracks, discovered before the holotype, were later assigned to this animal. The genus attracted much interest and became part of a scientific debate about the maximum sizes of theropod dinosaurs.

Eave-like supraorbital lacrimal-postorbital contact.

Proximal end of the scapula forwardly projected above the coracoid; tubercle-like triceps insertion on the ventral border of the scapula.
Lobule-shaped obturator process of the ischium; dorsally projected femoral head; posterior intercondylar groove in the proximal end of the tibia.

Gigantoraptor.etymology: From Greek gigas/gigantos, 'giant', + Latin raptor, 'thief/seizer'; means 'giant thief', referring to its status as the largest known oviraptorosaur
Gigantoraptor.description: Gigantoraptor is a genus of large oviraptorosaurian dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period. It is known from the Iren Dabasu Formation of Inner Mongolia, where the first remains were found in 2005.

dispute.summary: Gigantoraptor is now generally recovered as a basal caenagnathid (Longrich et al., 2013; Lamanna et al., 2014; Funston, 2020), a marked departure from its original description as a basal oviraptorid (Xu et al., 2007). A minority result (Hartman et al., 2019) still recovers it, with Microvenator, within Oviraptoridae. It is placed at Caenagnathidae following the prevailing view.

history.note: Placed at Caenagnathidae (basal) following the caenagnathid analyses; Hartman et al. (2019) alternatively recover it as an oviraptorid.

diagnostic_features: Short mandible less than 45% of femoral length, with a fossa on the lateral surface of the dentary close to the anterior end and a second fossa bounded dorsally by a lateral flange anterodorsal to the external mandibular fenestra.

Tail composed of opisthocoelous anterior caudal vertebrae, amphicoelous middle ones, and procoelous posterior ones, with pleurocoels on most caudal vertebrae and a pair of vertically arranged pneumatic openings on the lateral surface of anterior caudal centra.
Laterally bowed humerus with a prominent spherical humeral head, strongly medially curved deltopectoral crest, and a centrally constricted thick ridge along the posterior margin of the proximal half.

Metacarpal I with a medial condyle three times as high as and extending much more distally than the lateral one; metacarpal II with a prominent dorsolateral process on the proximal end and a longitudinal groove on the ventral margin of the proximal third of the shaft.

Femur with a constricted neck between the posteromedially oriented spherical femoral head and the anteroposteriorly wide trochanteric crest, and a patellar groove on the anterior surface of the distal end.
Small calcaneum obscured from anterior view by the wide astragalar main body; proximal projection on the lateral margin of distal tarsal IV; metatarsal III with ginglymoid distal end.

Gigantosaurus.etymology: From Ancient Greek gigas (giant) and sauros (lizard); meaning "giant lizard".
Gigantosaurus.description: Gigantosaurus is a dubious genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Kimmeridge Clay Formation of England. The type species, Gigantosaurus megalonyx, was named and described by Harry Govier Seeley in 1869.

Gigantspinosaurus.etymology: From Latin gigas/giganteus, 'enormous', + Latin spina, 'spine', + Greek sauros, 'lizard'; means 'giant-spined lizard', referring to its massive shoulder spines
Gigantspinosaurus.description: Gigantspinosaurus is a genus of stegosaurian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) Upper Shaximiao Formation of China. The type species is Gigantspinosaurus sichuanensis. It was a moderately sized member of the group, measuring up to 4.2 meters (14 ft) in length.

External mandibular fenestra present, with a well-developed coronoid process and an elongated ridge along the lateral surface of the dentary
Four firmly fused sacral vertebrae, the sacral neural spines co-ossified with the last dorsal neural spine into a fore-and-aft elongate plate

Gilmoreosaurus.etymology: Charles Whitney Gilmore's lizard; named in honor of American paleontologist Charles Whitney Gilmore, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Gilmoreosaurus.description: Gilmoreosaurus is a genus of hadrosauromorphan dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Asia. The type species is Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis, known from the Iren Dabasu Formation of Inner Mongolia, of latest Campanian to early Maastrichtian age. Additional specimens have been described as distinct species, including G. atavus from the Khodzhakul Formation of Uzbekistan, and G. arkhangelskyi from the Bissekty Formation, also of Uzbekistan. However, these are based on very fragmentary remains, and their classification is dubious. An additional species, G. kysylkumense, also from the Bissekty Formation, is sometimes included, though it has also been referred to the related genus Bactrosaurus.
diagnostic_features: Paddle-shaped postacetabular process of the ilium, less than 70% of the length of the iliac central plate.
Ilium combining an ischial tuberosity with a supraacetabular process whose apex lies posterodorsal to the ischial peduncle (a unique combination within Hadrosauroidea).
Manual phalanx III-1 with a strongly asymmetrical distal articular surface.

Giraffatitan.etymology: Titanic giraffe; from the animal name giraffe and Greek Titan, referring to its enormous size and giraffe-like long neck
Giraffatitan.description: Giraffatitan is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the late Jurassic Period (Kimmeridgian-Tithonian stages) in what is now Lindi Region, Tanzania. Only one species is known, G. brancai, named in honor of German paleontologist Wilhelm von Branca, who was a driving force behind the expedition that discovered it in the Tendaguru Formation. Giraffatitan brancai was originally described by German paleontologist Werner Janensch as a species of the North American sauropod Brachiosaurus from the Morrison Formation, as Brachiosaurus brancai. Recent research shows that the differences between the type species of Brachiosaurus and the Tendaguru material are so large that the African material should be placed in a separate genus.

Mid dorsal centra approximately same length as posterior dorsal centra
Anterior dorsal spines and transverse processes much taller and wider than those of posterior dorsals, forming shoulder withers
Neural arches short vertically and fore and aft; transversely broad transverse processes forming a shallow V
Dorsal column less than twice humerus length and short relative to vertebra height; body mass relatively modest relative to limbs
Dorsal centra pleurocoels moderate in size

Glacialisaurus.etymology: From Latin glacialis, 'icy' or 'frozen', + Greek sauros, 'lizard'; means 'icy lizard' or 'frozen lizard', referring to its discovery in Antarctica
Glacialisaurus.description: Glacialisaurus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic period of Antarctica. It is known from two specimens; the holotype (name-bearing specimen), a partial tarsus (ankle) and metatarsus, and a partial left femur (thigh bone). The fossils were collected by a team led by paleontologist William R. Hammer during a 1990-91 field expedition to the central region of the Transantarctic Mountains. They come from sedimentary rocks of the Hanson Formation and date to the Pliensbachian stage of the Early Jurassic, around 186 to 182 million years ago.

Glishades.etymology: Concealed in mud; from Latin glis (mud) and Greek Hades (lord of the underworld, meaning unseen), referring to being found in sedimentary strata
Glishades.description: Glishades is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur that lived in the Late Cretaceous in North America. It is based on AMNH 27414, two partial premaxillae discovered in the Upper Cretaceous rocks of the upper Two Medicine Formation in Montana, dated to about 74.5 million years ago. Cladistic analysis conducted by Prieto-Márquez suggests that Glishades is a non-hadrosaurid hadrosauroid, probably a sister taxon to Bactrosaurus johnsoni. The type species is Glishades ericksoni. In 2012, Campione et al. suggest the holotype specimen of Glishades might actually be an indeterminate juvenile saurolophine hadrosaurid and consider it to be a nomen dubium.

Glyptodontopelta.etymology: Glyptodon shield; named for resemblance of its armor to that of the prehistoric mammal Glyptodon, combined with Greek pelta (shield)
Glyptodontopelta.description: Glyptodontopelta is a monospecific genus of nodosaurid dinosaur from New Mexico that lived during the Late Cretaceous (lower to upper Maastrichtian, 69 to 66 Ma) in what is now the Naashoibito member of the Ojo Alamo Formation. The type and only species, Glyptodontopelta mimus, is known from numerous specimens that consist of osteoderms, a dentary, supraorbital and bone fragments. It was named in 2000 by Tracy Ford. Edmontonia australis is a junior synonym of Glyptodontopelta.

dispute.summary: Glyptodontopelta is known almost entirely from osteoderms. Vickaryous et al. (2004) listed the osteoderm taxon Edmontonia australis — since synonymized into Glyptodontopelta and revalidated by Burns (2008) — as a nomen dubium; the genus cannot be placed below Ankylosauria. It is retained at Ankylosauria incertae sedis.

history.note: Placed at Ankylosauria incertae sedis, armor-based and not placeable to family.

Gnathovorax.etymology: From Greek gnathos (jaw) and Latin vorax (voracious, devouring); meaning 'devouring jaw', referring to its predatory nature
Gnathovorax.description: Gnathovorax is a genus of herrerasaurid saurischian dinosaur from the Santa Maria Formation in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. The type and only species is Gnathovorax cabreirai, described by Pacheco et al. in 2019. The type specimen comprises a mostly complete and well-preserved articulated skeleton (considered one of the best herrerasaurid skeletons ever discovered), which fossilized in close association with rhynchosaur and cynodont remains. The discovery of this superb specimen has shed light onto poorly understood aspects of herrerasaurid anatomy such as endocranial soft tissues.

Gobihadros.description: Gobihadros is a genus of basal hadrosauroid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now the Bayanshiree Formation (dated to the Cenomanian-Santonian) of Mongolia. It contains only the type species Gobihadros mongoliensis, which has an estimated length of 7.5 m (25 ft).

Up to three functional teeth in the dentary tooth row (convergent in Hadrosauridae); other non-hadrosaurid hadrosauroids have only one or two functional teeth per position.
Sigmoidal dorsal outline of the ilium with a well-developed, fan-shaped posterior process.
Greater lateral expression of the supracetabular crest compared to Bactrosaurus, Probactrosaurus, Eolambia, Claosaurus, and Tethyshadros.
Spike-like manus digit 1, differing from Tethyshadros insularis, Plesiohadros djaktaensis, and Hadrosauridae.

Gobiraptor.description: Gobiraptor is a genus of oviraptorid maniraptoran dinosaur from the Maastrichtian-aged Nemegt Formation of Mongolia. The type and only species is Gobiraptor minutus, known from a single incomplete specimen-the holotype MPC-D 102/111. It has been found not to be closely related to the other oviraptorids it shared its environment with.

dispute.summary: Originally described as a large coelophysoid (Carpenter, 1997), Gojirasaurus quayi rests on a composite holotype (UCM 47221) of fragmentary, largely non-diagnostic elements. Nesbitt and others (2007) found that only some components — the tibia and pubis — are clearly coelophysoid and distinct from the co-occurring pseudosuchian Shuvosaurus, whereas others (the scapula and vertebrae) are indistinguishable from it and the serrated tooth could belong to any large carnivorous archosaur. Even the coelophysoid elements lack unambiguous autapomorphies — the robust tibia matches Coelophysis-like material apart from its larger size — so the taxon is widely treated as a metataxon and nomen dubium. Ezcurra and others (2020) recovered it on the stem lineage to Averostra; it is placed conservatively at Neotheropoda incertae sedis.

history.note: Placed at Neotheropoda, the least-inclusive clade the sources support.

Status set to nomen dubium: the holotype is a composite of fragmentary, largely non-diagnostic elements (a metataxon per Nesbitt and others, 2007), with scapula and vertebrae indistinguishable from the co-occurring Shuvosaurus and no unambiguous autapomorphies even in the coelophysoid tibia and pubis. Extended the dispute summary, removed the contested diagnostic_features, and wired in the Nesbitt and others (2007) and Ezcurra and others (2020) papers.

Like some other sauropods, Gondwanatitan was tall and ate tough shoots and leaves from the tops of trees. Its closest relative was Aeolosaurus. Gongbusaurus.etymology: Named for the imperial Chinese ministry of public works (gong bu), honoring the Tang dynasty poet Du Fu who served in that ministry after 760 AD as a 'junior consultant' (shi yi), combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.

A small herbivore, it is very poorly known. Two species have been assigned to it, but as the original name is based on teeth, there is no concrete evidence to connect the two species. Its fossils have been found in China.

Gongpoquansaurus.etymology: Gongpoquan reptile; named after Gongpoquan in the Mazongshan area of Gansu Province, China, where the specimen was collected
Gongpoquansaurus.description: Gongpoquansaurus is an extinct genus of basal hadrosauroid dinosaur that was not formally named until 2014, while the name was a nomen nudum for many years previously. It is known from IVPP V.11333, a partial skull and postcranial skeleton. It was collected in 1992 at locality IVPP 9208-21, from the Albian Zhonggou Formation (Xinminpu Group), in Mazongshan, Gansu Province, China. The specimen was first described and named by Lü Junchang in 1997 as the third species of Probactrosaurus, Probactrosaurus mazongshanensis. Following its description, several studies found it to be less derived than the type species of Probactrosaurus in relation to Hadrosauridae. In 2014, the species was formally redescribed, and the describers erected Gongpoquansaurus.

Gongshuilong.etymology: From "Gongshui" (the Gong River, near the discovery site in Jiangxi, China) and Chinese "long" (dragon); meaning "Gong River dragon".
Gongshuilong.description: Gongshuilong is an extinct genus of saurolophine hadrosaurid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age) Lianhe Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, Gongshuilong fanwei, known from a bonebed representing the disarticulated remains of at least two individuals. Gongshuilong is a member of the group Brachylophosaurini within the Hadrosauridae, and it is the second member of this otherwise North American clade, following Wulagasaurus, found in Asia. It is also the first hadrosaurid to be named from fossils found in South China. Gongshuilong is characterized by the uniquely elongated and curved neural spines of the vertebrae at the end of the tail, forming a tall, sail-like structure.
diagnostic_features: Greatly elongate, moderately recurved, posterodorsally directed neural spines on the posterior caudal vertebrae, about 8.5 times as tall as their corresponding centra, forming a sail-like structure along the tail.
Extremely shortened edentulous margin of the dentary, with a margin-to-tooth-row length ratio of about 0.05, markedly lower than in other saurolophids.
Poorly developed deltoid ridge on the lateral surface of the proximal scapula, unlike the condition in other saurolophines.

Gongxianosaurus.etymology: Named for Gongxian County in Sichuan Province, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Gongxianosaurus.description: Gongxianosaurus is a genus of basal sauropod dinosaur from the early Jurassic Period (Sinemurian-Pliensbachian stage). The only species is Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis. Based on four fragmentary to complete specimens found in the Ziliujing Formation, China (Sichuan Province), it is one of the most completely known early sauropods. The skeleton is known in large part, missing both the hand and the majority of the skull. Gongxianosaurus was firstly named and described in a short note published in 1998; however, a comprehensive description has yet to be published. Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis was named for the place it was found, near the village Shibei in Gong County (珙县; Pinyin: Gǒng Xiàn).

dispute.summary: Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis sits close to the sauropodiform-sauropod boundary. He et al. (1998), describing the genus, placed it within Sauropoda as an early and primitive sauropod retaining numerous prosauropod-like features, though without a cladistic analysis, and McPhee et al. (2014) likewise recovered it in an unresolved basal-Sauropoda polytomy. Rauhut et al. (2020) instead recovered it among sauropodiforms outside Sauropoda, and Pol et al. (2022) place it outside Eusauropoda on strong support.

history.note: Placed at Sauropodiformes incertae sedis; the basal-Sauropoda placement is recorded, but the boundary remains unresolved.

Anterior caudal neural spines broad and plate-shaped with extremely well-developed diapophyses that are broad anteroposteriorly and thin dorsoventrally; no caudal haemal arch is bifurcated
Forelimb length 70-75% the length of the hindlimb
Pes phalanges thick and short, lacking proximolateral ligament depressions; unguals lack dorsolateral longitudinal grooves

Gorgosaurus.etymology: From Greek gorgos (dreadful, fierce) and sauros (lizard); meaning 'dreadful lizard'
Gorgosaurus.description: Gorgosaurus is a genus of tyrannosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in western North America during the Late Cretaceous Period (Campanian), between about 76.5 and 75 million years ago. Fossil remains have been found in the Canadian province of Alberta and the U.S. state of Montana. Paleontologists recognize only the type species, G. libratus, although other species have been erroneously referred to the genus.

Premaxillary teeth long and slender with a keel on each side of a slightly convex lingual surface, laterally compressed with fore-aft diameter slightly greater than breadth
No triangular alveolar plates on the inner sides of the jaws
A foramen present in the surangular, positioned far back and near its upper border; no presplenial
Manus reduced to two digits (II and III) with metacarpal IV represented only by a proximal vestigial bone; humerus twice the length of the ulna
Metatarsal III nearly two-thirds the length of the femur; metatarsal I represented distally by a short vestigial bone giving digit I a forwardly directed position

species.name: Gorgosaurus libratus
species.etymology: From Latin 'libratus', the past participle of 'librare' meaning 'to balance', likely referring to the animal's balanced build.

Specimen from Montana showing severe pathologies: healed leg, rib, and vertebral fractures, osteomyelitis at the tip of the lower jaw resulting in permanent tooth loss, and possibly a brain tumor.

Very complete sub-adult preserving face-bite injuries, a thoroughly healed right fibula fracture, a healed dentary fracture, and a mushroom-like hyperostosis of a right pedal phalanx; preserved in a characteristic death pose.

Goyocephale.etymology: From Mongolian goyo (decorated, ornate) and Ancient Greek kephale (head); meaning 'decorated head'
Goyocephale.description: Goyocephale is an extinct genus of pachycephalosaurian ornithischian that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous about 76 million years ago. It was first described in 1982 by Altangerel Perle, Teresa Maryańska and Halszka Osmólska for a disarticulated skeleton with most of a skull, part of the forelimb and hindlimb, some of the pelvic girdle, and some vertebrae. Perle et al. named the remains Goyocephale lattimorei, from the Mongolian гоё (goyo), meaning "decorated", and the Ancient Greek κεφαλή (kephale), for head. The species name honors Owen Lattimore.
diagnostic_features: Supratemporal fenestra longitudinally oval with narrow interfenestral bridge about one third the transverse width of the fenestra
Occiput weakly concave with a relatively small occipital condyle
Ventral maxillary edge weakly arched laterally along its posterior portion
Medial portion of cranial roof indistinctly ornamented
Sacrum includes only four weakly coossified vertebrae

Dorsal surface of preacetabular process of ilium flat and bent angularly along medial and lateral margins; medial iliac flange short anteroposteriorly; postacetabular process straight and subrectangular in lateral view

species.name: Goyocephale lattimorei

Graciliceratops.description: Graciliceratops is a genus of neoceratopsian dinosaurs that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period.

Graciliraptor.etymology: Graceful thief; from Latin gracilis (graceful) and raptor (thief or seizer)
Graciliraptor.description: Graciliraptor is a genus of microraptorian dromaeosaurid dinosaur from the early Cretaceous Period. Its fossil, holotype IVPP V 13474, was found in Beipiao, Liaoning Province, China. The type species is Graciliraptor lujiatunensis, named and described in 2004 by Xu Xing and Wang Xiaoling. The generic name is derived from Latin gracilis (meaning "graceful") and raptor (meaning "thief"). The specific name refers to the village of Lujiatun where the fossil site is located.
diagnostic_features: Laminal structure connecting the postzygapophyses of middle caudals.
Middle caudals extremely long and slender (centrum length/width ratio ~8.6).
Ungual of manual digit I much smaller than that of manual digit II.
Proximal end of metacarpal III strongly expanded dorsoventrally, deeper than metacarpal II.
Proximal tibiotarsus shaft rectangular in cross section; tibiotarsus extremely slender (length/midshaft-diameter ratio ~28).
Astragalar medial condyle significantly expanded posteriorly; metatarsal II distally much wider than other metatarsals.

species.etymology: Named for the village of Lujiatun in Liaoning Province, China, where the fossil site is located.

Gravitholus.etymology: From Latin gravis (heavy) and tholus (dome); meaning 'heavy dome', referring to its thick skull roof
Gravitholus.description: Gravitholus was a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur from the late Cretaceous period (Campanian stage, around 75 million years ago). It was a pachycephalosaur, and like other pachycephalosaurids the skull roof formed a thick dome made of dense bone, which may have been used in head-butting contests over mates or territory. It lived in what is now Alberta, Canada, and was described in 1979 by W. P. Wall and Peter Galton. The type species is Gravitholus albertae.

dispute.summary: The validity of Gravitholus is contested. Dyer et al. (2023) used synchrotron microtomography and morphometrics to argue that Gravitholus albertae is a subjective junior synonym of Stegoceras validum, a conclusion followed by Jones and Viola (2026); its describing-era treatment (Longrich et al., 2010) considered it valid. Pending broad consensus it is retained as a valid basal pachycephalosaurid.

history.note: Placed at Pachycephalosauridae (Stegoceras-grade), kept valid pending consensus although recent work synonymizes it with Stegoceras validum.

diagnostic_features: Skull roof thickened to a very wide dome, larger than any known specimen of Stegoceras.
Parietal contains a large depression and many smaller pits.

Braincase significantly smaller relative to dome size compared even to large specimens of Stegoceras validus (endocranial length/frontoparietal length ratio of 31.3 vs. minimum ~42 for large Stegoceras).
Extreme dome width produces a significantly different width ratio compared to Stegoceras and Pachycephalosaurus.
Node-like ornamentation absent.

species.name: Gravitholus albertae
species.etymology: From 'Alberta', the Canadian province where the holotype was recovered, with the Latin suffix '-ae' indicating possession.

Gremlin.etymology: Named for the gremlin, a small troublesome mythical creature.
Gremlin.description: Gremlin is a genus of leptoceratopsid ceratopsian dinosaurs from the Campanian stage of the Cretaceous period, 77 million years ago. It contains one species, Gremlin slobodorum, named in 2023 by Michael J. Ryan and colleagues from a frontal bone found in the Oldman Formation of Alberta.

Transverse ridge and anterior margin of the frontal depression both diverge from the same point on the slightly raised medial frontal margin.
Transverse ridge marks the point of maximum thickness of the frontal, from which the bone tapers anteriorly and sharply posteriorly across the frontal depression.

Gryphoceratops.description: Gryphoceratops is an extinct genus of leptoceratopsid ceratopsian dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, southern Canada.

Gryponyx.etymology: Hooked-claw; from Greek grypos (hooked) and onyx (claw)
Gryponyx.description: Gryponyx is an extinct genus of massopod sauropodomorph known from southern Free State, central South Africa.

dispute.summary: Gryponyx africanus has been recovered as a basal massospondylid (Vasconcelos and Yates, 2004); some referred species are nomina dubia and the validity of the genus is debated (Jones, 2026).

Pubes and ischia form a complete symphysis with no opening from front of pubis to posterior end of ischium

Gryposaurus.etymology: From Greek grypos (hook-nosed, curved) and sauros (lizard); meaning 'hooked-nosed lizard', referring to its arched nasal profile
Gryposaurus.description: Gryposaurus (meaning "hook-nosed lizard"; sometimes incorrectly translated as "griffin (Latin gryphus) lizard") was a genus of duckbilled dinosaur that lived about 80 to 75 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous (late Santonian to late Campanian stages) of North America. Named species of Gryposaurus are known from the Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, Canada, and two formations in the United States: the Lower Two Medicine Formation in Montana and the Kaiparowits Formation of Utah. A possible additional species from the Javelina Formation in Texas may extend the temporal range of the genus to 66 million years ago.
diagnostic_features: Nasals highly arched, rising to extraordinary height a short distance in advance of the orbits; nasal apex as high as the summit of the squamosal behind the supratemporal fossa.
Skull uniquely deep anteriorly among Trachodontidae; depth at apex of nasal bones equal to about half the maximum skull length.
Lower anterior border of premaxillae expanded laterally and notched in a regular manner on each side of the median sutural union.
Predentary expanded laterally, deflected in its hinder half, and posteriorly bifurcated below at the midline into two processes received into excavations of the dentaries.
Orbit much smaller than the lateral temporal fossa; lateral temporal fossa more than twice as high as wide.
Body covered with small, polygonal, non-imbricating, tuberculate scales of rather uniform size, varying from 1/8 to 3/8 inch diameter with no definite pattern arrangement.

species.etymology: From Latin 'notabilis' meaning 'notable' or 'remarkable', in reference to the distinctive hooked nasal arch that sets this dinosaur apart from other hadrosaurs.

Anterior portion of the dentary sharply downturned.
Surangular with a distinct dorsal process on its median ridge.
Mandibular foramen ovoid (subcircular in other species).

Guaibasaurus.etymology: Named after the Guaíba River region of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, where it was discovered, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning 'Guaíba lizard'
Guaibasaurus.description: Guaibasaurus is an extinct genus of basal saurischian dinosaur known from the Late Triassic Caturrita Formation of Rio Grande do Sul, southern Brazil. Most analyses recover it as a sauropodomorph, although there are some suggestions that it was a theropod instead. In 2016 Gregory S. Paul estimated it at around 2 meters long (6.6 ft) and 10 kg (22 lbs), whereas in 2020 Molina-Pérez and Larramendi listed it at 3 meters (10 ft) and 35 kg (77 lbs).

dispute.summary: Guaibasaurus candelariensis has an unstable position: originally a basal theropod, it is recovered as a basal sauropodomorph by recent analyses (Novas and others, 2010, within Guaibasauridae; Hechenleitner and others, 2025, as sister to Bagualosauria). The family Guaibasauridae is not adopted here, being contested and effectively monotypic.

history.note: Placed at Sauropodomorpha incertae sedis (basal) following the recent sauropodomorph hypotheses; the basal-theropod alternative and the deprecated Guaibasauridae are recorded.

diagnostic_features: Midanterior dorsal neural arches with large pneumatic cavities opening below the base of the transverse process
Undivided infradiapophyseal lamina combined with a well-developed parapophyseal-prezygapophyseal lamina and a deep fossa below it
Acetabulum nearly closed, with only incipient reduction of the medial wall, plus an extremely large crista supracetabularis and a well-developed fossa brevis
Sacral centra of strongly unequal size, the anterior centrum about twice the volume of the next
Femur with a small anterior trochanter, a dorsolateral ridge above the anterior trochanter, and no trochanteric shelf
Calcaneum transversely narrow with a pronounced ventromedial process; metatarsal V strongly reduced and without phalanges while metatarsal I is unreduced

Gualicho.etymology: Named in reference to the gualichu, a malevolent supernatural entity in the mythology of the Mapuche and other Patagonian peoples
Gualicho.description: Gualicho is an enigmatic genus of theropod dinosaurs. The type species is Gualicho shinyae. It lived in what is now northern Patagonia, on what was then a South American island continent split off from the supercontinent Gondwana. The fossils were found in the Huincul Formation, dating to the late Cenomanian-early Turonian age of the upper Cretaceous Period, around 91 million years ago.

dispute.summary: The position of Gualicho shinyae is highly unstable. Apesteguía et al. (2016) recovered it as a neovenatorid carcharodontosaurian (an allosauroid) sister to Deltadromeus, arguing its tyrannosaurid-like didactyl manus is convergent rather than evidence of tyrannosauroid affinity; other analyses instead place it within Coelurosauria (Porfiri et al., 2018) or as an early-branching ornithomimosaur alongside Deltadromeus (Delcourt et al., 2025), and ceratosaurian traits have also been noted (Jones and Viola, 2026). Because these hypotheses span Allosauroidea and Coelurosauria, it is placed conservatively at Avetheropoda incertae sedis. It is not a tyrannosauroid.

history.note: Removed from Tyrannosauroidea and placed conservatively at Avetheropoda incertae sedis, pending resolution of its unstable position.
Confirmed placement at Avetheropoda incertae sedis; the allosauroid-versus-coelurosaur-versus-ornithomimosaur position remains unresolved.

diagnostic_features: Posterior dorsal vertebrae very elongated with slit-like pneumatic openings
Scapular blade narrow with sinuous rostral margin marked by a shallow notch between the acromion process and blade
First and second metacarpals co-ossified proximally; third metacarpal reduced to a splint; forelimb functionally didactyl
Pubes with little or no pubic apron and blade-like boot
Fibula with large fossa and accessory flange on proximocaudal corner, and ridge-like m. iliofibularis tubercle
Third metatarsal with expanded proximal articulation with posterior edge wider than rostral edge (antarctometatarsal condition)

Guanlong.etymology: From Chinese guan (crown) and long (dragon); meaning 'crown dragon', referring to its prominent cranial crest
Guanlong.description: Guanlong is an extinct genus of proceratosaurid tyrannosauroid dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) Shishugou Formation of China. It was first described in 2006 by Xu Xing and colleagues, who found it to represent a new taxon related to Tyrannosaurus. Two individuals are currently known, consisting of a partially complete adult and a nearly complete juvenile.
diagnostic_features: Deep and narrow groove along the anterior margin of the premaxilla.

Hadrosaurus.description: Hadrosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaurs that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous Period in what is now the Woodbury Formation in New Jersey about 83.6 to 77.9 million years ago. The holotype specimen was found in fluvial marine sedimentation, meaning that the corpse of the animal was transported by a river and washed out to sea. Hagryphus.etymology: From Egyptian Ha (a god of the western desert) and Greek gryps/gryphon (griffin); meaning 'Ha's griffin'
Hagryphus.description: Hagryphus is a monospecific genus of caenagnathid dinosaur from southern Utah that lived during the Late Cretaceous (upper Campanian stage, 75.95 Ma) in what is now the Kaiparowits Formation of the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument. The type and only species, Hagryphus giganteus, is known only from an incomplete but articulated left manus and the distal portion of the left radius. It was named in 2005 by Lindsay E. Zanno and Scott D. Sampson. Hagryphus has an estimated length of 2.4-3 meters (8-10 feet) and weight of 50 kilograms (110 lbs).

Lacking reduction and/or fusion of metacarpals and phalanges, distinguishing it from Avimimus and Caudipteryx

Halticosaurus.etymology: Jumping lizard; from Greek altikos (good at jumping) and sauros (lizard)
Halticosaurus.description: Halticosaurus is a dubious genus of theropod dinosaur from the late Triassic period (middle Norian stage, around 215.6-208 million years ago). It is known from a single fragmentary fossil specimen of the species H. longotarsus, found in the Middle Stubensandstein formation of what is present-day Germany The only known specimen was poorly preserved and may have been put together from bones of unrelated animals. Further research would be required to determine which of the bones belonged together, and what kind of theropod Halticosaurus was. However, most of the bones have been lost. For these reasons, Halticosaurus is considered to be a nomen dubium.
