Leptorhynchos.etymology: From Greek 'leptos' meaning 'slender' or 'thin' and 'rhynchos' meaning 'beak' or 'snout', referring to a slender beak.
Leptorhynchos.description: Leptorhynchos is an extinct genus of caenagnathid theropod from the Late Cretaceous of what is now the US state of Texas, although it has been suggested to also exist in Alberta and South Dakota. The type species is L. gaddisi, and it is currently the only widely accepted valid species. The generic name of Leptorhynchos comes from the Greek "leptos" meaning "small" and "rhynchos" meaning "beak". The specific epithet is in honor of the Gaddis family, who owned the land on which the holotype was discovered.

Leshansaurus.etymology: Named after Leshan, the city in Sichuan Province, China, near where fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Leshan lizard'
Leshansaurus.description: Leshansaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Shaximiao Formation of what is now China. It was described in 2009 by a team of Chinese paleontologists. The type species is Leshansaurus qianweiensis. Fossils of Leshansaurus were discovered in strata from the Shangshaximiao Formation, a formation rich in dinosaur fossils. Li et al. referred this taxon to Sinraptoridae - a group of carnosaurian theropods, but it may belong to Megalosauridae instead.

Lesothosaurus.etymology: Named after Lesotho, the country in southern Africa where it was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'lizard from Lesotho'
Lesothosaurus.description: Lesothosaurus is a monospecific genus of ornithischian dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic in what is now South Africa and Lesotho. It was named by paleontologist Peter Galton in 1978, the name meaning "lizard from Lesotho". The genus has only one valid species, Lesothosaurus diagnosticus. Lesothosaurus is one of the most completely-known early ornithischians, based on numerous skull and postcranial fossils from the Upper Elliot Formation. It had a simpler tooth and jaw anatomy than later ornithischians, and may have been omnivorous in some parts of the year.

dispute.summary: Lesothosaurus is one of the most unstable basal ornithischians. It has been recovered as the most basal thyreophoran (Butler and others, 2008; Boyd, 2015), as the basalmost neornithischian (Herne and others, 2019; Manitkoon and others, 2023, followed by Jones, 2026), and as an ornithischian outside Genasauria (Baron and others, 2017; Fonseca and others, 2024). Because these placements straddle Genasauria, it is placed at the least-inclusive uncontested node.

history.note: Placed at Ornithischia incertae sedis; recovered variously as basal Thyreophora, basalmost Neornithischia, or outside Genasauria.

diagnostic_features: Anterior premaxillary foramen piercing the premaxilla near the alveolar margin, opening onto the premaxillary palate just anterior to the first premaxillary tooth.

Forelimb very short, less than 40% of hind-limb length.

Groove on the dorsal margin of the proximal ischial shaft, passing onto the medial side of the blade.
Pedal digit I reduced, with metatarsal I splint-shaped proximally and the ungual extending just beyond the second metatarsal.

Liaoceratops.etymology: From 'Liaoning' (the Chinese province where it was discovered) combined with Greek 'keras' (horn) and 'ops' (face); meaning 'Liaoning horned face'
Liaoceratops.description: Liaoceratops, meaning "Liaoning horned face", is a ceratopsian dinosaur believed to be an early relative of the horned ceratopsids. It lived in the Early Cretaceous, 126 million years ago. It was discovered in China by a team of American and Chinese scientists. Liaoceratops was much smaller than its later relatives, but offers a glimpse into the early evolution of this group of dinosaurs.

Liaoningvenator.description: Liaoningvenator is a genus of troodontid theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China. It contains a single species, L. curriei, named after paleontologist Phillip J. Currie in 2017 by Shen Cai-Zhi and colleagues from an articulated, nearly complete skeleton, one of the most complete troodontid specimens known. Ligabueino.etymology: Named for Italian doctor and fossil enthusiast Giancarlo Ligabue, its discoverer, with the diminutive '-ino' suffix in Italian meaning 'little one', hence 'Ligabue's little one'.
Ligabueino.description: Ligabueino is a genus of abelisauroid theropod dinosaur named after its discoverer, Italian doctor Giancarlo Ligabue. It is known only from an extremely fragmentary specimen, measuring 79 cm (2.6 ft) long, found in the La Amarga Formation. In spite of initial reports that it was an adult, the unfused vertebrae indicate that the specimen was a juvenile. It was a theropod and lived during the Early Cretaceous Period (Barremian to early Aptian), in what is now Patagonia. Contrary to initial classifications that placed it as a member of the Noasauridae, Carrano and colleagues found in 2011 that it could only be placed with any confidence in the group Abelisauroidea. In 2024, Ligabueino was recovered as a sister taxon of Berthasauridae and Abelisauroidea.

Liliensternus.description: Liliensternus is an extinct genus of basal neotheropod dinosaur that lived approximately 210 million years ago during the latter part of the Triassic Period in what is now Germany. Liliensternus was a bipedal, ground-dwelling carnivore, that could grow up to 5.15 m (16.9 ft) long; however, this size estimate is based on specimens now believed to be subadults, and possible fragmentary remains indicate an adult length of 7 to 9 meters. It is the best represented Triassic theropod from Europe and one of the largest known.

Limusaurus.etymology: From Latin 'limus' meaning 'mud' or 'mire' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'mire lizard', referring to the specimens appearing to have died after being mired in mud.
Limusaurus.description: Limusaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in what is now China during the Late Jurassic, around 161 to 157 million years ago. The type and only species Limusaurus inextricabilis was described in 2009 from specimens found in the Upper Shishugou Formation in the Junggar Basin of China. The genus name consists of the Latin words for "mud" and "lizard", and the species name means "impossible to extricate", both referring to these specimens possibly dying after being mired. Limusaurus was a small, slender animal, about 1.7 m (5 ft 7 in) in length and 15 kg (33 lb) in weight, which had a long neck and legs but very small forelimbs (with reduced first and fourth fingers). It underwent a drastic morphological transformation as it aged: while juveniles were toothed, these teeth were completely lost and replaced by a beak with age. Several of these features were convergently similar to the later ornithomimid theropods as well as the earlier non-dinosaurian shuvosaurids.

Lingyuanosaurus.description: Lingyuanosaurus is a genus of therizinosaurian theropod from the Early Cretaceous of Liaoning Province, China. The type and only species is L. sihedangensis. It was uncovered within one of the formations that make up the Jehol biota, although the exact geological formation - and therefore also its precise geological age - is unknown.

dispute.summary: Lingyuanosaurus is a transitional therizinosaur whose precise position is weakly resolved. Its describers (Yao et al., 2019) recovered it within Therizinosauroidea, in an intermediate position between early-diverging genera such as Beipiaosaurus and later therizinosaurs, but support was low (a Bremer support of 1) and only a small fraction of the character matrix could be scored for the taxon. The Princeton Encyclopedia (Jones, 2026) instead treats it as a basal member of Therizinosauria, most closely related to Jianchangosaurus and Beipiaosaurus. It is placed conservatively at Therizinosauria.

history.note: Placed at Therizinosauria; Yao et al. (2019) recover it within Therizinosauroidea, but the position is weakly supported and Jones (2026) treats it as a basal therizinosaurian.

Linhenykus.etymology: Named for Linhe, a city near the fossil discovery site in Inner Mongolia, combined with Greek 'nykus' meaning 'claw'.
Linhenykus.description: Linhenykus is an extinct genus of alvarezsaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Inner Mongolia, China. It is the most basal known member of the Parvicursorinae. The genus gets its name from Linhe, a city near the site where the fossil was first found and Greek nykus, "claw". The specific name is derived from Greek monos, "single", and daktylos, "finger", a reference to the fact that it is the only known non-avian dinosaur to have had but a single digit.
diagnostic_features: Only phalanx-bearing digit in manus is digit II; digits III and IV entirely lack phalanges, making this the only functionally monodactyl nonavian dinosaur
Metacarpal III transversely compressed without distal articular surface
Longitudinal ventral furrow along entire length of each cervical centrum
Diapophyseal ridges on cervical vertebrae extend to posterodorsal rim of centrum
Weak ridge-like epipophyses on postzygapophyses of middle cervical vertebrae
Large pneumatic foramina in middorsal vertebrae
Anteriormost caudal vertebrae with amphiplatyan centra and neural spines located completely posterior to neural pedicles

species.name: Linhenykus monodactylus
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'monos' meaning 'single' and 'daktylos' meaning 'finger', referring to the fact that Linhenykus is the only known non-avian dinosaur with a single functional digit on each forelimb.

dispute.summary: Linheraptor is consistently recovered as a velociraptorine, as the sister taxon of Tsaagan (Jasinski et al., 2020; Pei et al., 2020; Jones et al., 2026). Its validity has been questioned: Senter and colleagues argued it is a junior synonym of Tsaagan mangas, but this was rejected by later restudy (Xu et al., 2015). The velociraptorine placement is not in doubt; only the genus-level distinction from Tsaagan is contested.

history.note: Placed in Velociraptorinae (sister to Tsaagan); the proposed synonymy with Tsaagan is noted but rejected by recent restudy.

Linheraptor.etymology: Named for Linhe, a city in Inner Mongolia near the fossil discovery site, combined with Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief' or 'plunderer'.
Linheraptor.description: Linheraptor is a genus of dromaeosaurid dinosaur which lived in what is now China in the Late Cretaceous. It was named by Xu Xing and colleagues in 2010, and contains the species Linheraptor exquisitus. This bird-like dinosaur was less than 2 m (6.5 ft) long and was found in Inner Mongolia. It is known from a single, nearly complete skeleton.

Several large foramina on lateral surface of jugal

Pneumatic foramen present on axis vertebra

species.etymology: From Latin 'exquisitus' meaning 'exquisite' or 'excellent', referring to the exceptionally well-preserved nature of the holotype skeleton.

Lirainosaurus.etymology: From Basque lirain (slender) combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "slender lizard"
Lirainosaurus.description: Lirainosaurus is a genus of titanosaur sauropod which lived in what is now Spain. The type species, Lirainosaurus astibiae, was described by Sanz, Powell, Le Loeuff, Martinez, and Pereda-Suberbiola in 1999. It was a relatively small sauropod, measuring 4 meters (13 ft) long, possibly up to 6 meters (20 ft) long for the largest individuals, and weighed about 2-4 metric tons (2.2-4.4 short tons).

Lamina in interzygapophysial fossa in anterior caudal vertebrae
Spinopostzygapophysial structure not posteriorly projected in posterior caudal vertebrae
Lateroanterior process on sternal plate
Ridge in ventral margin of medial side of scapular blade

Lishulong.description: Lishulong is a genus of sauropodiform dinosaur from the Early Jurassic (Sinemurian-Toarcian) Lufeng Formation of China. The type and only species is Lishulong wangi.

Liubangosaurus.etymology: Named after Liubang village, the holotype locality in Guangxi Province, China; meaning "Liubang lizard"
Liubangosaurus.description: Liubangosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now China. Liubangosaurus is known from the holotype NHMG 8152, five complete and articulated middle-caudal dorsal vertebrae that were collected from the Xinlong Formation in Fusui County, Guangxi Province. The type species is L. hei, which honors He Wenjian, who discovered the site where Liubangosaurus was discovered.
diagnostic_features: Prezygapophysis closely contacts with parapophysis, with the prdl and prpl absent.
Cavity present on the dorsal surface of the diapophysis.
Neural spine very low, with its distal end level with that of the diapophysis.
Distal end of the neural spine strongly expanded laterally to form a platform.
Vertically directed infradiapophyseal lamina expands or bifurcates ventrally to form an inverted 'Y'.
Highly positioned parapophyses large and tear-drop in shape.

species.etymology: Named for He Wenjian, who discovered the fossil site at Liubang Quarry in Guangxi Province, China, honored in the genitive Latin '-i' suffix.

Lohuecotitan.etymology: Named for Lo Hueco, the fossil site in Spain where it was discovered, combined with Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant'.
Lohuecotitan.description: Lohuecotitan is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur which lived during the Late Cretaceous in Spain. The only species known in the genus is Lohuecotitan pandafilandi, described and named in 2016.

dispute.summary: Placed within Lithostrotia as incertae sedis. The describing analysis (Díez Díaz et al., 2016) recovered Lohuecotitan only as an indeterminate derived lithostrotian in a polytomy, and later work recovers it as a basal lithostrotian (Díez Díaz et al., 2018). It is placed at Lithostrotia pending resolution.

history.note: Placed at Lithostrotia incertae sedis; recovered as an indeterminate derived lithostrotian and later as a basal lithostrotian.

diagnostic_features: Posterior centrodiapophyseal lamina dorsally and ventrally widened or bifurcated in anterior and middle dorsal vertebrae
Short postspinal lamina with transversely expanded distal end represented by smooth scars in dorsal vertebrae
Anteriormost caudal vertebrae with medial spinoprezygapophyseal and medial spinopostzygapophyseal laminae ventrally connected with prespinal and postspinal laminae
Anterior caudal neural spines with dorsal projection of prespinal and postspinal laminae, resulting in V-shaped outline in lateral view
Anterior caudal neural spines bearing greek-cross-like cross-section
Middle caudal vertebrae with two rough structures in dorsal edge of posterior articulation extending to dorsal surface of centrum
Articular ends of posterior haemal arch rami fully divided in two articular facets
Tuberosity between anterior and lateral trochanter of fibula

Lokiceratops.etymology: Named for Loki, the Norse god, combined with Greek 'ceratops' meaning 'horned face' (from 'keras' meaning 'horn' and 'ops' meaning 'face'), hence 'Loki horned face'. The species name 'rangiformis' means 'reindeer-shaped' in reference to its elaborate ornamentation.
Lokiceratops.description: Lokiceratops is an extinct genus of centrosaurine ceratopsian dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) Judith River Formation of Montana, United States. The genus contains a single species, L. rangiformis, known from most of the skull and a partial skeleton. Four other ceratopsians are known from the same stratigraphic interval as Lokiceratops-more than in any other locality-suggesting that this clade was very diverse during the Late Cretaceous of northern Laramidia.
diagnostic_features: Presence of unadorned nasal
Elongate, uncurved ep1 epiossification directed in plane of frill along posterior margin of parietosquamosal frill
Hypertrophied, lateral curving epiparietal ep2 directed in plane of frill, relatively larger than any other parietal epiossification within Centrosaurinae
Both ischia distinctly kinked distally at about two-thirds of shaft length where ischia contact medially
Postorbital horncore bases deeply excavated by sinuses penetrating a distance equivalent to the orbital diameter of each horncore

species.name: Lokiceratops rangiformis
species.etymology: From Latin 'rangiformis' meaning 'reindeer-shaped', referencing the mammal genus Rangifer (caribou or reindeer) whose antlers are bilaterally asymmetrical like the frill ornamentations of Lokiceratops.

Loncosaurus.etymology: Meaning uncertain; either from Araucanian 'lonco' meaning 'chief' or Greek 'lonche' meaning 'lance', combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Loncosaurus.description: Loncosaurus is an extinct genus of ornithopod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of Provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina. The type (and only known) species is Loncosaurus argentinus, described by the famous Argentinian paleontologist Florentino Ameghino, but is considered a dubious name. Details on this animal are often contradictory, befitting a genus that was long confused for a theropod.

dispute.summary: Loncosaurus argentinus is based on a partial femur, long confused with theropods; it is now regarded as an indeterminate iguanodontian and a nomen dubium (Norman, 2004).

history.note: Placed at Iguanodontia incertae sedis; nomen dubium.

diagnostic_features: Teeth with anterior edge denticulate down to base of crown, highly compressed with thin enamel layer
Great development of internal trochanter of femur, probably somewhat hooked
Femur body cylindrical with large medullary cavity (diameter 4.5-5 cm, ~50 cm total length)

species.name: Loncosaurus argentinus
species.etymology: No etymology was given by Ameghino (1899). Likely from Latin 'argentinus' meaning 'Argentine', a reference to the country of origin.

Lophorhothon.etymology: From Greek 'lophos' meaning 'crested' and 'rhothon' meaning 'nose', giving the meaning 'crested nose', referring to the nasal crest of the holotype.
Lophorhothon.description: Lophorhothon is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Alabama, and possibly Georgia and North Carolina. It was the first dinosaur genus discovered in Alabama, in the United States.

dispute.summary: Lophorhothon atopus was originally described as a basal hadrosaurine, inside Hadrosauridae (Langston, 1960), but later analyses place it within Hadrosauromorpha just outside Hadrosauridae, among the closest non-hadrosaurid relatives of the family (Alarcón-Muñoz and others, 2023; Jones, 2026).

history.note: Placed at Hadrosauromorpha; the historical inside-Hadrosauridae interpretation reflected, not adopted.

Frontals strongly domed above the orbits
Squamosals very widely separated medially, not meeting at the midline

Lophostropheus.etymology: From Greek 'lophè' meaning 'crest' and 'stropheus' meaning 'pertaining to the vertebrae', giving the meaning 'crest vertebrae', referring to the prominent dorsal and ventral laminae on the cranial cervical vertebrae.
Lophostropheus.description: Lophostropheus is an extinct genus of coelophysoid theropod dinosaur that lived approximately 205.6 to 196.5 million years ago during the boundary between the Late Triassic Period and the Early Jurassic Period, in what is now Normandy, France. Lophostropheus is one of the few dinosaurs that may have survived the Triassic-Jurassic extinction event.

Loricatosaurus.etymology: From Latin loricatus (armored) combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "armored lizard"
Loricatosaurus.description: Loricatosaurus is a genus of stegosaurid dinosaur known from Callovian-aged (Middle Jurassic) rocks of England and France.

Anterior caudal vertebrae bear small dorsal projections about two-thirds along transverse process
Mid-caudal vertebrae with large anterior and posterior chevron facets converging ventrally, creating V-shaped centra in lateral view

Loricosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'lorica' (armor/cuirass) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'armor lizard', in reference to the dermal armor on which the genus is based.
Loricosaurus.description: Loricosaurus is a genus of sauropod represented by a single species, L. scutatus. It is a titanosaur that lived near the end of the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 71 million years ago in the early Maastrichtian, being found in the province of Neuquen, Argentina in the Allen Formation. Due to the presence of armor, at first it was believed that it was an ankylosaur, but today it is considered to be that of a titanosaur.

dispute.summary: The type material is dermal armor only. Modern literature considers Loricosaurus scutatus a possible junior synonym of Neuquensaurus or Saltasaurus, but no formal synonymization has been published.

history.note: Refined from Titanosauria to Saltasaurinae incertae sedis; the osteoderms are indeterminate saltasaurine armor, and the species is treated as a nomen dubium.

species.name: Loricosaurus scutatus
species.etymology: No etymology was given by Huene (1929); the epithet is likely from Latin 'scutatus' meaning 'armed with a shield', referring to the dermal plates that form the type material.

type_specimen.material: Twenty-six cutaneous ossifications and dermal plates of varying sizes (1.3-15 cm diameter, 0.5-7 cm thickness).

Losillasaurus.etymology: Named after Losilla, the village near the fossil locality in Valencia, Spain; meaning "Losilla lizard"
Losillasaurus.description: Losillasaurus is a genus of turiasaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic and possibly Early Cretaceous (Kimmeridgian-?Berriasian) of southeastern Spain. The type species, Losillasaurus giganteus, was discovered in the Villar del Arzobispo Formation in Valencia, and formally described by Casanovas, Santafé, and Sanz in 2001. The holotype material is from a subadult and includes part of a skull; complete cervical, dorsal, sacral, and caudal vertebrae as well as several fragments; skeletal elements from the limbs including a humerus, ulna, radius, and metacarpal; sternal plates; and from the pelvis: the ilium, ischium, and pubis. The genus is characterized by the dimension and shape of the neural spine of the proximal caudal vertebrae. The humerus is 143 centimeters (56 in) long, which despite being from a subadult specimen is within 20% of the size of Paralititan. The size estimation proposed by Francisco Gascó in his master thesis is 15-18 m (49-59 ft) in length and 12-15 t (13-17 short tons) in body mass.
diagnostic_features: Neural spines of proximal caudal vertebrae arched dorsocaudally in lateral view (cutlass shaped)
Ratio of craniocaudal dimension of neural spine base to total height approximately 0.50
Middle and caudal dorsal vertebral centra opisthocoelous
Ventral median keels on cervical centra reduced or absent
Pleurocoels present in dorsal vertebral centra

species.name: Losillasaurus giganteus
species.etymology: From Latin 'giganteus' meaning 'gigantic', referring to the large size of this sauropod, whose humerus alone measures 143 centimeters.

type_specimen.material: Procoelous proximal caudal vertebral centrum; length/height ratio >0.5 < 0.6; neural spine transversely compressed and cutlass shaped; caudal ribs wing shaped (specimen Lo-5)

dispute.summary: The affinities of Lourinhanosaurus are highly uncertain. It has variously been referred to Allosauroidea (as a sinraptorid/metriacanthosaurid), to Megalosauroidea, and to Coelurosauria. Carrano et al. (2012) recovered it weakly allied with Coelurosauria, while Hartman et al. (2019) and Jones et al. (2026) place it near the base of Avetheropoda without resolving whether it is an allosauroid or a coelurosaur. It is placed conservatively at Avetheropoda incertae sedis, the least-inclusive clade common to the competing hypotheses.

history.note: Moved from Coelurosauria to Avetheropoda incertae sedis; allosauroid, megalosauroid, and coelurosaur hypotheses unresolved (Carrano et al., 2012; Hartman et al., 2019).

Lourinhanosaurus.etymology: Named for Lourinhã, the town in Portugal near where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'Lourinhã lizard'. The species name honors Portuguese paleontologist Miguel Telles Antunes.
Lourinhanosaurus.description: Lourinhanosaurus was a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic Period (Kimmeridgian/Tithonian) in Portugal. It is one of many large predators discovered at the Lourinhã Formation and probably competed with coeval Torvosaurus gurneyi, Allosaurus europaeus, and Ceratosaurus.

Neural spines of anterior caudal vertebrae with well-developed spike-like anterior process
Pubic blade perforated by large vertical ellipsoidal foramen
Lesser trochanter well separated from main body of femur in lateral view

Lourinhasaurus.etymology: Named after Lourinhã, the municipality in Portugal associated with the fossil-bearing formation, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'lizard from Lourinhã'
Lourinhasaurus.description: Lourinhasaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur dating from Late Jurassic strata of Estremadura, Portugal. The genus is monotypic, containing one species, Lourinhasaurus alenquerensis. The type specimen for this species was discovered near the town of Alenquer, near an abandoned mill. The specimen is housed at the Geological Museum of Lisbon. The research history of Lourinhasaurus is not without controversies, with referred specimens later being interpreted as not belonging to the genus (such as the type specimen of Supersaurus (=Dinheirosaurus) lourinhanensis). Lourinhasaurus means "lizard from Lourinhã" literally translated, despite the fact that the type specimen wasn't found in the Lourinhã municipality.
diagnostic_features: Cranial-to-middle dorsal vertebrae with a transversely concave ventral face bounded by longitudinal smooth crests.
Sagittal keel on the dorsal margin of the sacral neural spines.
Sacral neural spines, when vertical, becoming significantly higher caudally, with the dorsal margin bearing a marked cranial slope.
Prespinal process with a sagittal (prespinal) lamina in the dorsal sector of the sacral spine, subdividing a smooth prespinal fossa.
Circular and deep spinoprezygapophyseal fossa on the proximal caudal vertebrae (also shared by Jobaria).

Dorsal surface of the most proximal caudal spine sloping cranially and transitioning continuously to the cranial face of the spine, the caudal edge forming a transverse hook-like process in lateral view.
Circular process on the distal surface of carpal II.
Longitudinal crest on the ventral margin of the ilium's postacetabular process near the ischiatic peduncle.
Caudally oriented postacetabular process, with the chord through the ischiatic and pubic articulations passing through the ventral margin of the postacetabular process.
Axis of the pubic peduncle and the ischiatic articulation parallel.
Marked crest and groove bordering the lateral margin of the acetabulum on the ischium.
Tibia and fibula of equal length (implying a more distal position of the fibula relative to the tibia for reception of the astragalus).
Marked deflection of the entire femoral shaft without a lateral bulge.

Luanchuanraptor.etymology: Named after Luanchuan, Henan Province, China combined with Latin raptor (thief/seizer); meaning "Luanchuan thief"
Luanchuanraptor.description: Luanchuanraptor is a genus of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of China. The genus is based on a partial skeleton from the Qiupa Formation in Luanchuan, Henan. They were medium-sized dromaeosaurids, the first Asian dromaeosaurid taxa described from outside the Gobi Desert or northeastern China.

Lucianovenator.etymology: Named for Don Luciano Leyes, who first reported the fossil remains, combined with Latin 'venator' meaning 'hunter'.
Lucianovenator.description: Lucianovenator is an extinct genus of coelophysid theropod dinosaur which lived in Argentina during the Triassic. The genus name Lucianovenator translates to "Luciano's hunter", in reference to Don Luciano Leyes, who first reported the remains. The species name bonoi refers to Tulio del Bono, a local scientific authority who collaborated on the describers' research. It is one of the few neotheropods known from South America.

Length of anterior cervical ribs equivalent to five cervical centra
Cervical vertebrae extremely elongated (>3× longer than posterior articular surface height)
Deeply concave posterior articular face of cervical centra

Lurdusaurus.etymology: From Latin 'lurdus' meaning 'heavy' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'heavy lizard', in reference to its massive proportions. The species name 'arenatus' is Latin for 'sandy', as it was found in a desert.
Lurdusaurus.description: Lurdusaurus is a genus of massive and unusually shaped iguanodont dinosaur from the Elrhaz Formation in Niger. It contains one species, L. arenatus. The formation dates to the Early Cretaceous, roughly 112 million years ago.
diagnostic_features: Massively proportioned iguanodontid with unusually robust skeletal construction throughout

Forelimbs and hindlimbs short relative to dorsal centrum length (60-70% shorter than in European species)

history.note: Placed at Carcharodontosauria incertae sedis; membership in Carcharodontosauridae is unresolved.

It includes one species, Lusovenator santosi.

Lythronax.etymology: From Greek 'lythron' (λύθρον) meaning 'gore' and 'anax' (ἄναξ) meaning 'king', hence 'gore king'. The species name is from Greek 'argestes' (ἀργεστής), Homer's name for the wind from the southwest, referring to where the specimen was found in North America.
Lythronax.description: Lythronax is a genus of tyrannosaurid dinosaur that lived in North America around 81.9-81.5 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period. The only known specimen was discovered in Utah in the Wahweap Formation of the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument in 2009, and it consists of a partial skull and skeleton. In 2013, it became the basis of the new genus and species Lythronax argestes; the generic name Lythronax means "gore king", and the specific name argestes originates from the Greek poet Homer's name for the wind from the southwest, in reference to the specimen's geographic provenance in North America.

type_specimen.notes: The holotype is one adult individual, but no single catalog number was ever assigned to it: its material was accessioned across five lots, MNS 2000/132, 2001/122, 2002/95, 2003/69 and 2004/54. The describing paper states that only remains providing relevant anatomical or taxonomic information were described, so most elements carry no number at all. The ids listed here are those the paper ties explicitly to a holotype element and are therefore a subset, not the whole animal; the teeth, sacral fragments, chevrons and rib fragments are largely unnumbered. The lot numbers are deliberately not listed as ids, because lot MNS 2001/122 also holds the Soriatitan golmayensis holotype from the same quarry.

Magyarosaurus.etymology: From Hungarian 'Magyar' meaning 'Hungarian' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; named for Hungary, the country that controlled the Transylvanian region where it was found at the time of discovery.
Magyarosaurus.description: Magyarosaurus is a genus of dwarf sauropod dinosaur from late Cretaceous Period (early to late Maastrichtian) in today's Transylvania. It is one of the smallest-known adult sauropods, measuring less than 3 m (9.8 ft) long and weighing less than 1,000 kg (2,200 lb). The type and only species is Magyarosaurus dacus. It has been found to be a close relative of Rapetosaurus in the family Saltasauridae in the sauropod clade Titanosauria in a 2005 study.

dispute.summary: Mahakala was originally described as the basalmost dromaeosaurid (Turner et al., 2007) and is still recovered in that position by some analyses. Cau et al. (2017) instead recovered it within Halszkaraptorinae, the placement adopted here and followed by Jones et al. (2026), though Jasinski et al. (2020) recovered it outside that clade. It is placed in Halszkaraptorinae following the prevailing recent view.

history.note: Placed in Halszkaraptorinae following Cau et al. (2017) and Jones et al. (2026); the basalmost-dromaeosaurid reading is noted.

Mahakala.etymology: Named after Mahakala, a deity common to Hinduism and Buddhism.
Mahakala.description: Mahakala is a genus of halszkaraptorine theropod dinosaur from the Campanian-age (about 80 million years ago) Upper Cretaceous Djadokhta Formation of Ömnögovi, Mongolia. It is based on a partial skeleton found in the Gobi Desert. Mahakala was a small dromaeosaurid, and its skeleton shows features that are also found in early troodontids and avialans. Despite its late appearance, it is among the most basal dromaeosaurids. Its small size, and the small size of other basal deinonychosaurians, suggests that small size appeared before flight capability in birds.

dispute.summary: The composition of Mamenchisaurus is unsettled and the genus is poorly defined. Many species and fragmentary specimens have been referred to it over the years, several of them fragmentary and undiagnostic, and repeated analyses have failed to recover the genus as monophyletic (Moore and colleagues, 2020, 2023; Wang and colleagues, 2019). The type species, M. constructus, rests on fragmentary material that yields little character information: Moore and colleagues (2023) recovered no autapomorphies for it, found its phylogenetic position unstable, and regarded the forked mid-caudal chevrons long cited as diagnostic of the genus as possibly an artifact of reconstruction. It frequently falls outside the clade containing the other referred species (Dai and colleagues, 2025). Moore and colleagues (2023) placed M. sinocanadorum outside that clade as well, closest to Xinjiangtitan, but withheld taxonomic action pending a re-evaluation of the type species, and Dai and colleagues (2025) retained the generic name for their new species expressly to avoid further nomenclatural confusion. The referred species also span an implausible interval: Wang and colleagues (2019) dated the upper Suining Formation, the horizon of M. anyuensis, to 114.4 million years, some 30 million years younger than the Late Jurassic species, and called for a total re-evaluation of the genus. Moore and colleagues (2020) likewise failed to recover ZDM 0126 as sister to the M. hochuanensis holotype, casting doubt on that referral.

history.note: Retained at Mamenchisauridae with the referred species held as valid. Recent analyses recover the genus as non-monophyletic, but no author has yet proposed a replacement arrangement, so the existing combinations stand pending revision of the type species.

Mamenchisaurus.etymology: Named after Mamenchi (a transliteration of the Chinese place name for a ferry crossing, Maming Creek), where the first fossils were found near Yibin, Sichuan, China, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Mamenchi lizard'
Mamenchisaurus.description: Mamenchisaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaurs known for their remarkably long necks, which made up nearly half the total body length. Numerous species have been assigned to the genus; however, the validity of these assignments has been questioned. Fossils have been found in the Sichuan Basin and Yunnan Province in China. Several species from the Upper Shaximiao Formation, whose geologic age is uncertain, have been described. However, evidence suggests this formation to be no earlier than the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic. M. sinocanadorum dates to the Oxfordian stage (161.2 to 158.7 mya), and M. anyuensis to the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous (around 114.4 mya). Most species were medium-large to large sauropods, measuring roughly 15 to 26 meters (49 to 85 ft) in length-possibly up to 35 meters (115 ft), based on two undescribed vertebrae.

Manidens.etymology: From Latin 'manus' (hand) and 'dens' (tooth), referring to the hand-shaped form of the posterior lower teeth.
Manidens.description: Manidens is an extinct genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur from the Early Jurassic of Patagonia. It is a sister taxon of the closely related Pegomastax from South Africa. Fossils have been found in the Cañadón Asfalto Formation in Chubut Province, Argentina, considered to be originally dated to the Bajocian, latter were found to be from Toarcian beds.

dispute.summary: Manidens is a Middle Jurassic Patagonian heterodontosaurid recovered within Heterodontosaurinae as its basalmost member by the most comprehensive analyses (Sereno, 2012; Fonseca and others, 2024), the position followed by Jones (2026). Its describers (Pol and others, 2011) instead placed it just outside the Gondwanan clade, as its sister taxon.

history.note: Reparented from Heterodontosauridae to Heterodontosaurinae following Sereno (2012), Fonseca and others (2024), and Jones (2026); Pol and others (2011) place it as sister to the subfamily.

Manipulonyx.etymology: From Latin 'manipulare' (to manipulate, to handle) and Greek 'onyx' (claw), referring to the specialized forelimb interpreted as a tool for handling eggs.
Manipulonyx.description: Manipulonyx is an extinct genus of parvicursorine alvarezsaurid theropod from the Maastrichtian Nemegt Formation of the Khermeen Tsav locality, Govi-Altai Province, southern Mongolia. The single species, Manipulonyx reshetovi, is known from a fragmentary skeleton (PIN 3142/364) that preserves the most complete forelimb of any parvicursorine yet described, including the first documented complete set of proximal carpals (ulnare, intermedium, radiale) and a series of dermal carpal spikes (medial, lateral, and palmar) articulated with the carpometacarpus. Averianov, Lopatin and Atuchin (2025) interpret these spikes, together with the rudimentary third and fourth digits and the absence of a flexor tubercle on ungual II-2, as adaptations for gripping and piercing dinosaur eggs with the hypertrophied manual claw — a hypothesis supported by eggshell fragments associated with the holotype on its 1979 field label.

Olecranon process of ulna hypertrophied; manual digit 2 hypertrophied with very large and robust ungual phalanx bearing a large proximodorsal process on phalanx II-1.
Ventral canals of manual phalanx II-2 closed laterally; manual digits 3 and 4 greatly reduced but present.
Supraacetabular crest of ilium arcuate, not extending anteriorly beyond pubic peduncle; entocondylar tuber of femur present and directed posteriorly.
Popliteal fossa of femur open distally; metatarsal 4 with lateral flexor ridge.

Mantellisaurus.etymology: Named for Gideon Mantell, the English geologist and paleontologist who first described Iguanodon, combined with Greek '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Mantellisaurus.description: Mantellisaurus is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur that lived in the Barremian and early Aptian ages of the Early Cretaceous Period of Europe. Its remains are known from Belgium (Bernissart), England, Spain and Germany. The type and only species is M. atherfieldensis. Formerly known as Iguanodon atherfieldensis, the new genus Mantellisaurus was erected for the species by Gregory Paul in 2007. According to Paul, Mantellisaurus was more lightly built than Iguanodon and more closely related to Ouranosaurus, making Iguanodon in its traditional sense paraphyletic. It is known from many complete and almost complete skeletons. The genus name honors Gideon Mantell, the discoverer of Iguanodon.

dispute.summary: Mantellisaurus atherfieldensis is grouped with Iguanodon (and, in some analyses, Barilium and Comptonatus) in a monophyletic Iguanodontidae by Lockwood and others (2024), but this family is traditionally paraphyletic and Iguanodontidae is not consistently recovered.

history.note: Placed at Hadrosauriformes, the least-inclusive uncontested node; the monophyletic Iguanodontidae of Lockwood and others (2024) reflected, not adopted.

Mapusaurus.etymology: From Mapudungun 'mapu' (earth or land) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'earth lizard'
Mapusaurus.description: Mapusaurus is a genus of giant carcharodontosaurid carnosaurian dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Cenomanian-Turonian ages of the Late Cretaceous. It is known from a bonebed of between seven and nine specimens, excavated from the strata of the Huincul Formation between 1997 and 2001 as part of the Argentinian-Canadian Dinosaur Project. In 2006, Rodolfo Coria and Philip J. Currie scientifically described Mapusaurus. Only one species of Mapusaurus, M. roseae, has been described, named after the rose-colored rocks in which it was discovered and sponsor Rose Letwin.

Maraapunisaurus.etymology: From Ute 'maraapuni' meaning 'it is very large' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', giving the meaning 'very large lizard', named for the enormous estimated size of the specimen.
Maraapunisaurus.description: Maraapunisaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of western North America. It contains one species, Maraapunisaurus fragillimus, which was originally named Amphicoelias fragillimus. It has sometimes been estimated to be the largest dinosaur specimen ever discovered. Based on surviving descriptions of a single fossil bone, scientists have produced numerous size estimates over the years; the largest estimate M. fragillimus to have been the longest known animal at 58 meters (190 ft) in length with a mass of 150 tonnes (150 long tons; 170 short tons). However, because the only fossil remains were lost at some point after being studied and described in the 1870s, evidence survived only in contemporary drawings and field notes.

Martharaptor.etymology: Named in honor of Martha C. Hayden, the paleontologist assistant who helped discover the Hayden-Corbett site in the Cedar Mountain Formation of Utah where the specimen was found, combined with Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief'.
Martharaptor.description: Martharaptor is a genus of therizinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of the Cedar Mountain Formation in Utah. They can be distinguished from other therizinosaurs by means of several features of the skeleton (particularly the hands and feet) which were intermediate between early therizinosaurs such as Falcarius and Beipiaosaurus, and more "advanced" members of the group like therizinosaurids. The deep and homogeneous hand claws clearly differ from the case in early therizinosauroids, but the foot has not yet acquired the robust morphology of therizinosaurids.

dispute.summary: Martharaptor is a poorly known basal therizinosaur whose precise position is unresolved. Its describers (Senter et al., 2012) recovered it near the base of Therizinosauroidea, but with weak support, and Hartman et al. (2019) found it to occupy several equally parsimonious positions as a therizinosaur less derived than Alxasaurus. It is therefore placed conservatively within Therizinosauria rather than at a finer node.

Masiakasaurus.etymology: From Malagasy 'masiaka' meaning 'vicious' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'vicious lizard'.
Masiakasaurus.description: Masiakasaurus is a genus of small predatory theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of Madagascar. In Malagasy, masiaka means "vicious"; thus, the genus name means "vicious lizard". The type species, Masiakasaurus knopfleri, was named after the musician Mark Knopfler, whose music inspired the expedition crew. It was named in 2001 by Scott D. Sampson, Matthew Carrano, and Catherine A. Forster. Unlike most theropods, the front teeth of Masiakasaurus projected forwards instead of straight down. This unique dentition suggests that they had a specialized diet, perhaps including fish and other small prey. Other bones of the skeleton indicate that Masiakasaurus were bipedal, with much shorter forelimbs than hindlimbs. It was a small theropod, reaching 1.8-2.1 m (5.9-6.9 ft) long and weighing 20 kg (44 lb). Masiakasaurus lived from 72.1 to 66 million years ago, along with animals such as Majungasaurus, Rapetosaurus, and Rahonavis. Masiakasaurus was a member of the group Noasauridae, small predatory ceratosaurs found primarily in South America.

Massospondylus.etymology: From Greek 'massos' meaning 'longer' and 'spondylos' meaning 'vertebra', referring to what Richard Owen identified as elongated tail vertebrae.
Massospondylus.description: Massospondylus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic of southern Africa. It was described by Richard Owen in 1854 from remains discovered in South Africa, and is thus one of the first dinosaurs to have been named. The name Massospondylus means 'longer vertebra', alluding to what Owen identified as tail vertebrae; these vertebrae are now known to be from the neck. Although the original fossils were destroyed in London during The Blitz, a plethora of specimens have since been assigned to the genus, making it one of the best-known sauropodomorphs from the Early Jurassic. The genus lived during the Hettangian, Sinemurian, and Pliensbachian ages, which lasted from ca. 201 to 184 million years ago. Most fossils come from the upper Elliot and Clarens formations of South Africa and Lesotho, but the genus is also found in the Forest Sandstone and the Mpandi Formation of Zimbabwe. Material from the US, India, and Argentina was previously assigned to the genus, but the US and Argentinian specimens are now assigned to their own genera (Sarahsaurus and Adeopapposaurus). Because of their great abundance, Massospondylus fossils have been used to date rocks, and a biozone, the Massospondylus Range Zone, is named after the genus.

Matheronodon.etymology: Named after French paleontologist Philippe Matheron, combined with Greek 'odon' (tooth); meaning 'Matheron's tooth'.
Matheronodon.description: Matheronodon is a genus of rhabdodontid ornithopod dinosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of the Grès à Reptiles Formation in France. The genus contains a single species, M. provincialis, which is known from a single maxilla and associated teeth. It was named by Pascal Godefroit and colleagues in 2017. The teeth of Matheronodon are large but few in number. The teeth are also in an unusual arrangement, emerging alternatingly from one of a pair of fused tooth sockets in its mouth. In life, the teeth would have functioned like a pair of scissors, allowing Matheronodon to feed on the tough leaves of monocot plants.

Mei.description: Mei is a genus of duck-sized troodontid dinosaur first unearthed by paleontologists from the Yixian Formation in Liaoning, China in 2004. Mei lived during the Early Cretaceous period.

Melanorosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'melas' meaning 'black', 'oros' meaning 'mountain', and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'Black Mountain Lizard', named for the Black Mountains (Thaba Nyama) near the South African discovery site.
Melanorosaurus.description: Melanorosaurus is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur that lived during the Late Triassic period. An omnivore from South Africa, it had a large body and sturdy limbs, suggesting it moved quadrupedally. Its limb bones were massive and heavy like the limb bones of true sauropods.

dispute.summary: Melanorosaurus readi is a derived sauropodiform hovering on the boundary of Sauropoda; depending on the Sauropoda definition it is the immediate non-sauropodan sister of the clade or just inside it.

history.note: Placed at Sauropodiformes incertae sedis; the precise Sauropoda boundary remains unresolved.

diagnostic_features: Posterior margin of the ulna with a pronounced sigmoidal outline.
Sigmoidal dorsal margin of the iliac pubic peduncle.
Ratio of ilium height at the level of the ischiac peduncle to total ilium length greater than 0.67.
Ilium with a straight posterior margin continuous with the ischial peduncle, steeply angled at 65° to the horizontal.
Proximal caudal vertebrae with dorsoventrally elongate, mediolaterally narrow, heart-shaped centra at least 1.42 times taller than wide.
Proximal caudal centra with a deeply incised ventral midline groove.
Proximal caudal centra with foramina on their lateral surfaces.

Mendozasaurus.etymology: Named for Mendoza Province in Argentina where it was discovered, combined with Greek '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Mendozasaurus.description: Mendozasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur. It was a member of Titanosauria, which were massive sauropods that were common on the southern landmasses during the Cretaceous. It is represented by several partial skeletons from a single locality within the Coniacian (lower Upper Cretaceous) Sierra Barrosa Formation in the south of Mendoza Province, northern Neuquén Basin, Argentina.

Postzygapostspinal laminae in anterior dorsal vertebrae parallel to postzygapophyseal facet planes
Dorsoventrally extended interzygapophyseal cavity in anterior caudal vertebrae limited by spinopostzygapophyseal and spinoprezygapophysial laminae
Middle caudal vertebrae slightly procoelous with reduced posterior condyles displaced dorsally
Laminar mid-posterior caudal neural spines with horizontal straight dorsal border and anterodorsal right angle
Large subconic-spherical osteoderms lacking cingulum

Menefeeceratops.etymology: Named after the Menefee Formation where it was found, combined with Greek 'keras' (horn) and 'ops' (face); meaning 'Menefee Formation horned face'.
Menefeeceratops.description: Menefeeceratops is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from the Menefee Formation in New Mexico, United States. It is potentially the oldest known member of the ceratopsids, as well as the centrosaurine subfamily, related to animals including Yehuecauhceratops and Crittendenceratops. The type and only species is Menefeeceratops sealeyi, known from a partial, non-articulated skeleton.

Episquamosal locus 1 with three secondary undulations
Two subequal embayments on posterior squamosal margin with dorsal distinctly larger

Shallow groove on medial squamosal surface along ventrolateral and ventroposterior margins
Elongate postorbital horns distally curving anteriorly
Dentary with two elongated ridges on lateral surface forming distinct anterior triangular fossa

Menucocelsior.description: Menucocelsior is a genus of medium-sized titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Allen Formation of Argentina. The type and only species is Menucocelsior arriagadai.

First caudal with well-developed anteroventral ridge extending along transverse process
Humerus gracile, lacking strongly expanded ends, deltopectoral crest not extending beyond mid-shaft
Fibula relatively short and stout but nearly straight, with single prominent lateral tuberosity
Distal fibular end shows prominent proximodistally extended bony flange diverging strongly from shaft

Meraxes.description: Meraxes is a genus of large carcharodontosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Huincul Formation of Patagonia, Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Meraxes gigas.

Only Late Cretaceous carcharodontosaurid preserving near-complete forelimbs (47% femur length)
Well-developed hyposphen-hypantrum in anterior caudal vertebrae unique among carcharodontosaurids
Unique protuberances and rugosity patterns on dermal cranial bones
Tongue-like posterior projection of parietals over supraoccipital

Mercuriceratops.etymology: From Latin 'Mercurius' (the Roman messenger god, whose winged helmet is evoked by the rod-and-flange shape of the squamosal) and Greek 'keras' (horn) and 'ops' (face); meaning 'Mercury's horned face'.
Mercuriceratops.description: Mercuriceratops is an extinct genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsid from the late Campanian of northern Laramidia, with the holotype recovered from the upper Judith River Formation of Fergus County, Montana, and a paratype squamosal from the lower Dinosaur Park Formation of Dinosaur Provincial Park, Alberta. The single species, Mercuriceratops gemini, is diagnosed by a uniquely rod-shaped posterior ramus of the squamosal — constricted into a mediolaterally compressed bar instead of the tapering triangle typical of chasmosaurines — with a hatchet-shaped lateral margin bearing four tab-shaped episquamosals. The "twin" species name refers to the two right squamosals from two formations on either side of the Canada-Montana border.
diagnostic_features: Squamosal posterior ramus constricted into a rod-shaped (mediolaterally compressed, subrectangular cross-section) bar rather than a tapering obtuse or broadly rounded triangle in dorsal view.
Lateral margin of the squamosal hatchet-shaped in dorsal view, with the posterolateral bar offset from the anterolateral flange by a deep embayment (notch).
Anterolateral flange bears four large, tab-shaped, well-fused episquamosals on its lateral margin.
Elongate episquamosals extending along the lateral margin of the posteriorly projecting rod-shaped squamosal bar.
Deeply incised longitudinal grooves on the medioventral surface of the posterior squamosal shaft forming a robust, tightly interdigitating sutural contact for the parietal.

species.name: Mercuriceratops gemini
species.etymology: From Latin 'gemini' (twins), referring to the paired right squamosals from Montana and Alberta and to the mythological twins Castor and Pollux who became the Gemini constellation.

type_specimen.material: Almost complete right squamosal (maximum preserved length 793 mm), preserving the anterior postorbital contact, medial supraorbital fenestra margin, parietal contact surface, and most of the lateral margin.

Meroktenos.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'meros' meaning 'thigh' and 'ktēnos' meaning 'beast'.
Meroktenos.description: Meroktenos is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur that lived during the Late Triassic period of what is now Lesotho.

history.note: Placed at Sauropodiformes incertae sedis; the Lessemsauridae alternative and the Sauropoda boundary are recorded.

Femoral shaft straight in anterior and lateral views
Femoral shaft significantly wider lateromedially than anteroposteriorly (eccentricity 1.58, vs <1.41 in others)
Oblique fourth trochanter on femur

Mesetasaurus.etymology: 'Meseta', after the name of the locality (Meseta de Artigas), plus 'saurus', Greek for reptile.
Mesetasaurus.description: Mesetasaurus is a genus of aeolosaurin titanosaurian sauropod dinosaurs known from the Guichón Formation (Late Cretaceous, potentially Coniacian to Maastrichtian) of Paysandú Department, Uruguay. The genus contains a single species, the type species Mesetasaurus protector, known from two well-preserved caudal vertebrae. It is the second titanosaurian taxon known from its unit, after the saltasauroid Udelartitan.
diagnostic_features: Anterior caudal centra strongly procoelous, with ventral margins ranging from flat to slightly transversely concave.
Neural arch anteriorly displaced within the anterior caudal vertebrae.

Anterior-most caudal centrum: anterior face slightly inclined (about 10 degrees); ovoid blind fossa below the anteroposterior axis, close to the condyle; wide ventral surface with paired neurovascular foramina.
Anterior-most caudal centrum condyle strongly convex and slightly eccentric; prezygapophyses long, anterodorsally projected at about 30 degrees.
Posterior anterior caudal centrum: anterior face strongly anteriorly inclined (about 25 degrees); centrum slightly dorsoventrally depressed.
Posterior anterior caudal centrum: narrow ventral face bounded by ventrolateral ridges; condyle very strongly convex and strongly eccentric; prezygapophyses sub-horizontal (about 10 degrees).

Metriacanthosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'metrios' (moderate), 'akantha' (spine or thorn), and 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'moderately-spined lizard'.
Metriacanthosaurus.description: Metriacanthosaurus is a genus of metriacanthosaurid dinosaur from the Oxford Clay Formation of England, dating to the Late Jurassic period, about 160 million years ago (lower Oxfordian). It is the only metriacanthosaurid currently named from outside of Asia.

Mexidracon.description: Mexidracon is an extinct genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaurs from the late Cretaceous Cerro del Pueblo Formation of Coahuila, Mexico. The genus contains a single species, M. longimanus, known from a partial skeleton. Mexidracon is the second ornithomimosaur to be named from this formation, following the deinocheirid Paraxenisaurus in 2020.

Microceratus.description: Microceratus is a genus of small ceratopsian dinosaur that lived in the Cretaceous period of Mongolia. It walked on two legs, had short front arms, a characteristic ceratopsian frill and beak-like mouth, and was around 60 cm (2.0 ft) long. It was one of the most primitive ceratopsians, or horned dinosaurs, along with Psittacosaurus, which was also discovered in Mongolia.

dispute.summary: Microceratus gobiensis is a replacement name for the preoccupied Microceratops; most referred material has been reassigned to Graciliceratops, leaving a poorly diagnosable basal neoceratopsian widely treated as a nomen dubium.

Lower jaw: anterior end twisted inwards in inferior view (vs. straight in Protoceratops andrewsi)

Microcoelus.etymology: From Greek 'mikros' (small) and 'koilos' (hollow); meaning 'small hollow', a reference to the shallow lateral pit on the holotype dorsal vertebra.
Microcoelus.description: Microcoelus is a dubious genus of small titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Santonian stage) Bajo de la Carpa Formation, Argentina. It is known from only a single dorsal vertebra, although a left humerus was formerly referred to this taxon, but it is now considered to belong to Neuquensaurus. The type (and only known) species is M. patagonicus, described by British paleontologist Richard Lydekker in 1893.
diagnostic_features: Anterior dorsal vertebrae opisthocoeolous with well-marked rib-facets on fore part of arch lamina
Lateral pits (shallow, somewhat circular depressions) on dorsal vertebrae, apparently without communication with interior of bone
Caudal vertebrae amphicoelous (or platycoeolous), differing from procoeolous caudals of Titanosaurus and Argyrosaurus
Humerus short and broadly expanded, with large swollen deltoid crest extending lower on shaft than in Titanosaurus australis or Argyrosaurus
Zygapophyses of caudal vertebrae very slightly developed and scarcely articulated with one another

The supposed preoccupier "Microsaurus" (cited from Hatcher 1900; Lull 1910) was itself only a misspelling of Microcoelus, so the replacement was unnecessary. Listed by Olshevsky (1991).

species.etymology: From Patagonia, the region of Argentina where the type material was collected.

Micropachycephalosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'mikros' (small), 'pachys' (thick), 'kephale' (head), and 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'small thick-headed lizard'.
Micropachycephalosaurus.description: Micropachycephalosaurus is an extinct genus of basal marginocephalian dinosaur, containing only the type species, Micropachycephalosaurus hongtuyanensis. It lived in China during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) and was found in the Jiangjunding Formation. It has the longest name of any dinosaur, with 23 letters in the genus name alone, while the full binomial contains 37 letters.

dispute.summary: Despite its name, Micropachycephalosaurus hongtuyanensis is not confidently a pachycephalosaur. The dedicated redescription (Butler and Zhao, 2009) found no unambiguous synapomorphies and treated it as Cerapoda incertae sedis; some analyses recover it as a basal ceratopsian (Butler and others, 2011; Jones, 2026) while Fonseca and others (2024) recover it as a pachycephalosaur.

history.note: Placed at Cerapoda incertae sedis following the dedicated redescription (Butler and Zhao, 2009), which declines assignment to either Ceratopsia or Pachycephalosauria; conflicting ceratopsian and pachycephalosaurian results reflected, not adopted.

Microraptor.etymology: From Greek 'mikros' (small) and Latin 'raptor' (one who seizes); meaning 'small thief' or 'small raptor'
Microraptor.description: Microraptor is a genus of small, four-winged dromaeosaurid dinosaurs. Numerous well-preserved fossil specimens have been recovered from Liaoning, China. They date from the early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation (Aptian stage), 125 to 120 million years ago. Three species have been named (M. zhaoianus, M. gui, and M. hanqingi), though further study has suggested that all of them represent variation in a single species, which is properly called M. zhaoianus. Cryptovolans, initially described as another four-winged dinosaur, is usually considered to be a synonym of Microraptor.

Middle caudal vertebrae about 3-4 times as long as anterior dorsal vertebrae

Strongly recurved and slender pedal unguals with prominent flexor tubercle

notable_specimens.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology
notable_specimens.significance: Preserves the remains of an enantiornithine bird within its rib cage, direct evidence that Microraptor preyed on birds and likely foraged in the trees.

notable_specimens.significance: Preserves fish scales in its abdominal cavity, evidence that Microraptor also hunted fish. Combined with anterodorsally inclined front teeth often associated with piscivory, it indicates Microraptor was an opportunistic feeder in both arboreal and aquatic habitats.

Preserves a complete lizard, the new genus Indrasaurus, swallowed head-first in its stomach as in modern carnivorous birds and lizards. The lizard bones lack pitting and scarring, showing the Microraptor died shortly after eating, before significant digestion.

Microvenator.etymology: From Greek 'mikros' meaning 'small' and Latin 'venator' meaning 'hunter'; translates as 'small hunter', named for its small size.
Microvenator.description: Microvenator is a genus of oviraptorosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Cloverly Formation in what is now south central Montana. The holotype fossil is an incomplete skeleton, most likely a juvenile with a length of 1.3 m (4.3 ft), and consequently, the adult size remains uncertain. Microvenator is primitive and may be the "sister taxon to all other oviraptorosaurs."

Mierasaurus.etymology: Named for Bernardo de Miera y Pacheco, an eighteenth-century Spanish cartographer and explorer of the American Southwest, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Mierasaurus.description: Mierasaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Utah, United States. The taxon was first described and named in 2017 by Rafael Royo-Torres and colleagues, from a mostly complete skeleton including a disarticulated partial skull and mandible, teeth, multiple vertebrae from along the length of the body, both scapulae, radius and ulna bones, a left manus, a complete pelvis, both femora and the entire left hindlimb. Additionally, they referred a lower jaw and femur from juvenile individuals, which were found nearby, to the genus. Collectively, Mierasaurus is among the most completely known North American sauropods. The genus name honors Bernardo de Miera y Pacheco, the first European scientist to enter what is now Utah. The type species for Mierasaurus is Mierasaurus bobyoungi, named after Robert Glen Young, a paleontologist who researched the Early Cretaceous of Utah.
diagnostic_features: Otosphenoidal ridge extends from anterior surface of paroccipital process near its ventral margin and restricted to medialmost part of latter process
Occipital condyle has pair of rounded ridges extending dorsoventrally on either lateral face of condylar articular surface
Atlantal intercentrum bears pair of depressions in medial surface facing posteromedially, each receiving anterolateral margin of odontoid process
Cervical ribs bear ridge or bulge on lateral surface of tuberculum immediately posterior to base of anterior process
Lateral depression on distal ramus of haemal arches
Metacarpal I longer than metacarpal IV
Very short ischium compared to pubis (ischium:pubis length ratio 0.75)
Fourth trochanter placed in proximal part of femur
Femur with subequal distal condyles
Pedal unguals 2 and 3 compressed dorsoventrally

Minmi.etymology: Named for Minmi Crossing, a location in Queensland, Australia near where it was found; the Wikipedia article retrieved is about a Japanese musician, not the dinosaur.
Minmi.description: Minmi is a genus of small herbivorous ankylosaurian dinosaur that lived during the early Cretaceous Period of Australia, about 120 to 112 million years ago.

Arbour and Currie (2015) regarded Minmi paravertebra as a nomen dubium, while others uphold it; phylogenetic analyses recover it as an unstable wildcard, even outside Eurypoda in the preferred tree of Raven et al. (2023). It is retained at Ankylosauria incertae sedis.

Minotaurasaurus.etymology: Named after the Minotaur of Greek mythology (the bull of Minos) combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Minos's bull reptile'.
Minotaurasaurus.description: Minotaurasaurus is a monospecific genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous (late Campanian stage, ~75-71 Ma) in what is now the Djadochta Formation. The type and only species, Minotaurasaurus ramachandrani, is known from two skulls, a cervical vertebra and a cervical half ring. It was named and described in 2009 by Clifford Miles and Clark Miles. The holotype of Minotaurasaurus has been suspected to be illegally exported out of Mongolia. It has been suggested to be a synonym of Tarchia but more recent publications consider it as a distinct genus.

dispute.summary: The validity of Minotaurasaurus is contested. Arbour and Currie (2015) treated it as a junior synonym of Tarchia kielanae, whereas Penkalski and Tumanova (2016) and Wiersma and Irmis (2018) found it distinct. Retained as a valid ankylosaurine pending consensus.

history.note: Placed at Ankylosaurinae, kept valid although some analyses synonymize it with Tarchia.

Miragaia.etymology: Named for Miragaia, a parish in Porto, Portugal near where the fossil was discovered; the Wikipedia article retrieved is about the Portuguese locality itself.
Miragaia.description: Miragaia is a genus of long-necked stegosaurid dinosaur. Its fossils have been found in Upper Jurassic rocks in Portugal (Lourinhã Formation, Sobral Unit) and possibly also Wyoming and Utah, United States (Morrison Formation). Miragaia has the longest neck known for any stegosaurian, which included at least seventeen vertebrae. Some researchers consider this taxon to be a junior synonym of Dacentrurus.

dispute.summary: The validity of Miragaia is contested. It was erected as a long-necked dacentrurine (Mateus et al., 2009) and is widely treated as valid, but Sánchez-Fenollosa and Cobos (2025) synonymized it with Dacentrurus armatus. Either way it falls within Dacentrurinae.

history.note: Placed at Dacentrurinae, whether a valid dacentrurine or a junior synonym of Dacentrurus.

It lived during the Late Cretaceous (85-80 Ma) and two species have been named, M. suessi and M. vorosi, although the latter has been regarded as a junior synonym of the ceratopsian Ajkaceratops.

Mongolosaurus.etymology: Named after Mongolia, where the fossil was discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Mongolia lizard'
Mongolosaurus.description: Mongolosaurus is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur which lived during the Early Cretaceous of China.

dispute.summary: Placed at Somphospondyli incertae sedis. Known largely from teeth and fragmentary material, Mongolosaurus was originally described as a sauropod of undetermined family (Gilmore, 1933). Its redescription (Mannion, 2011) reaffirmed its validity and recovered it as a titanosaurian sauropod, whereas D'Emic (2012) regarded its affinities as equivocal, noting a few euhelopodid- like characters that would place it as a non-titanosaurian somphospondylan against the titanosaur features identified by Mannion. Somphospondyli is the least-inclusive clade both readings accept.

history.note: Retained in Titanosauria following Mannion (2011) and later work; a non-titanosaurian somphospondylan position and a nomen-dubium history are noted.

Broadened to Somphospondyli incertae sedis: the titanosaur reading (Mannion, 2011) and the euhelopodid, non-titanosaurian somphospondylan possibility raised by D'Emic (2012) straddle the Titanosauria boundary, so the conservative shared node is adopted.

diagnostic_features: Teeth tapering and obtusely pointed, slightly flattened on inner side with angularly rounded outer side, bearing low longitudinal carinae (ridges) on either side extending to apex
Tooth carinae faintly serrate (on at least one tooth), distinguishing them from the spatulate, non-serrate teeth of Diplodocus and Pleurocoelus
Pulp cavity continued to top of crown
Atlas intercentrum relatively wider and more deeply excavated on ventral surface than in Diplodocus, with neurapophyses more constricted above base

Third cervical strongly opisthocoelous, lacking true pleurocentral cavities, with capitular facet processes not produced below level of centrum (contrasting with Diplodocus, Helopus, Haplocanthosaurus)
Third cervical with incipient bifid spinous processes indicated by parallel ridges, differing from well-developed spines of Diplodocus, Helopus, and Camarasaurus

Mongolostegus.etymology: From 'Mongol' (Mongolia, where it was found) and Greek 'stegos' (roof); meaning 'Mongolian roof', referencing Mongolia and its classification as a stegosaur.
Mongolostegus.description: Mongolostegus is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian-Albian ages) Dzunbain Formation of Mongolia. The genus contains a single species, Mongolostegus exspectabilis, known from a fragmentary single specimen representing the first stegosaur named from Mongolia. It is one of the youngest known stegosaurs, along with Yanbeilong and an unnamed species from the Hekou Group of China. In contrast to these taxa, which are members of the late-diverging stegosaur subfamily Stegosaurinae, Mongolostegus may have affinities to more basal taxa such as the Huayangosauridae.

dispute.summary: Mongolostegus is known from very fragmentary material and behaves as a rogue taxon; Sánchez-Fenollosa and Cobos (2025) recover it as either a huayangosaurid or an early-diverging stegosaurid and exclude it from their primary analysis. It is placed at Stegosauria incertae sedis.

history.note: Placed at Stegosauria incertae sedis, fragmentary rogue taxon with unresolved family placement.

Mononykus.etymology: From Greek 'monos' (one) and 'onyx' (claw); meaning 'one claw', referring to its single functional forelimb claw.
Mononykus.description: Mononykus is a genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia, specifically the Nemegt Formation. Mononykus was a very small theropod, estimated around 1 to 1.2 meters (3.3 to 3.9 ft) in length with a weight of 3.5 kilograms (7.7 lb). As in Shuvuuia, Mononykus likely developed a shaggy feathering. It was lightly built with long, thin legs and highly reduced and specialized forelimbs that were likely used for foraging termite mounds or other insect colonies.

Montanoceratops.etymology: From 'Montana' (the U.S. state where it was first discovered) combined with Greek 'keras' (horn) and 'ops' (face); meaning 'Montana horned face'
Montanoceratops.description: Montanoceratops is an extinct genus of small ceratopsian dinosaur that lived approximately 70 million years ago during the latter part of the Cretaceous Period in what is now Montana and Alberta. Montanoceratops was a small sized, moderately-built, ground-dwelling, quadrupedal herbivore, that could grow up to an estimated 2.5 m (8.2 ft) in length and 170 kg (370 lb) in body mass.

Caudal neural spines very long, some more than five times the height of the corresponding centrum, versus two to two-and-a-half times in Leptoceratops
Splenial heavier and more elongate, with a more massive anterior end than in Leptoceratops

Sacrodorsal and first sacral rib facets closely spaced near ilium dorsal margin

It is an obscure tooth genus sometimes referred to the Early Cretaceous English wastebasket taxon Pelorosaurus.

Compressed tooth with elliptical cross-section; lateral faces rounded at external edge

Minimal dentin exposure; main vascular foramen visible

Transversely compressed, subtriangular distal articular condyle of the fourth metatarsal in distal view

Mosaiceratops.etymology: From Latin 'mosaicus' meaning 'mosaic' and Greek 'keras' meaning 'horn' and 'ops' meaning 'face', giving the meaning 'mosaic horned face', referring to the mix of features from basal neoceratopsians, psittacosaurids, and other basal ceratopsians.
Mosaiceratops.description: Mosaiceratops is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaur that lived in the upper Cretaceous Xiaguan Formation in what is now the Henan Province of China. It was described by Zheng, Jin, and Xu in 2015 as the type species Mosaiceratops azumai. Although phylogenetic analyses have found it to be the basalmost neoceratopsian, the authors noted that several features in the premaxilla and nasal bones are shared with Psittacosaurus, indicating that neoceratopsians evolved premaxillary teeth twice and that the latter is not as primitive as previously thought.

Elongate anterior process of jugal with sub-parallel dorsal and ventral edges
Two tubercles developed in the ventral border infraorbital ramus
Distal end of dorsal ilium edge dorsoposteriorly directed
Edentulous premaxilla
Inverted T-shape jugal in lateral view
T-shape postorbital with slender and elongate jugal and squamosal processes
Basal tubera separated by a deep middle notch

Murusraptor.description: Murusraptor is a genus of carnivorous megaraptoran theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Coniacian age) Sierra Barrosa Formation, part of the Neuquén Group of Patagonia, in Argentina, South America. Musango.etymology: Named for the Musango Concession Area and nearby Musango Island at the type locality on Lake Kariba; 'musango' is a chiShona word meaning 'living in the bush', alluding to the remoteness of the site.
Musango.description: Musango is an extinct genus of unaysaurid sauropodomorph dinosaurs from the Upper Triassic (Norian) Pebbly Arkose Formation of Zimbabwe. The genus contains a single species, Musango matusadonaensis, known from a partial skeleton. Musango represents the fifth dinosaur genus to be named from Zimbabwe.

dispute.summary: The unaysaurid affinity of Musango rests on a single analysis with weak support throughout. Barrett and others (2026) recover Musango as the sister taxon of the sympatric Musankwa within Unaysauridae in all most-parsimonious trees, but that pairing is supported by one highly homoplastic astragalar character at a Bremer support of 1, and the authors caution that the relationship is unlikely to prove robust as new material comes to light. The position of Unaysauridae itself alternates between a sister-group relationship with Plateosauridae and the earliest-diverging position within Massopoda.

history.note: Placed in Unaysauridae following Barrett and others (2026), the only analysis so far to include the taxon; the weak support for that position and for the Musango–Musankwa pairing is recorded here rather than by attaching the genus to a less resolved parent.

diagnostic_features: Middle caudal vertebrae bear exceptionally elongate transverse processes, more than twice the centrum's transverse width and exceeding centrum anteroposterior length
Distal ends of the middle caudal transverse processes are anteroposteriorly expanded and fan-shaped
The supraacetabular crest of the ilium bifurcates posteriorly into two ridges
The lateral margin of the pubic apron is greatly thickened and expanded anteroposteriorly relative to the medial margin, forming a prominent buttress
The medial surface of the fibula's proximal expansion bears a deep concavity with a prominent ventrally extending midline ridge
Two subparallel ridges extend from the posteromedial corner of the astragalus's ascending process

Mussaurus.etymology: From Latin 'mus' (mouse) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'mouse lizard', named for the small size of juvenile specimens originally known.
Mussaurus.description: Mussaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropodomorph dinosaur that lived in southern Argentina during the Sinemurian stage of the Early Jurassic. It receives its name from the small size of the skeletons of juvenile and infant individuals, which were once the only known specimens of the genus. However, since Mussaurus is now known from adult specimens, the name is something of a misnomer.
